--- Linked review document (full text, verbatim) ---
Feedback: Automotive Lakehouse Data Models - Value Chain Coverage Review
Repository: https://[v1-repo-url-redacted]
Date: May 23, 2026
Reviewer: AI (controlled by [REVIEWER])
---
Disclaimer: This feedback was generated by an AI system under the direction and control of [REVIEWER]. 
---
1. Executive Summary
The automotive data model repository provides an impressively comprehensive and well-structured Lakehouse data model for the automotive manufacturing industry. It is available in two scope variations - a Minimum Viable Model (MVM, 14 domains, 209 tables) and an Expanded Coverage Model (ECM, 19 domains, 548 tables). Both models are designed for deployment on the Databricks platform and include DDL schemas, metric views, sample data, DBML diagrams, and RDF ontologies.
This review evaluates whether the model adequately covers the main parts of the automotive value chain: R&D, Purchasing, Production, Logistics, Sales, Aftersales, and Field Services - and whether the relevant operational systems are considered.
---
2. Value Chain Coverage Assessment
2.1 R&D (Research & Development) - COVERED
Model Domains: Engineering, Vehicle (product_catalog)
Strengths:
The Engineering domain is well-represented with subdomains for design engineering, component validation, program governance, and supply planning.
Key R&D artifacts are modeled: engineering BOMs, design specifications, CAD model references, DVP (Design Verification Plan) plans, FMEA records, ECU specifications, powertrain specs, material specifications.
Engineering Change Management (ECO/ECN) is properly included.
Vehicle program management with milestone tracking (P0 through SOP) supports APQP phase-gate processes.
Prototype build and validation test records are present in the ECM.
Digital twin references are included (ECM only).
Operational Systems Referenced: Siemens Teamcenter, CATIA, ENOVIA, PTC Windchill - these are the correct PLM/CAD systems for the automotive industry.
Gaps / Suggestions:
No explicit domain for advanced R&D topics such as simulation data management (CFD, FEA result datasets), test bench data, or autonomous driving development data (sensor datasets, scenario libraries). While CFD/FEA/NVH are mentioned in descriptions, dedicated data products for simulation results would strengthen this area.
Patent and IP management data is absent - not critical for a Lakehouse model, but worth noting for completeness.
Requirements management (e.g., DOORS/Polarion/Jira integration) is mentioned implicitly through "linked requirements" but lacks a dedicated requirements traceability data product.
Verdict: Well covered. The model captures the essential R&D data structures. The ECM variant is particularly strong here.
---
2.2 Purchasing / Procurement - COVERED
Model Domains: Supply, Procurement (ECM only)
Strengths:
The Supply domain covers procurement operations, supplier management, quality assurance (PPAP), and inbound logistics even in the MVM.
The ECM adds a full Procurement domain with contract governance, procurement operations (PO, requisitions, approvals, sourcing events), spend analytics, and supplier management.
Supplier evaluation, scorecards, compliance, and development plans are well represented.
RFQ/RFQ response workflows are modeled.
Scheduling agreements and delivery schedules reflect JIT/JIS practices common in automotive.
Operational Systems Referenced: SAP MM/SRM concepts are clearly reflected in the data structures (purchase requisitions, purchase orders, scheduling agreements, info records, goods receipts).
Gaps / Suggestions:
The MVM excludes the entire Procurement domain (marked as "Domain not in MVM"). For small-to-mid automotive businesses, basic purchase order and supplier management should arguably be in the MVM. The current workaround of having "stub" tables (purchaseorder, poline, supplier) in the MVM Supply domain partially addresses this, but these are marked as "MVM only (stub or new)" which feels incomplete.
No explicit modeling of e-procurement portals or supplier collaboration platforms (e.g., Ariba, Covisint/SupplyOn).
Commodity management and hedging (important for raw material purchasing in automotive) is absent.
Verdict: Well covered in the ECM; adequate but thin in the MVM.
---
2.3 Production / Manufacturing - COVERED
Model Domains: Manufacturing, Quality, Inventory
Strengths:
The Manufacturing domain is comprehensive with plant operations, production execution, quality assurance, and supply management subdomains.
Key manufacturing concepts are modeled: production orders, build sequences, build stages, vehicle builds, production confirmations, material consumption, downtime events, shop floor events, WIP inventory.
The Quality domain includes the full IATF 16949 / APQP toolkit: FMEA, control plans, inspection plans, SPC charts, PPAP submissions, defect management, and audit capabilities.
Manufacturing BOM (mBOM) and routing are properly separated from the engineering BOM.
Capacity planning, production scheduling, shift management, and work center modeling are present.
Operational Systems Referenced: SAP PP (Production Planning), MES (Manufacturing Execution System) concepts are well reflected. References to AGV (Automated Guided Vehicle) routes and movements show awareness of Industry 4.0 shopfloor automation.
Gaps / Suggestions:
No explicit MES integration layer - while shopfloorevent captures MES-like data, a more structured MES data model (work instructions, operator assignments per station, cycle time tracking) would be beneficial.
OEE (Overall Equipment Effectiveness) is implicitly calculable from downtimeevent and productionconfirmation data, but an explicit OEE metric view or pre-aggregated OEE data product would be a practical addition.
Paint shop, body shop, and assembly-specific process parameters could be modeled more explicitly (currently generalized under process_parameter in the ECM).
Energy consumption tracking per production line/plant is missing - increasingly important for ESG reporting.
Verdict: Strong coverage. Manufacturing is one of the best-modeled areas.
---
2.4 Logistics - COVERED
Model Domains: Logistics, Inventory
Strengths:
The Logistics domain is well-structured with carrier management, compound operations, customs documentation, and transport planning subdomains.
Finished vehicle logistics are specifically modeled: vehicle compounds, compound movements, vehicle handovers, vehicle transport orders, vessel voyages, load plans.
Inbound logistics (CKD/SKD kits, inbound shipments/inspections) are covered under the Supply domain.
Multi-modal transport is addressed: shipping lines, rail car assignments, vessel voyages, and road transport.
Port processing and customs (import/export declarations) are present in the ECM.
In-transit inventory tracking bridges logistics and inventory management.
Operational Systems Referenced: TMS (Transport Management System) concepts are well reflected. The model structure aligns with SAP TM patterns.
Gaps / Suggestions:
Yard management (vehicle compound storage optimization, slot assignments) is partially covered by vehicle_compound but could be more detailed.
Last-mile delivery (dealer delivery scheduling, customer home delivery for direct-to-consumer models) is underrepresented.
Returnable packaging / container management (Ladungstraeger-Management) - a critical operational topic in automotive logistics - is not explicitly modeled.
Dangerous goods handling is not addressed.
Verdict: Well covered, particularly for finished vehicle distribution. Inbound parts logistics could be slightly more detailed.
---
2.5 Sales - COVERED
Model Domains: Sales, Dealer, Customer
Strengths:
The Sales domain covers lead management, quote/order processing, fleet contracts, incentive programs, and sales territory management.
The Dealer domain is notably strong with dealer operations, inventory management, sales performance, and service support - reflecting the franchise dealer model central to automotive.
Customer domain includes customer identity, engagement analytics, loyalty management, and vehicle ownership.
Fleet sales are well-modeled with fleet contracts, fleet contract lines, and fleet accounts.
Incentive programs and MSRP scheduling are properly included.
The configurator flow (quote to order to vehicle order to production) is traceable through the model.
Operational Systems Referenced: CRM concepts (leads, opportunities, campaigns, activities) align with Salesforce/SAP CRM patterns. DMS (Dealer Management System) integration is referenced.
Gaps / Suggestions:
Online/digital sales channels (configurator sessions, online orders, e-commerce) are absent - increasingly important as OEMs move to agency/direct models.
Used vehicle / pre-owned sales are only covered via usedvehicleappraisal in the dealer domain (ECM only). A more complete CPO (Certified Pre-Owned) workflow would be valuable.
Financing and leasing (F&I - Finance & Insurance) is not modeled, despite being a major revenue stream. This is a notable gap.
Subscription-based vehicle models (vehicle-as-a-service) are partially covered under the Mobility domain but not connected to the Sales flow.
Verdict: Good coverage of traditional OEM-to-dealer sales. Gaps in digital sales, F&I, and subscription models.
---
2.6 Aftersales - COVERED
Model Domains: Aftersales, Dealer (service_support)
Strengths:
The Aftersales domain is one of the most detailed in the model, with subdomains for dealer management, parts logistics, product catalog, service operations, and technical support.
Warranty management is comprehensive: warranty policies, warranty claims, goodwill adjustments, warranty parts returns, service contracts, and service contract claims.
Recall management: recall campaigns, campaign VINs, recall completions, and service campaigns.
Technical Service Bulletins (TSBs) and repair operations are well-modeled.
Parts distribution with service parts, parts order lines, and parts returns supports the aftermarket supply chain.
Labor time standards and MSRP price books support workshop costing.
Operational Systems Referenced: SAP CS (Customer Service), DMS integration concepts are present. The model reflects standard warranty systems (e.g., OEM warranty platforms).
Gaps / Suggestions:
Connected vehicle diagnostics integration (OBD-II live data feeding into aftersales workflows) is only present in the Mobility domain (ECM), not directly linked to aftersales service operations.
Over-the-air (OTA) software updates as an aftersales activity (vs. recall alternative) could be better connected to the aftersales service flow.
Customer self-service portals (appointment booking, service history access) are not modeled.
Extended warranty / third-party warranty provider data is limited.
Verdict: Strong coverage. Aftersales is one of the model's highlights.
---
2.7 Field Services - PARTIALLY COVERED
Model Domains: No dedicated domain; partially distributed across Aftersales, Dealer, and Mobility
Assessment:
Field services in the automotive context can mean different things:
a) Dealer Field Representatives (OEM to Dealer support):
dealerrepassignment exists in the Sales domain (ECM only).
Dealer quality assessments and performance scorecards exist.
However, a structured field visit / field activity tracking model for OEM field representatives is absent.
b) Mobile Service / Roadside Assistance:
Not modeled at all. No data products for roadside assistance cases, mobile mechanic dispatching, towing events, or breakdown management.
c) Field Quality & Warranty [INTERNAL-TEAM]:
qualityppapsubmission, supplierqualityevent, and field_return exist in the Quality domain.
warrantyqualitysignal is in the ECM.
But a dedicated "field quality investigation" or "field failure analysis" data product is missing.
d) Connected Vehicle Field Data:
The Mobility domain (ECM only) has telemetry events, DTC events, predictive maintenance alerts, and remote diagnostics - these are strong building blocks for field service intelligence.
However, this domain is entirely excluded from the MVM.
Gaps / Suggestions:
A dedicated Field Services domain (or subdomain) would strengthen the model - covering field technician dispatching, mobile service orders, roadside assistance, field quality investigations, and field engineering reports.
Integration between connected vehicle telemetry and service scheduling (proactive maintenance triggers) should be modeled as a cross-domain workflow.
Verdict: Partially covered. Field services concepts are scattered across multiple domains without a cohesive structure. This is the weakest area of the value chain coverage.
---
3. Operational Systems Coverage Summary

---
4. Cross-Cutting Observations
MVM vs. ECM balance: The MVM excludes 5 entire domains (Asset, Mobility, Procurement, Product, Workforce). While the MVM is designed to be lean, excluding Procurement and Mobility entirely may be too aggressive - basic purchasing and connected vehicle data are increasingly core even for smaller operations.
Industry 4.0 / Digitalization: The model has some Industry 4.0 elements (AGV, digital twins, OTA) but could be more explicit about IoT sensor data, edge computing data flows, and AI/ML model metadata (e.g., predictive quality models, computer vision inspection results).
ESG / Sustainability: Environmental, Social, and Governance data is underrepresented. CO2 emissions tracking, energy consumption, water usage, social compliance audits, and ESG reporting structures are increasingly mandatory (CSRD, EU Taxonomy) and not modeled.
Data Governance: The model includes compliance and audit domains but does not explicitly model data catalog metadata, data quality rules, data lineage, or data ownership - which are important for a Lakehouse architecture.
Metric Views: Both models include metric views (101 in ECM, 128 in MVM), which is a practical addition for analytics readiness. The MVM actually has more metric views than the ECM, suggesting a stronger analytics focus in the lighter model.
---
5. Overall Assessment

Overall Verdict: The automotive data model is a well-structured, comprehensive reference model that covers the majority of the automotive value chain. The ECM variant in particular offers enterprise-grade breadth with 19 domains and 548 tables. The main area for improvement is Field Services, which should be consolidated into a dedicated domain. Secondary recommendations include adding F&I (Finance & Insurance) for sales, strengthening the MVM's procurement coverage, and adding ESG/sustainability data products.
---

Projected date on which the last surviving granted patent in the family will expire, calculated as 20 years from the earliest filing date (utility) or 15 years from grant (design), subject to patent term extensions. Used for IP portfolio lifecycle planning.
Name of the external law firm or patent attorney firm responsible for prosecuting and maintaining this patent family. Used for outside counsel management and cost allocation.
Externally-known alphanumeric identifier assigned to the patent family by the IP management system or patent office (e.g., INPADOC family number). Used for cross-referencing across jurisdictions.
Current lifecycle status of the patent family reflecting the overall prosecution and enforcement state across all member applications.
Official title of the invention as filed, representing the primary human-readable label for the patent family. Typically derived from the earliest priority application.

Classification of the patent family by the nature of the intellectual property protection sought. Indicates whether a FRAND licensing commitment has been formally declared to a standards body for this patent family. Triggers specific licensing obligations and royalty rate constraints.

Result of the most recent Freedom-to-Operate (FTO) analysis for the technology covered by this patent family, indicating whether the company can commercialize the invention without infringing third-party rights.

Number of independent claims in the lead application, each defining a distinct scope of protection. Independent claims are the primary measure of patent breadth.

Total number of named inventors across all applications in the patent family. Used for inventor recognition reporting and royalty distribution calculations.
Legal name of the corporate entity that holds title to the patent family (assignee of record). May differ from the operating business unit when IP is held by a holding company or subsidiary.

Cumulative licensing revenue received for this patent family in the current fiscal year, expressed in the reporting currency. Used for IP monetization performance tracking.

Reference master defining the standard build stages in the vehicle manufacturing process (e.g., Stamping, Body Shop, E-Coat, Paint, Trim-1, Chassis, Trim-2, Final, PDI). Captures stage code, stage name, sequence order, process area, standard cycle time, and applicable vehicle types. Used to structure vehicle_build traceability and production reporting.
became.after: Manufacturing build stage definitions (body shop, paint, trim, final assembly) with process parameters

became.before: production_execution

Master record for plant and line capacity planning, capturing planned production capacity by plant, production line, shift pattern, and planning period (weekly/monthly). Includes rated capacity (JPH × available hours), demonstrated capacity, capacity utilization percentage, bottleneck work center, planned overtime hours, and capacity plan version. Supports S&OP (Sales and Operations Planning) and capital investment decisions.
became.after: Production capacity planning records for lines and plants with demand vs available capacity

became.before: Transactional record for production line changeover events when switching between vehicle models, body styles, or powertrain variants on a shared production line. Captures changeover type (model mix change, color change, tooling swap, line retooling), planned and actual changeover start/end times, duration, affected production line, changeover team, and production loss (units not produced). Supports SMED (Single-Minute Exchange of Die) improvement programs.
became.after: Production line changeover events when switching between vehicle models or variants

became.before: production_execution

This association product records the compliance certification of a production order against a specific regulatory requirement. It captures the compliance status, supporting evidence document path, and the date the certification was achieved for each order‑requirement pair.. Existence Justification: Each production order must be verified against multiple regulatory requirements, and each regulatory requirement applies to many production orders. The compliance status, supporting evidence, and certification date are recorded for every order‑requirement pair, and quality engineers actively create, update, and delete these records as part of the manufacturing compliance process.
became.after: Manufacturing compliance certifications (ISO, IATF, environmental) for plants and production lines

became.before: quality_assurance

Transactional record capturing unplanned and planned production downtime events at the work center or line level. Tracks downtime start and end timestamps, duration (minutes), downtime category (mechanical failure, tooling change, material shortage, quality hold, scheduled maintenance, changeover), affected work center, production order impact, and responsible team. Critical for OEE analysis and SCADA-integrated downtime reporting.
became.after: Production line and equipment downtime events with root cause, duration, and OEE impact

became.before: production_execution
Master reference table for factory_calendar. Referenced by factory_calendar_id.
became.after: Factory calendar defining working days, holidays, shutdown periods, and special production days

became.before: Line-item record within a manufacturing BOM representing a single component or sub-assembly required to build a vehicle. Captures component part number, description, quantity per vehicle, unit of measure, installation work center, installation sequence, alternative part references, effectivity start/end dates, and scrap factor. Supports JIT/JIS material call-offs and shop floor assembly instructions.
became.after: Individual component line items within a production BOM with quantities, effectivity, and sourcing details

became.before: supply_management

Represents the contractual agreement between a manufacturing plant and a supplier. Each record captures the specific terms that apply to that plant‑supplier pair, such as lead time, minimum order quantity, pricing, and quality requirements.. Existence Justification: Each manufacturing plant can source materials from multiple suppliers, and each supplier can serve multiple plants. The business manages these plant‑supplier links through contracts that capture lead times, minimum order quantities, pricing, and other terms. The relationship is actively created, updated, and tracked as a distinct agreement.
became.after: Supply agreements between manufacturing plants and suppliers for JIT/JIS material delivery

became.before: supply_management

Transactional record tracking the usage of production tooling (dies, fixtures, jigs, welding guns, torque tools) against specific production orders and work centers. Captures tool ID, tool type, usage start and end timestamps, production order reference, work center, stroke count or cycle count, cumulative usage against tool life limit, and tool condition at usage. Supports predictive tooling maintenance and PPAP tooling traceability.
became.after: Tooling usage records tracking tool deployment, cycle counts, and wear on the manufacturing floor This product is the single source of truth (SSOT) for its concept in the ECM Lakehouse.

became.before: production_execution

Transactional record capturing actual material consumption (goods issue) against a production order on the shop floor. Tracks consumed part number, quantity consumed, unit of measure, consumption timestamp, work center, production order reference, storage location, batch number, and variance from planned BOM quantity. Feeds SAP MM goods movement and cost accounting for production variance reporting.
became.after: Material consumption postings against production orders tracking actual vs planned usage

became.before: production_execution
Master reference table for operator_team. Referenced by operator_team_id.
became.after: Operator team definitions for production line staffing and shift assignments

became.before: Master record for each manufacturing plant or assembly facility operated by Automotive. Captures plant identity, location, type (stamping, body shop, paint, final assembly, CKD/SKD), production capacity, SOP/EOP dates, plant code, and operational status. SSOT for plant-level identity referenced across MES, SAP PP, and logistics domains.
became.after: Manufacturing plant/facility master data including location, capacity, certifications and operational parameters

became.before: Transactional record capturing actual process parameter readings collected from PLC/SCADA systems during manufacturing operations. Includes parameter type (weld current, weld time, torque value, paint film thickness, oven temperature, press force, adhesive bead width), measured value, upper and lower control limits (UCL/LCL), pass/fail status, timestamp, work center, production order, and VIN reference. Supports SPC (Statistical Process Control) and IATF 16949 process monitoring requirements.
became.after: Manufacturing process parameters (torque, temperature, pressure, etc.) captured from PLC/SCADA systems

became.before: production_execution

Manufacturing Bill of Materials (BOM) record representing the production-level BOM used on the shop floor for a specific vehicle configuration and model year. Distinct from the engineering BOM (eBOM) in the engineering domain — this is the manufacturing BOM (mBOM) as released to production. Captures BOM header (vehicle model, MY, plant, effectivity dates), BOM status, and reference to the engineering change order that authorized it. Managed via SAP PP and Teamcenter PLM BOM transfer.
became.after: Production bill of materials (MBOM) derived from engineering BOM with plant-specific configurations

became.before: supply_management

Transactional record confirming the completion of a production order or a partial operation within a production order. Captures confirmation number, production order reference, confirmed quantity (yield and scrap), actual activity times (setup, machine, labor), confirmation timestamp, shift, work center, and operator. Triggers SAP PP order settlement and inventory goods receipt. SSOT for actual production output reporting.
became.after: Production order confirmations recording completed operations, quantities, and labor/machine hours

became.before: production_execution

Master record for each production line within a plant, including stamping lines, body shop lines, paint booths, and final assembly lines. Tracks line code, line type, designed throughput (JPH - Jobs Per Hour), current shift configuration, AGV integration flags, PLC/SCADA system references, and operational status. Owned by manufacturing as the SSOT for line-level capacity and configuration.
became.after: Assembly/production line master data including capacity, automation level, and MES integration

became.before: Core transactional record representing a manufacturing work order issued to produce a specific vehicle or sub-assembly. Captures order number, order type (vehicle build, sub-assembly, rework), planned and actual start/finish dates, target quantity, produced quantity, order status, priority, shift assignment, and MES order reference. Links to plant, production line, and vehicle configuration. SSOT for shop floor execution tracking in SAP PP and Apriso MES.
became.after: Production/manufacturing order for vehicle or component production with scheduling, costing, and status tracking

became.before: production_execution

Represents the allocation of a manufacturing production order to a dealership. Each record links one production order to one dealership and captures allocation-specific details such as allocation number, status, date, priority tier, and type.. Existence Justification: Production orders are work orders that generate vehicles, and the allocation process assigns portions of these orders to multiple dealerships for distribution. A single production order can be split across several dealerships, and each dealership receives many production orders over time. The allocation itself carries attributes such as allocation number, status, date, priority tier, and type, which are managed as a distinct business entity.
became.after: Allocation of production orders to specific lines, shifts, and time slots for scheduling optimization

became.before: quality_assurance

Master production schedule (MPS) record defining planned vehicle production volumes by plant, production line, model, MY (Model Year), and time period (daily, weekly, monthly). Captures scheduled quantity, confirmed quantity, schedule version, freeze horizon, schedule status, and MRP run reference. Integrates with SAP PP MRP and supports capacity planning and supplier call-off generation.
became.after: Production scheduling data including planned volumes, capacity utilization, and freeze horizons

became.before: Reference master defining the valid production variants (option combinations) that can be built on a specific production line for a given model year. Captures variant code, model, MY, powertrain type (ICE, HEV, PHEV, BEV), body style, trim level, market destination, and line compatibility flags. Supports build sequence feasibility validation and JIS sequencing rules. Distinct from the commercial product catalog — this is the manufacturing-feasible variant definition.
became.after: Production variant definitions representing buildable vehicle configurations on a production line

became.before: quality_assurance

Transactional record for rework or repair operations initiated on a vehicle or sub-assembly that failed an in-process quality check. Captures rework order number, originating production order, VIN reference, defect description, rework type (in-line repair, offline rework, teardown), assigned work center, planned and actual rework hours, rework status, and disposition (repaired, scrapped, concession). Integrates with quality domain defect records.
became.after: Rework orders for defective units requiring correction before proceeding in production

became.before: quality_assurance
Master reference table for routing. Referenced by routing_id.
became.after: Manufacturing routing definitions specifying the sequence of operations for producing a product

became.before: supply_management

Transactional record capturing scrapped materials, components, or vehicle units during the manufacturing process. Tracks scrap item (part number or VIN), scrap quantity, scrap reason code, scrap location (work center, process stage), production order reference, scrap value, disposal method, and authorization reference. Feeds SAP CO production variance accounting and quality PPM (Parts Per Million) defect rate reporting.
became.after: Scrap records for materials and components scrapped during production with reason codes and costs

became.before: production_execution

Reference master for production shift definitions at each plant and production line. Captures shift code, shift name (Day, Afternoon, Night, Weekend), planned start and end times, break schedule, planned production hours, and applicable plant and line assignments. Used for production order scheduling, OEE calculation, and workforce planning integration.
became.after: Shift definition and scheduling including break patterns, capacity targets, and OEE goals

became.before: Granular transactional record capturing real-time shop floor events generated by MES, PLC, and SCADA systems during production. Includes event type (station entry, station exit, torque confirmation, weld completion, paint cure, AGV arrival, hold trigger, alarm), event timestamp, work center, production order reference, VIN reference, operator ID, and event payload. Enables real-time production monitoring and OEE (Overall Equipment Effectiveness) calculation.
became.after: Real-time shop floor events from MES/SCADA including quality checks, machine events, and operator actions

became.before: production_execution

Transactional record capturing the actual build event for a single vehicle unit on the shop floor, from body-in-white through final assembly. Tracks VIN assignment, production order reference, actual start and completion timestamps per build stage (stamping, body shop, paint, trim, chassis, final), build status, shift, operator team, and any hold or rework flags. SSOT for vehicle-level build traceability and genealogy in the manufacturing domain.
became.after: Individual vehicle build record tracking the manufacturing lifecycle from body shop through final assembly

became.before: production_execution

Represents the contractual relationship between a vehicle build and a mobility service. Each record captures the period of subscription, billing details, status, and the service tier applicable to that vehicle.. Existence Justification: Each vehicle build can be subscribed to multiple mobility services (e.g., remote diagnostics, OTA updates) and each mobility service can be subscribed by many vehicle builds across the fleet. The subscription is an operational contract that is created, updated, and terminated by business users, and it carries its own attributes such as start/end dates, billing amount, and status.
became.after: Subscription-based vehicle production orders linking mobility service subscriptions to manufacturing

became.before: quality_assurance

Snapshot and movement record for Work-in-Progress (WIP) inventory on the shop floor. Tracks WIP item identity, associated VIN or sub-assembly ID, current location (work center, buffer zone, AGV carrier), quantity, WIP status (in-process, on-hold, awaiting inspection, scrapped), entry and exit timestamps per location, and production order reference. Supports real-time WIP visibility and JIT material flow management.
became.after: Work-in-progress inventory tracking parts and sub-assemblies on the production floor

became.before: production_execution

Master record for individual work centers (stations) within a production line. Captures work center code, name, type (manual, automated, robotic), cycle time standard, takt time, capacity category, shift availability, and associated PLC/SCADA node identifiers. Supports JIS sequencing and MES shop floor execution at the station level.
became.after: Work center master data representing individual manufacturing stations with capacity, cost rates, and equipment details

before.description: Identifier of the AGV fleet management controller or traffic management system (e.g., a specific SCADA or AGV supervisor node) that dispatched and managed this movement. Supports multi-controller fleet architectures and fault isolation.

The manufacturing assembly stage to which this AGV movement is associated (e.g., stamping, body shop, paint, trim, chassis, final assembly). Enables stage-level material flow analysis and supports multi-stage production traceability.
The average travel speed of the AGV in metres per second during this movement. Used to identify speed anomalies, assess compliance with shop floor speed limits, and support throughput optimization.

The AGV battery state of charge as a percentage at the time the movement task ended. Combined with battery_level_start_pct to calculate energy consumption per movement and model battery degradation over time.

The AGV battery state of charge as a percentage at the time the movement task began. Used for fleet energy management, charge scheduling optimization, and identifying movements that may have been impacted by low battery conditions.

The shop floor location code of the target delivery point for this AGV movement. Used to verify correct delivery to the intended assembly station or buffer zone and to support JIS (Just-in-Sequence) call-off validation.
Human-readable descriptive name of the destination location (e.g., 'Final Assembly Line 2 Station 14', 'Trim Shop Sequencing Buffer'). Supports operational dashboards and exception reporting.

The total distance in metres travelled by the AGV during this movement event, as reported by the AGV's odometry or navigation system. Used for fleet utilization reporting, energy consumption modelling, and route efficiency analysis.

became.before: workforce.employee.employee_id

before.description: The identifier of the shop floor operator or MES user who manually initiated, overrode, or acknowledged this AGV movement task. Null for fully automated movements with no human intervention. Supports operator accountability and manual override tracking.

The fault or exception code reported by the AGV or fleet controller during this movement (e.g., obstacle detected, navigation error, battery low, load sensor failure). Null if no fault occurred. Used for predictive maintenance, FMEA (Failure Mode and Effects Analysis), and fleet reliability reporting.
Human-readable description of the fault or exception that occurred during this movement. Provides operational context for maintenance technicians and MES operators beyond the structured fault_code.

The precise date and time when the fault or exception was detected during this AGV movement. Null if no fault occurred. Used for mean time between failures (MTBF) calculation and maintenance response time analysis.

Indicates whether this AGV movement was manually overridden or initiated by a human operator rather than being fully automated by the MES or AGV fleet controller (True = manual override, False = fully automated). Used for automation rate reporting and exception analysis.

Indicates whether this AGV movement was triggered by a JIS (Just-in-Sequence) call-off signal from the assembly line (True = JIS-triggered, False = standard replenishment or non-sequenced movement). Critical for sequencing compliance reporting and line-feed performance analysis.

The weight in kilograms of the load carried by the AGV during this movement, as measured by the AGV's onboard load sensor. Used for payload compliance monitoring, energy consumption analysis, and overload fault detection.

The unique task or dispatch identifier assigned by the MES (Manufacturing Execution System) — specifically Apriso/Dassault — to this AGV movement instruction. Used for cross-system reconciliation between the AGV fleet controller and the MES shop floor execution layer.

The precise date and time (ISO 8601 with timezone offset) when the AGV completed or terminated the movement task. Null if the movement is still in progress. Used with movement_start_timestamp to derive actual cycle time.

The precise date and time (ISO 8601 with timezone offset) when the AGV began executing the movement task. Used for cycle time calculation, throughput analysis, and JIS (Just-in-Sequence) compliance verification.

before.description: The identifier of the shop floor operator or MES user who manually initiated, overrode, or acknowledged this AGV movement task. Null for fully automated movements with no human intervention. Supports operator accountability and manual override tracking.

The shop floor location code (e.g., storage lane, buffer zone, work station address) from which the AGV departed for this movement. Encoded per the plant's internal location addressing scheme (e.g., aisle-bay-level). Used for material flow mapping and route optimization.

Human-readable descriptive name of the origin location (e.g., 'Body Shop Buffer Lane 3', 'Paint Shop Entry Conveyor', 'Stamping Parts Supermarket'). Supports operational reporting and shop floor visualization dashboards.

Human-readable description of the part or component being transported (e.g., 'Front Door Inner Panel LH', 'Battery Module Assembly EV'). Supports operational reporting without requiring a join to the parts master.

The OEM (Original Equipment Manufacturer) part number of the primary component or assembly being transported by the AGV. Supports Bill of Materials (BOM) traceability and JIS (Just-in-Sequence) delivery verification at the assembly line.
The MES-scheduled completion time for this AGV movement task. Compared against movement_end_timestamp to measure on-time delivery performance and identify bottlenecks in material flow.
The MES-scheduled start time for this AGV movement task. Compared against movement_start_timestamp to measure schedule adherence and identify JIS (Just-in-Sequence) delivery deviations.

The dispatch priority assigned to this AGV movement by the MES or AGV fleet controller. Critical and high priority movements are typically associated with JIS (Just-in-Sequence) call-offs or line-stop prevention. Used for queue management and SLA reporting.

The number of parts, units, or assemblies carried by the AGV in this movement. Used for material flow volume reporting, inventory reconciliation, and JIT (Just-in-Time) delivery quantity verification.

Indicates whether the AGV deviated from its assigned route during this movement (True = deviation occurred, False = route followed as planned). Deviations may indicate obstacles, dynamic re-routing, or system faults requiring investigation.

Current or target assembly stage for this sequence position: 'stamping' = metal forming; 'body_shop' = body-in-white welding; 'paint' = paint application; 'final_assembly' = trim and chassis assembly; 'PDI' = Pre-Delivery Inspection. Drives shop floor routing in the MES.

Drivetrain configuration of the vehicle: FWD (Front-Wheel Drive), RWD (Rear-Wheel Drive), AWD (All-Wheel Drive), or 4WD (Four-Wheel Drive). Determines axle and driveshaft JIS call-off and assembly routing.

Code identifying the regulatory homologation variant of the vehicle (e.g., US-NHTSA, EU-UNECE, CARB-ZEV). Ensures correct BOM variant selection for emissions, safety, and market-specific compliance requirements.

Free-text or coded reason for the most recent modification to this build sequence record (e.g., material shortage, quality hold, customer order change, line disruption). Required for change control audit trail under IATF 16949.

became.before: vehicle.configuration.configuration_id

before.description: Reference to the vehicle configuration record defining the model, trim, powertrain, and option codes for the vehicle to be assembled at this sequence position.

Comma-separated list of vehicle body types or powertrain categories for which this build stage applies (e.g., Sedan, SUV, Truck, EV, HEV, PHEV, ICE, Commercial). Enables stage filtering in mixed-model assembly lines and supports model-specific production routing. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: Sedan|SUV|Truck|EV|HEV|PHEV|ICE|Commercial|CKD|SKD — promote to reference product]

Maximum number of vehicle units that can be held in the buffer/queue between this build stage and the next stage. Defines the WIP (Work in Progress) inventory limit for line balancing and is used in production simulation and bottleneck analysis.

Standard CO2-equivalent emissions in kilograms per vehicle unit processed at this build stage. Supports EPA and CARB (California Air Resources Board) environmental compliance reporting, sustainability KPIs, and manufacturing carbon footprint tracking.

Reference code of the APQP (Advanced Product Quality Planning) control plan document governing quality control activities at this build stage. Specifies product/process characteristics, control methods, and reaction plans for out-of-control conditions per IATF 16949.

The EOP (End of Production) date on which this build stage is scheduled to be or was decommissioned. Null if the stage is currently active with no planned end date. Used for production planning horizon management and asset retirement scheduling.

Reference identifier linking this build stage to its corresponding FMEA (Failure Mode and Effects Analysis) document. Ensures traceability between the process stage definition and its risk assessment per IATF 16949 and APQP (Advanced Product Quality Planning) requirements.

Classification of hazardous materials present or used at this build stage per DOT and EPA regulations (e.g., paint solvents, E-Coat chemicals, welding fumes). Drives EHS (Environmental Health and Safety) compliance, PPE requirements, and ISO 14001 environmental management reporting.

IATF 16949 process category designation for this build stage: special-characteristic (processes producing special product/process characteristics requiring enhanced control), standard-process, critical-process (safety-critical per FMVSS), or monitoring-only (observation without active control). Drives audit scope and PPAP (Production Part Approval Process) requirements.

Maximum allowable ambient or process temperature in degrees Celsius for this build stage. Exceeding this threshold triggers a quality hold and SCADA alarm. Particularly relevant for paint curing ovens, E-Coat baths, and weld quality control.

Minimum allowable ambient or process temperature in degrees Celsius for this build stage to operate within specification. Critical for paint shop, E-Coat, and adhesive curing stages where temperature directly affects product quality. Used in SPC (Statistical Process Control) monitoring.

Comma-separated list of MY (Model Year) designations for which this build stage definition is applicable (e.g., MY2024,MY2025) or ALL if applicable across all model years. Supports model-year-specific production routing and engineering change management.

Alphanumeric code identifying the specific plant area or shop within the manufacturing facility where this build stage is physically located (e.g., SH01 for Stamping Hall 1, BS02 for Body Shop 2). Aligns with SAP S/4HANA work center and plant layout master data.

Identifier of the PLC (Programmable Logic Controller) program controlling the automated equipment at this build stage. Used for change management, version control of control programs, and traceability of equipment configuration changes per IATF 16949 requirements.

Target defect rate for this build stage expressed in PPM (Parts Per Million). Defines the quality performance benchmark used in IATF 16949 supplier and process quality reporting, SPC control limit setting, and continuous improvement initiatives.

Stage code of the immediately preceding build stage in the standard production sequence. Defines the upstream dependency for production flow control, WIP (Work in Progress) tracking, and JIS (Just-in-Sequence) scheduling. Null for the first stage in the sequence.

Reference code of the SAP QM (Quality Management) inspection plan associated with this build stage. Defines the inspection characteristics, sampling procedures, and acceptance criteria applied during quality gate checks. Linked to FMEA (Failure Mode and Effects Analysis) and APQP documentation.

Safety risk classification of this build stage per DOT and OSHA standards: standard (routine operations), elevated-risk (requires additional PPE or safety protocols), critical-safety (safety-critical operations with mandatory sign-off), or restricted-access (limited to certified personnel only).

The SAP S/4HANA PP routing operation code corresponding to this build stage. Enables direct linkage between the build stage reference master and SAP production order routing operations for cost allocation, scheduling, and confirmation.

Standard shift pattern under which this build stage operates: single (one shift per day), double (two shifts), triple (three shifts), or continuous (24/7 operation). Used for capacity planning, labor scheduling in SuccessFactors, and production throughput calculations.

The SOP (Start of Production) date on which this build stage was first commissioned and became operational for regular production. Used for asset lifecycle tracking, warranty baseline calculations, and production history reporting.

Stage code of the immediately succeeding build stage in the standard production sequence. Defines the downstream handoff point for production flow control and vehicle build traceability. Null for the final stage (PDI) in the sequence.

became.before: workforce.employee.employee_id

before.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: REQUIRED: Each build stage is overseen by a supervisor employee; needed for accountability and shift handover reports.

SAP S/4HANA work center identifier associated with this build stage. Links the build stage to capacity planning, cost center allocation, and production order routing in the ERP system. Enables integration between MES stage execution and SAP PP/CO modules.
Date and time when the capacity plan was formally approved by the designated authority. Marks the transition from 'submitted' to 'approved' status in the S&OP governance process.
Name or employee identifier of the S&OP or manufacturing leadership authority who approved this capacity plan. Required for audit trail and governance compliance under IATF 16949.

Total scheduled production hours available in the planning period after accounting for planned downtime, shift breaks, and scheduled maintenance. Used in conjunction with rated_capacity_jph to compute rated capacity in units.

Narrative description of the primary capacity constraint at the bottleneck work center (e.g., 'Paint oven cycle time limits throughput to 58 JPH', 'Robotic welding cell maintenance window reduces available hours'). Supports root cause analysis and CapEx justification.

became.before: manufacturing.work_center.work_center_id

before.description: Reference to the work center identified as the capacity bottleneck constraining overall line throughput during this planning period. Used to prioritize capacity improvement investments and focus S&OP constraint management.

Difference between planned_production_units and demonstrated_capacity_units, representing the capacity shortfall or surplus for the planning period. Positive value indicates a capacity gap requiring corrective action (overtime, additional shifts, CapEx); negative value indicates surplus capacity.

Classification of the capacity planning methodology used. 'rough_cut' (RCCP — Rough Cut Capacity Planning) for high-level S&OP; 'detailed' for work-center-level CRP (Capacity Requirements Planning); 'constraint_based' for Theory of Constraints analysis; 'what_if' for scenario planning and CapEx evaluation.

Planned capacity utilization rate expressed as a percentage, calculated as (planned_production_units / rated_capacity_units) × 100. Drives S&OP decisions on overtime, additional shifts, and capital investment. Target thresholds are typically 85–95% for automotive assembly.

Estimated capital expenditure amount required to address the capacity gap identified in this plan. Expressed in the plant's operating currency. Used for CapEx budget submissions and investment approval processes.

Indicates whether this capacity plan identifies a requirement for capital investment (CapEx) to close a capacity gap (e.g., new tooling, additional robots, facility expansion). Triggers CapEx approval workflow in SAP FI/CO.

Hours allocated for model changeovers, tooling changes, and line reconfigurations during the planning period. Relevant for mixed-model assembly lines producing multiple vehicle variants (e.g., ICE and BEV on the same line).

ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for all monetary values in this capacity plan record (e.g., USD, EUR, MXN, CNY). Ensures consistent financial reporting across multi-plant, multi-currency manufacturing operations.

Planned number of vehicles to be produced per working day during the planning period, derived from planned_production_units / working_days. Used for daily MES scheduling and shift-level production targets.

Actual production output achieved in a comparable prior period, used as the realistic baseline for capacity planning. Reflects real-world constraints such as quality losses, minor stoppages, and changeovers. Key input to APQP (Advanced Product Quality Planning) capacity studies.

became.before: workforce.employee.employee_id

before.description: Reference to the manufacturing or industrial engineering employee responsible for maintaining and updating this capacity plan. Supports accountability tracking in S&OP governance.

Planned End of Production (EOP) date for the vehicle model or program covered by this capacity plan. Marks the milestone when production of the model is scheduled to cease. Used for capacity wind-down planning and asset redeployment decisions.
Fiscal year (FY) to which this capacity plan belongs, used for CapEx (Capital Expenditure) alignment, budget planning, and financial reporting. Format: FY followed by 4-digit year (e.g., FY2025).

Total direct labor headcount required to execute the planned production volume during the planning period. Used for workforce planning, hiring decisions, and labor cost budgeting in SuccessFactors and SAP CO.

Indicates whether the capacity plan is constrained by a bottleneck work center that limits overall line throughput below the planned production target. When True, the bottleneck_work_center_id and bottleneck_constraint_description fields are populated.
Automotive model year (MY) for which this capacity plan is prepared. Capacity plans are typically aligned to MY production programs, SOP (Start of Production), and EOP (End of Production) milestones.
Number of production shifts planned per working day for this capacity plan (e.g., 1, 2, or 3 shifts). Directly determines available production hours and total capacity for the planning period.
Last calendar date of the planning period covered by this capacity plan record. Together with plan_start_date, defines the planning window for capacity supply and demand balancing.

Externally-known, human-readable business identifier for the capacity plan record, used in S&OP (Sales and Operations Planning) communications, SAP PP capacity planning transactions (CM01/CM21), and cross-functional reporting. Format: CP-{PLANT}-{YEAR}-{MONTH}-{SEQ}.

became.before: workforce.employee.employee_id

before.description: Reference to the manufacturing or industrial engineering employee responsible for maintaining and updating this capacity plan. Supports accountability tracking in S&OP governance.
First calendar date of the planning period covered by this capacity plan record. Used to align capacity supply with demand signals from S&OP and MRP (Material Requirements Planning) runs.

Version identifier of the capacity plan, enabling management of multiple planning iterations (e.g., v1.0, v2.0) within the same planning period. Supports S&OP cycle versioning and plan-over-plan variance analysis.

Total planned downtime hours for the production line during the planning period, including scheduled maintenance, tooling changeovers, model changeovers, and planned shutdowns. Reduces available production hours from the theoretical maximum.

Subset of planned downtime hours specifically allocated to preventive and predictive maintenance activities on production equipment. Tracked separately from changeover downtime for maintenance KPI reporting and SAP PM integration.

Total overtime hours planned for the production line during the planning period to meet production targets beyond standard shift capacity. Feeds into workforce cost planning and labor budget in SAP CO.

Number of vehicles planned for production in the planning period as agreed in the S&OP process. Represents the demand signal that capacity must satisfy. Compared against rated and demonstrated capacity to identify gaps.

Granularity of the capacity planning horizon for this record. 'weekly' supports short-term MES scheduling; 'monthly' supports S&OP cycles; 'quarterly' and 'annual' support CapEx and strategic workforce planning.

Demand scenario underpinning this capacity plan. 'base' reflects the consensus S&OP forecast; 'optimistic' reflects upside demand; 'pessimistic' reflects downside risk; 'stretch' reflects maximum achievable output. Enables scenario comparison for executive decision-making.

Powertrain technology type planned for production in this capacity plan. ICE = Internal Combustion Engine; HEV = Hybrid Electric Vehicle; PHEV = Plug-in Hybrid Electric Vehicle; BEV = Battery Electric Vehicle; FCEV = Fuel Cell Electric Vehicle. Impacts tooling, line configuration, and capacity requirements.

Theoretical maximum production rate expressed in Jobs Per Hour (JPH) for the production line under ideal conditions. Derived from takt time and line design specifications. Used as the baseline for capacity utilization calculations in S&OP.

Theoretical maximum number of vehicles that can be produced in the planning period, calculated as rated_capacity_jph × available_hours. Represents the upper bound of production capacity for S&OP and CapEx planning.

Source system identifier for this capacity plan record in SAP S/4HANA PP (Production Planning) module, used for data lineage traceability and reconciliation between the lakehouse Silver layer and the operational ERP system.

became.before: manufacturing.shift.shift_id

before.description: Reference to the shift pattern (e.g., 1-shift, 2-shift, 3-shift) applied in this capacity plan. Shift pattern determines available production hours and directly impacts rated capacity calculation.

Planned Start of Production (SOP) date for the vehicle model or program covered by this capacity plan. Marks the milestone when full-rate production is scheduled to begin. Critical for capacity ramp-up planning and APQP milestone tracking.

Planned takt time in seconds for the production line during this planning period, representing the rate at which vehicles must be produced to meet customer demand. Takt time = available production time / planned production units. Core metric in JIS (Just-in-Sequence) and line balancing.

Internal OEM (Original Equipment Manufacturer) code identifying the vehicle model or program (e.g., platform code, nameplate code) for which this capacity plan is prepared. Enables capacity planning at the model/program level.

Actual date and time when the changeover physically commenced on the production line, as recorded by MES (Manufacturing Execution System) or operator input.

Indicates whether the changeover was a scheduled/planned event (True) or an unplanned/emergency changeover triggered by a quality issue, equipment failure, or urgent customer order change (False).

Flags whether this changeover event is designated as a target for SMED (Single-Minute Exchange of Die) improvement analysis. Enables filtering of changeover records for lean manufacturing improvement programs.

Time in minutes spent on post-changeover line verification, first-off inspection, and quality gate checks before resuming full production. Supports APQP (Advanced Product Quality Planning) and PPAP (Production Part Approval Process) compliance.

Native changeover event identifier from the Apriso/Dassault MES (Manufacturing Execution System). Enables traceability and reconciliation between the lakehouse silver layer and the operational MES source system.

Scheduled date and time when the changeover was planned to begin, as defined in the production schedule. Used for SMED (Single-Minute Exchange of Die) baseline comparison.

Indicates whether the post-changeover quality gate inspection was passed (True) before resuming full production. A False value indicates the line was held pending rework or re-inspection per IATF 16949 quality control requirements.

Standardized code indicating the business reason that triggered the changeover event (e.g., scheduled model mix, customer order sequence, engineering change, maintenance requirement). Used for root cause analysis and frequency reporting.
Free-text description providing additional context for the changeover reason, supplementing the reason code with operator or supervisor notes.

Number of vehicle units scrapped or rejected during the changeover transition period before the first good unit was produced. Contributes to quality loss calculation in OEE (Overall Equipment Effectiveness).

Body style classification of the vehicle to be produced after the changeover (e.g., sedan, SUV, truck). Used to categorize body style changeover events.
Paint color code of the vehicle to be produced after the changeover. Relevant for color change changeover events in the paint shop.

Powertrain variant to be produced after the changeover. ICE (Internal Combustion Engine), HEV (Hybrid Electric Vehicle), PHEV (Plug-in Hybrid Electric Vehicle), BEV (Battery Electric Vehicle), FCEV (Fuel Cell Electric Vehicle).
Vehicle model code of the product to be produced on the line immediately after the changeover. Identifies the incoming model in a model mix change scenario.

The engineering-specified nominal or target value for this process parameter as defined in the control plan. Used as the centre line for SPC charting and deviation calculation.

Identifies the operational system of record from which this manufacturing BOM record was sourced (e.g., 'SAP_PP' for SAP Production Planning, 'TEAMCENTER' for Siemens Teamcenter PLM).
