Enables EBITDA (Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortization) analysis at the plant and cost center level.

Total unplanned downtime duration recorded during this production confirmation period, in minutes. Captured from SCADA/PLC systems or MES downtime tracking. Used for OEE (Overall Equipment Effectiveness) availability calculation, maintenance planning, and production loss analysis.

Coded reason for any downtime recorded during this confirmation period. Maps to the plant's downtime reason catalog (e.g., 'MECH' = Mechanical Failure, 'MATL' = Material Shortage, 'QUAL' = Quality Hold, 'CHNG' = Changeover). Used for root cause analysis, maintenance prioritization, and production loss reporting.

Indicates whether this confirmation is the final confirmation for the production order (SAP PP IEDD — Final Confirmation Indicator). When True, SAP PP automatically closes the production order, triggers goods receipt for the finished product, and initiates order settlement to CO (Controlling). Critical for order lifecycle management and inventory accuracy.

Indicates whether the automatic goods receipt (GR) to inventory has been successfully posted as a result of this production confirmation. True = inventory has been updated with the confirmed yield quantity. Used for inventory reconciliation and to identify confirmations where GR posting failed or is pending.

Actual direct labor time consumed for this production operation, recorded in minutes. Maps to SAP PP activity type for labor (ISRLA — Actual Labor Time). Used for labor cost settlement to the production order, workforce productivity analysis, and standard vs. actual cost variance reporting.
Planned direct labor time for this operation as defined in the SAP PP routing, recorded in minutes. Baseline for labor efficiency variance analysis and standard cost calculation.

The timestamp when this production confirmation record was last modified in the source system. Tracks reversals, corrections, and status updates. Used for incremental data loading in the Databricks Silver Layer pipeline and change data capture (CDC) processing.

Actual machine runtime consumed for this production operation, recorded in minutes. Maps to SAP PP activity type for machine time (ISRÜT — Actual Machine Time). Core input for OEE calculation, takt time variance analysis, and capacity utilization reporting. Compared against planned machine time from the routing to identify bottlenecks.
Planned machine time for this operation as defined in the SAP PP routing, recorded in minutes. Baseline for actual vs. planned machine time variance analysis and takt time adherence reporting.

SAP material number (MATNR) of the finished or semi-finished product being confirmed. Identifies the vehicle model, sub-assembly, or component produced in this confirmation. Essential for inventory goods receipt posting and BOM (Bill of Materials) reconciliation.

The confirmation or transaction reference number from the Apriso/Dassault MES system that corresponds to this SAP PP production confirmation. Enables cross-system traceability between the MES shop floor execution record and the SAP ERP confirmation posting. Critical for audit trails and discrepancy resolution.

The vehicle model year (MY) of the product being confirmed. Used for production output reporting by model year, regulatory compliance tracking (CAFE, EPA emissions), and alignment with SOP (Start of Production) and EOP (End of Production) milestones. Retained as a denormalized attribute for direct reporting without joining to vehicle configuration.

became.before: workforce.employee.employee_id

before.description: Reference to the production operator (employee/personnel number) who posted or was responsible for this confirmation. Used for traceability, quality accountability, and workforce productivity analysis. Maps to SAP HR personnel number (PERNR) or MES operator badge ID.

Status of the SAP CO production order settlement triggered by this final confirmation. 'pending' = settlement not yet executed; 'settled' = actual costs fully settled to cost objects; 'partially_settled' = partial settlement completed; 'not_required' = non-final confirmation, settlement not applicable. Used for period-end closing and financial reporting.

became.before: manufacturing.plant.plant_id

before.description: Reference to the manufacturing plant where this production confirmation was posted. Enables plant-level production output reporting, capacity utilization analysis, and multi-plant benchmarking.

The powertrain technology type of the vehicle or assembly being confirmed. ICE = Internal Combustion Engine, HEV = Hybrid Electric Vehicle, PHEV = Plug-in Hybrid Electric Vehicle, BEV = Battery Electric Vehicle, FCEV = Fuel Cell Electric Vehicle. Used for regulatory reporting (CAFE, EPA, CARB), EV production mix analysis, and R&D investment tracking.

SAP PP production order number (AUFNR) to which this confirmation is posted. Links the confirmation to the originating manufacturing order for order settlement, cost collection, and goods receipt triggering. Retained as a business attribute for direct shop floor reporting without requiring a join.

SAP QM inspection lot number (PRUEFLOS) created automatically upon goods receipt posting from this confirmation. Links the production output to the quality inspection record for in-process and final inspection results. Used for quality traceability and IATF 16949 inspection record management.

Flag indicating whether this confirmation record is a reversal entry (CO13 reversal in SAP PP). True = this record reverses a previously posted confirmation. Used to identify correction entries in production output reporting and to exclude reversed confirmations from yield and time aggregations.

became.before: manufacturing.production_confirmation.production_confirmation_id

before.description: Reference to the original production confirmation record that this entry reverses. Populated only when reversal_indicator is True. Enables audit trail reconstruction and net quantity calculation when reversals are present. Self-referencing within the production_confirmation product.

Coded reason for scrap recorded against this confirmation. Maps to SAP QM defect codes or MES scrap reason catalog (e.g., 'DIM' = Dimensional Non-conformance, 'WLD' = Weld Defect, 'PNT' = Paint Defect, 'ASY' = Assembly Error). Required for PPM (Parts Per Million) defect analysis, FMEA updates, and quality improvement initiatives per IATF 16949.

Actual machine/workstation setup time consumed for this operation, recorded in minutes. Maps to SAP PP activity type for setup (ISRST — Actual Setup Time). Used for capacity planning, OEE (Overall Equipment Effectiveness) calculation, and comparison against planned setup time from the routing.

Planned setup time for this operation as defined in the SAP PP routing, recorded in minutes. Provides the baseline for actual vs. planned setup time variance analysis. Sourced from the routing master data at the time of production order creation.

became.before: manufacturing.shift.shift_id

before.description: Reference to the production shift during which this confirmation was recorded. Enables shift-level production output analysis, yield comparison across shifts, and workforce productivity reporting.

SAP storage location (LGORT) to which the confirmed yield quantity is posted as a goods receipt. Identifies the physical inventory location within the plant (e.g., finished goods area, WIP buffer, sequencing area). Required for inventory management and JIS (Just-in-Sequence) delivery coordination.

Actual takt time achieved for this production confirmation, expressed in seconds per unit. Calculated as total operation time divided by yield quantity. Used for production line balancing, bottleneck identification, and comparison against the planned takt time to assess line efficiency. Key metric in JIS (Just-in-Sequence) production management.

Actual teardown/cleanup time consumed after the production operation, recorded in minutes. Maps to SAP PP activity type for teardown. Included in total operation time for accurate takt time and capacity utilization calculations. Relevant for paint booth cleaning, tooling changeover, and AGV (Automated Guided Vehicle) repositioning cycles.

17-character Vehicle Identification Number assigned to the vehicle unit confirmed in this production record. Populated for final assembly confirmations where a specific vehicle unit is produced. Null for sub-assembly or component-level confirmations. Enables full build traceability from production confirmation to vehicle delivery.

Indicates the assembly kit type this line is configured to process: CKD (Completely Knocked Down — full kit assembly from parts), SKD (Semi Knocked Down — partial pre-assembly), CBU (Completely Built Up — no kit assembly, line-off only), or multi (capable of multiple kit types). Relevant for export assembly plants and regulatory homologation.

Current IATF 16949 (International Automotive Task Force) quality management system audit status for this production line: compliant (no non-conformances), minor_nc (minor non-conformance identified), major_nc (major non-conformance — corrective action required), suspended (production suspended pending corrective action), or not_audited (not yet subject to IATF audit).

Date of the most recent IATF 16949 quality management system audit conducted on this production line. Used for audit cycle management, corrective action tracking, and regulatory compliance reporting to OEM customers and certification bodies.

became.before: workforce.employee.employee_id

before.description: Employee identifier of the production line manager or area manager responsible for this line's operations, quality, and safety performance. References the SuccessFactors HR system employee record. Used for accountability assignment, escalation routing, and workforce reporting.

Type of paint application system used on this line (applicable to paint shop lines): waterborne (water-based paint — lower VOC emissions), solventborne (solvent-based paint), powder_coat (electrostatic powder coating), or none (non-paint line). Drives EPA/CARB VOC (Volatile Organic Compound) emissions compliance reporting and environmental permit management.

Identifier or name of the PLC (Programmable Logic Controller) system or network controlling this production line's automated equipment (e.g., 'Siemens S7-1500 Network A', 'Allen-Bradley ControlLogix Zone 3'). Used for maintenance management in SAP PM, SCADA integration, and cybersecurity asset inventory.

became.before: manufacturing.work_center.work_center_id

before.description: The SAP S/4HANA PP (Production Planning) work center identifier corresponding to this production line. Enables direct linkage between the lakehouse production_line master and SAP production orders, capacity planning, and cost center assignments in SAP CO (Controlling).

Identifier or name of the SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition) system monitoring and controlling this production line (e.g., 'Ignition SCADA Plant2-Zone1', 'Wonderware InTouch Line FA-01'). Used for real-time production monitoring, alarm management, and integration with MES and ERP systems.

Current shift schedule configuration for the production line, indicating the number of operating shifts per day: 1_shift (single day shift), 2_shift (day and afternoon), 3_shift (continuous 24-hour), or 4_shift_rotating (rotating continental schedule). Drives capacity planning, workforce scheduling in SuccessFactors, and MRP calculations in SAP PP.

Identifies the operational system of record from which this production line master record was sourced: SAP_PP (SAP S/4HANA Production Planning), Apriso_MES (Apriso/Dassault Manufacturing Execution System), Teamcenter (Siemens Teamcenter PLM), Manual (manually entered), or SCADA (derived from SCADA system configuration). Used for data lineage and reconciliation.

The Just-in-Sequence (JIS) sequence number assigned to this production order, defining its position in the assembly line build sequence. Critical for JIS supply chain synchronization — ensures parts arrive at the line in the exact order vehicles are built. Managed by MES and communicated to tier-1 suppliers.

became.before: workforce.employee.employee_id

before.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: REQUIRED: Order creation audit requires tracking planner employee; essential for traceability and compliance.

became.before: customer.party.party_id

before.description: Foreign key linking to customer.party. Business justification: Order‑to‑customer linkage required for order fulfillment, warranty, and recall reports; manufacturers need to know which party placed each production order.

became.before: compliance.homologation_record.homologation_record_id

before.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.homologation_record. Business justification: Production Order release process checks Homologation_Record to ensure model/year has regulatory approval before manufacturing starts.

became.before: mobility.mobility_fleet_account.mobility_fleet_account_id

before.description: Foreign key linking to mobility.mobility_fleet_account. Business justification: Required for fleet sales processing: link production order to the purchasing fleet account for order tracking, invoicing, and delivery coordination.

became.before: sales.opportunity.opportunity_id

before.description: Foreign key linking to sales.opportunity. Business justification: Supports Opportunity‑to‑Production conversion analysis; ties each production order back to the sales opportunity that generated it.

became.before: procurement.procurement_supplier.procurement_supplier_id

before.description: Foreign key linking to procurement.supplier. Business justification: Enables Production Order Supplier Impact Analysis, identifying the primary supplier for critical components.

The SAP QM (Quality Management) inspection lot number created for quality inspection activities associated with this production order. Links production execution to quality results, usage decisions, and non-conformance records. Maps to SAP QM inspection lot (QMNUM).

became.before: sales.quote.quote_id

before.description: Foreign key linking to sales.quote. Business justification: Provides Quote‑to‑Production traceability for financial and compliance reporting; links the quote that was accepted to the resulting production order.

became.before: supply.supply_purchase_order.supply_purchase_order_id

before.description: Foreign key linking to supply.supply_purchase_order. Business justification: Production scheduling aligns each production order with its originating purchase order to ensure material availability and OTD compliance.
Unique identifier for the allocation instance

became.before: dealer.dealership.dealership_id

before.description: Foreign key linking to the dealership
Priority tier assigned to the allocation for fulfillment sequencing
Name or employee identifier of the production planning manager who formally approved this schedule version for release to the shop floor. Required for IATF 16949 document control and audit trail.
Timestamp when the production schedule was formally approved for release. Marks the transition from 'draft' to 'released' status and triggers supplier call-off generation.

Manufacturing process stage covered by this schedule record. Reflects the major shop areas in automotive assembly: stamping (metal forming), body shop (welding/joining), paint (surface treatment), final assembly (powertrain/trim installation), or trim-chassis-final (TCF integrated line).
Total available production capacity in hours for this schedule period on the assigned production line, accounting for planned downtime, maintenance windows, and shift patterns.
Body style classification of the vehicles scheduled for production. Used for production line configuration, tooling setup, and capacity planning by body type.

Ending sequence number for the JIS (Just-in-Sequence) build order within this schedule period. Together with build_sequence_start defines the range of vehicle sequence numbers assigned to this schedule.

Starting sequence number for the JIS (Just-in-Sequence) build order within this schedule period. Used by MES and AGV systems to sequence vehicle bodies through the production line in the correct order.

Classification of the production build type. 'standard' = full series production; 'ckd' = Completely Knocked Down (CKD) kit assembly; 'skd' = Semi Knocked Down (SKD) assembly; 'pilot' = pre-production pilot build; 'pre_series' = pre-series validation build.
Timestamp when supplier delivery call-offs were transmitted to the supply base for this production schedule. Used for OTD (On-Time Delivery) tracking and supplier performance measurement.
Official End of Production (EOP) date for the vehicle model/model year. Schedules beyond this date are invalid. Used for phase-out planning, last-time-buy procurement, and regulatory deregistration.

Fiscal period (month number 1-12 or 1-16 for special periods) within the fiscal year. Enables alignment of production volumes with financial reporting periods for management accounting and EBITDA analysis.
Fiscal year (FY) to which this production schedule belongs. Used for financial planning, CapEx allocation, and EBITDA reporting alignment between production volumes and financial periods.

became.before: billing.run.run_id

before.description: Reference to the SAP MRP (Material Requirements Planning) run that generated or last updated this production schedule. Enables traceability of schedule origin and supports re-planning analysis.

became.before: aftersales.nameplate.nameplate_id

before.description: Foreign key linking to product.nameplate. Business justification: REQUIRED: Production schedules are often filtered by nameplate; nameplate‑level planning dashboards need this FK.

ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code for the primary regulatory market for which these vehicles are being produced. Determines applicable homologation standards (NHTSA/FMVSS for USA, UNECE for Europe, etc.), emissions certification (EPA, CARB, Euro 6), and CAFE compliance tracking. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: USA|CAN|MEX|DEU|GBR|CHN|JPN|KOR|AUS|BRA — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

Business reason code or description for the most recent schedule revision. Examples: material shortage, capacity constraint, demand change, quality hold, tooling failure, model mix adjustment. Required for change control audit trail per IATF 16949.

Free-text field for production planners to record contextual notes, exceptions, or special instructions associated with this schedule record. Examples: tooling changeover notes, quality hold references, special customer order constraints.
Precise timestamp when production is scheduled to complete for this schedule record. Used for shift planning, takt time validation, and downstream logistics coordination.
Precise timestamp when production is scheduled to begin on the line for this schedule record. Used for JIS (Just-in-Sequence) sequencing, AGV routing, and supplier call-off timing.

Official Start of Production (SOP) date for the vehicle model/model year being scheduled. Marks the formal launch of series production. Used to validate that schedule dates fall within the active production window.

Boolean flag indicating whether supplier delivery call-offs (JIT/JIS delivery schedules) have been generated and transmitted to suppliers based on this production schedule. True = call-offs sent; False = pending call-off generation.

became.before: vehicle.model.model_id

before.description: Reference to the vehicle model (e.g., sedan, SUV, truck, EV) being scheduled for production. Links to the vehicle master product record.

SAE J3016 automation level of the ADAS (Advanced Driver Assistance Systems) suite fitted to this production variant: L0 (no automation), L1 (driver assistance), L2 (partial automation), L2_PLUS (enhanced partial automation), L3 (conditional automation). Drives ECU (Electronic Control Unit) software configuration, OTA (Over-the-Air Update) eligibility, and UNECE UN R157 regulatory compliance.

Numeric score (1–10) representing the relative assembly complexity of this production variant compared to the base variant on the same production line. Higher scores indicate more assembly operations, longer cycle times, or specialized tooling requirements. Used for JIS (Just-in-Sequence) sequencing optimization to balance line loading and avoid consecutive high-complexity builds.

Usable battery pack capacity in kilowatt-hours (kWh) for BEV, PHEV, and HEV variants. Null for pure ICE variants. Drives assembly sequencing for battery marriage station, WLTP (Worldwide Harmonised Light Vehicles Test Procedure) range certification, and EPA electric range labelling.

Standardized code identifying the vehicle body configuration for this production variant (e.g., SEDAN, SUV, TRUCK, COUPE, HATCHBACK, MINIVAN). Determines stamping die sets, body shop tooling, and paint booth configuration requirements. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: SEDAN|SUV|TRUCK|COUPE|HATCHBACK|MINIVAN|CONVERTIBLE|WAGON|VAN|CROSSOVER — promote to reference product]

Certified CO2 tailpipe emission in grams per kilometre (g/km) under WLTP or NEDC test cycle for this production variant. Used for EU CO2 fleet average compliance (Regulation (EU) 2019/631), CAFE (Corporate Average Fuel Economy) calculations, and vehicle taxation band classification in destination markets.

Three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code identifying the primary market for which this production variant is homologated and destined (e.g., 'USA', 'DEU', 'JPN'). Governs regulatory compliance requirements (NHTSA FMVSS, Euro NCAP, UNECE), emission standards, and right-hand vs left-hand drive configuration.

Drivetrain configuration specifying which axles receive motive power: FWD (Front-Wheel Drive), RWD (Rear-Wheel Drive), AWD (All-Wheel Drive), or 4WD (Four-Wheel Drive). Determines chassis assembly routing, driveshaft fitment, and NVH (Noise Vibration Harshness) validation requirements.

Total engine displacement in cubic centimetres (cc) for ICE (Internal Combustion Engine) and HEV/PHEV variants. Null for BEV and FCEV variants. Used for regulatory classification under EPA, CARB, and UNECE emissions standards, and for CAFE (Corporate Average Fuel Economy) fleet averaging calculations.

Current engineering change revision level for this production variant as managed in Siemens Teamcenter PLM or PTC Windchill (e.g., 'A', 'B', 'C1', 'REV3'). Tracks design maturity and ensures the correct BOM (Bill of Materials) version is applied during production. Incremented upon each approved engineering change notice (ECN).

Date on which this production variant is scheduled to cease production (EOP — End of Production). Drives last-order scheduling, tooling decommissioning planning, and spare parts provisioning for after-sales service obligations.

EPA-certified combined fuel economy in miles per gallon (MPG) for ICE, HEV, and PHEV variants in NAFTA markets. Null for BEV/FCEV variants. Used for CAFE (Corporate Average Fuel Economy) fleet compliance reporting to EPA and consumer window sticker labelling under 49 CFR Part 575.

Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) in kilograms for this production variant. Used for regulatory classification under DOT FMVSS, UNECE weight regulations, and CAFE (Corporate Average Fuel Economy) fleet averaging. Also drives chassis assembly torque specifications and suspension tuning parameters.

Steering wheel position for this production variant: LHD (Left-Hand Drive) for markets such as USA, Germany; RHD (Right-Hand Drive) for markets such as UK, Japan, Australia. Determines instrument panel assembly variant, steering column routing, and body shop tooling configuration.

became.before: compliance.homologation_record.homologation_record_id

before.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.homologation_record. Business justification: Variant definitions are approved via homologation; linking ensures variant builds only when approved.

Regulatory type-approval and homologation status for this production variant in the target destination market: PENDING (application submitted), CERTIFIED (full approval granted), CONDITIONAL (provisional approval with conditions), EXPIRED (certification lapsed), NOT_REQUIRED. Governs whether the variant can be legally sold in the destination market.

Indicates whether this production variant can be produced as a CKD (Completely Knocked Down) kit for assembly at an overseas plant (True = CKD eligible). Drives export documentation, customs tariff classification, and overseas plant BOM (Bill of Materials) configuration in SAP MM.

Indicates whether this production variant is eligible for JIS (Just-in-Sequence) supplier call-off sequencing (True = JIS eligible). JIS-eligible variants require sequenced component delivery synchronized to the build sequence, impacting supplier logistics contracts and MES call-off trigger configuration.

Indicates whether this production variant has been validated as feasible for assembly on the assigned production line (True = compatible, False = not compatible). Serves as the primary gate flag in MES (Manufacturing Execution System) build sequence feasibility validation and JIS (Just-in-Sequence) call-off authorization.

Indicates whether this production variant supports OTA (Over-the-Air) software updates for ECU (Electronic Control Unit) and infotainment systems (True = OTA capable). Drives connected vehicle service provisioning in Geotab/Bosch IoT platform and UNECE UN R156 software update regulatory compliance.

Maximum number of consecutive units of this production variant that can be scheduled back-to-back in the build sequence without violating line balancing or ergonomic constraints. Enforced by MES (Manufacturing Execution System) JIS (Just-in-Sequence) sequencing rules to prevent operator fatigue and tooling overload.

Cross-reference identifier for this production variant in the Apriso/Dassault MES (Manufacturing Execution System). Used for real-time build sequence call-off, WIP (Work in Progress) tracking, and quality gate routing on the shop floor.

became.before: vehicle.model.model_id

before.description: Foreign key linking to vehicle.model. Business justification: Variant Definition Process links each variant to its vehicle model for configuration management and regulatory compliance.

Overall NCAP (New Car Assessment Programme) safety star rating achieved by this production variant (1 to 5 stars, or NOT_RATED if not yet assessed). Applicable to Euro NCAP, NHTSA NCAP, or ANCAP depending on destination market. Used for regulatory compliance reporting and marketing communications.

Code identifying the bundled option package associated with this production variant (e.g., 'TECH_PKG', 'SAFETY_PKG', 'LUXURY_PKG'). Maps to a specific set of BOM (Bill of Materials) components and assembly operations in Siemens Teamcenter PLM and SAP PP configurable material management.

Classification of the paint application process required for this production variant: STANDARD (solid colour), METALLIC, PEARL, MATTE, or TWO_TONE. Determines paint booth routing, cure cycle parameters, and paint material BOM (Bill of Materials) components in the body shop and paint shop assembly stages.

became.before: manufacturing.plant.plant_id

before.description: Reference to the manufacturing plant where this production variant is authorized to be built. Determines line compatibility, tooling availability, and regulatory homologation scope.

Current PPAP (Production Part Approval Process) approval status for this production variant. PPAP approval is a mandatory quality gate before SOP (Start of Production) under IATF 16949. Status values: NOT_REQUIRED, PENDING, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED. Drives production release authorization in MES.

became.before: manufacturing.production_bom.production_bom_id

before.description: Reference to the manufacturing BOM (Bill of Materials) version applicable to this production variant. Links to the BOM master in Siemens Teamcenter PLM or SAP MM (Materials Management) to resolve component lists for production planning and MRP (Material Requirements Planning) execution.

became.before: billing.rebate_agreement.rebate_agreement_id

before.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the production variant record. Primary key for the manufacturing-feasible variant definition. Role: MASTER_RESOURCE.

Regulatory compliance region grouping for this production variant, used to apply the correct homologation ruleset: NAFTA (North America), EU (European Union), APAC (Asia-Pacific), LATAM (Latin America), MEA (Middle East & Africa), CHINA. Determines applicable NCAP (New Car Assessment Programme) standards, emissions regulations, and safety certification requirements.

became.before: manufacturing.routing.routing_id

before.description: Reference to the manufacturing routing (operation sequence) applicable to this production variant in SAP PP (Production Planning). Defines the sequence of work centers, operations, and standard times required to build this variant from stamping through final assembly.

SAP S/4HANA material master number (MM module) corresponding to this production variant's configurable material (KMAT). Used for MRP (Material Requirements Planning), production order creation in SAP PP, and cost object controlling in SAP CO.

Date on which this production variant is authorized to enter volume production (SOP — Start of Production). Used for production planning gate reviews, PPAP (Production Part Approval Process) milestone tracking, and supplier readiness confirmation.

Standard labor hours required to complete the full assembly of this production variant from stamping through final assembly and PDI (Pre-Delivery Inspection). Used for production cost standard setting, workforce planning, and SAP CO (Controlling) cost object calculation.

Cross-reference identifier for this production variant in Siemens Teamcenter PLM (Product Lifecycle Management) variant configuration module. Enables traceability between the manufacturing master data record and the engineering variant definition in the PLM system of record.

Type of transmission fitted in this production variant: AUTOMATIC (conventional automatic), MANUAL (manual gearbox), CVT (Continuously Variable Transmission), DCT (Dual-Clutch Transmission), or SINGLE_SPEED (for BEV/FCEV). Drives assembly routing to the correct powertrain marriage station and torque tooling specification.

Alphanumeric code identifying the equipment and feature trim level for this variant (e.g., 'BASE', 'XLE', 'PLATINUM', 'SPORT'). Determines option package applicability, BOM (Bill of Materials) component selection, and MSRP (Manufacturer Suggested Retail Price) tier in the commercial catalog.

Indicates whether this production variant is equipped with V2X (Vehicle-to-Everything) communication hardware (True = V2X capable). Drives telematics module assembly sequencing, spectrum licensing compliance, and connected mobility service activation in Geotab/Bosch IoT platform.

OEM (Original Equipment Manufacturer) internal model code identifying the vehicle platform or nameplate (e.g., 'F150', 'RAV4', 'MODEL3'). Links the production variant to the vehicle program in PLM (Product Lifecycle Management) and SAP MM (Materials Management).

Official WLTP (Worldwide Harmonised Light Vehicles Test Procedure) certified driving range in kilometres for BEV and PHEV variants. Null for ICE and HEV variants. Used for EU regulatory labelling, EPA range certification cross-reference, and consumer-facing range claims.

Code representing the specific assembly stage or station within the production line where the nonconformance was detected (e.g., body framing, paint primer, trim line, chassis marriage). Supports JIS (Just-in-Sequence) traceability.
The BOM (Bill of Materials) component or part number of the specific sub-assembly or component requiring rework. References the engineering BOM managed in Siemens Teamcenter or SAP MM.
Reference number or identifier of the corrective action (CAR) or 8D problem-solving report raised in response to this rework event. Links the rework order to the formal quality improvement process.

Standardized code identifying the physical location or zone on the vehicle or sub-assembly where the defect was found (e.g., body zone, paint zone, chassis area). Used for spatial defect analysis and NVH (Noise Vibration Harshness) correlation.

Code indicating the method by which the defect was detected prior to rework order creation (e.g., visual inspection, automated gauge check, functional test, quality audit, customer feedback). Supports FMEA (Failure Mode and Effects Analysis) detection ranking analysis.

Date and time when the nonconformance was originally detected during in-process quality inspection, triggering the creation of this rework order. The principal business event timestamp for this transaction.

Final disposition decision for the nonconforming unit after rework evaluation. Repaired indicates successful correction; scrapped indicates the unit is unrecoverable; concession (use-as-is) indicates acceptance of the nonconformance with documented deviation; return to supplier applies to purchased components.

Code identifying the specific quality inspection checkpoint or gate (e.g., body-in-white audit, paint final audit, end-of-line check) at which the defect was detected and the rework order was initiated.

Indicates whether the vehicle or sub-assembly is placed on a regulatory hold pending rework completion and re-inspection. A regulatory hold prevents the unit from advancing to the next production stage or shipping.
Indicates whether this rework event caused a production line stoppage (Andon pull or line stop). Used for OEE (Overall Equipment Effectiveness) impact analysis and production downtime reporting.
The vehicle model year (MY) of the unit undergoing rework. Used for regulatory compliance reporting, warranty analysis, and production quality trending by model year.
Code identifying the specific production line (e.g., stamping, body shop, paint, final assembly) where the defect was originally detected and the rework order was raised.

Document number or reference to the approved rework instruction, repair standard, or Technical Service Bulletin (TSB) that governs the rework procedure. Ensures traceability to authorized repair methods.

Total internal labor cost incurred for the rework operation, calculated from actual rework hours and the applicable labor rate. Expressed in the plant's operating currency. Used for quality cost (Cost of Poor Quality - COPQ) reporting.

Cost of replacement parts and materials consumed during the rework operation. Sourced from SAP MM goods issue postings against the rework order. Contributes to total Cost of Poor Quality (COPQ) calculation.
Current lifecycle status of the rework order within the shop floor execution workflow. Tracks progression from creation through completion or cancellation as managed in MES or SAP QM.

Standardized code classifying the root cause of the defect as determined through root cause analysis (e.g., 5-Why, Ishikawa). Populated upon rework completion. Supports FMEA (Failure Mode and Effects Analysis) and SPC (Statistical Process Control) improvement actions.
Number of components or sub-assemblies scrapped as a result of this rework order where repair was not feasible. Used for PPM (Parts Per Million) defect rate calculation and scrap cost reporting.

Code identifying the operational system of record from which this rework order record was sourced (e.g., SAP QM, Apriso/Dassault MES, or manual entry). Supports data lineage and Silver Layer ingestion traceability.
Internal product/model code identifying the vehicle nameplate or platform (e.g., truck, SUV, EV, HEV) associated with the rework order. Aligns with PLM product structure in Siemens Teamcenter.

17-character Vehicle Identification Number (VIN) of the vehicle or vehicle body on which rework is being performed. Nullable for sub-assembly rework not yet associated with a VIN. Conforms to ISO 3779 standard.

became.before: manufacturing.routing.routing_id

before.description: Self-referencing FK on routing (alternate_routing_id)
User identifier who approved the routing change.
Date when the routing change was formally approved.
Business reason for the most recent change to the routing.
Applicable industry or internal compliance standard (e.g., ISO/TS 16949).
User identifier who originally created the routing.
Free‑form description of the routing purpose, scope and special instructions.
Date when the routing is retired or superseded; null if open‑ended.
Date when the routing becomes valid for production planning.

Informs CapEx planning and Industry 4.0 transformation roadmap.
fully_automated|highly_automated|semi_automated|manual|collaborative
Total available production hours per day for this work center, accounting for planned shift schedules and scheduled breaks. Used in SAP PP capacity requirements planning (CRP) and MES scheduling.

Capacity classification of the work center: bottleneck (constraining throughput of the line), standard (normal capacity), buffer (excess capacity used to absorb variation), or flexible (can be redeployed across lines). Critical for Theory of Constraints analysis and production scheduling.
bottleneck|standard|buffer|flexible
Date on which this work center was officially commissioned and made available for production use. Used for asset age tracking, depreciation calculation, and maintenance lifecycle management.

Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Work‑center cost tracking for OEE and labor cost reporting uses a finance cost center; replacing cost_center_code with cost_center_id is standard practice.
Timestamp when this work center master record was first created in the data platform. Used for data lineage, audit trail, and record lifecycle management.
ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the cost rates (machine_rate_per_hour, labor_rate_per_hour) associated with this work center (e.g., USD, EUR, JPY).

Standard cycle time in seconds for this work center to complete one unit of work. Used in production scheduling, capacity calculation, and bottleneck analysis. Represents the designed throughput rate per station.

Date on which this work center was or is planned to be permanently decommissioned and removed from production service. Nullable for active stations. Used for asset lifecycle planning and capacity forecasting.

Identifier of the production supervisor or team leader responsible for this work center. Used for accountability tracking, escalation routing, and workforce management integration with SuccessFactors.

Rated energy consumption of this work center in kilowatts (kW) under standard operating conditions. Used for energy management, sustainability reporting, and ISO 14001 environmental compliance tracking.
Physical floor area occupied by this work center in square meters. Used for facility layout planning, ergonomic assessments, and plant capacity management.

Foreign key linking to asset.functional_location. Business justification: Required for Work Center Maintenance Planning reports linking each work center to its functional location in the plant hierarchy.

Indicates whether this work center has been identified as a production bottleneck constraining overall line throughput. Bottleneck stations receive priority in capacity planning, maintenance scheduling, and continuous improvement initiatives.

Indicates whether this work center participates in JIS (Just-in-Sequence) production sequencing. When true, the MES enforces strict vehicle sequence delivery to this station to support mixed-model assembly.

Indicates whether this work center serves as a quality gate (inspection checkpoint) in the production flow. Quality gate stations require SPC (Statistical Process Control) data capture and may hold WIP pending quality approval.
DECIMAL(10,2)
confidential
Standard direct labor cost rate per hour (in local currency) for this work center. Used in production order costing, standard cost roll-up, and labor efficiency variance reporting.
Date of the most recent calibration or measurement system verification performed on this work center's tooling and gauges. Required for IATF 16949 Clause 7.1.5 measurement system compliance.
Timestamp of the most recent update to this work center master record. Used for change tracking, data freshness monitoring, and incremental ETL processing in the Databricks lakehouse.
Textual description of the physical location of the work center within the plant (e.g., 'Building A, Bay 3, Row 5'). Supports maintenance routing, safety inspections, and shop floor navigation.
DECIMAL(10,2)
confidential
Standard machine cost rate per hour (in local currency) for this work center, used in production order costing, standard cost calculation, and variance analysis in SAP CO.

Maintenance strategy applied to this work center: preventive (scheduled interval-based), predictive (condition-monitoring-based), corrective (repair after failure), or condition_based (triggered by sensor thresholds). Drives SAP PM maintenance planning.
preventive|predictive|corrective|condition_based

Standard mean time between failures (MTBF) in hours for this work center, representing the expected average operational time between unplanned breakdowns. Used in reliability analysis, maintenance planning, and OEE (Overall Equipment Effectiveness) benchmarking.

Standard mean time to repair (MTTR) in hours for this work center, representing the average time required to restore the station to operational status after a failure. Used in maintenance planning and availability calculations.

Native work center identifier in the Apriso/Dassault MES system. Used for cross-system traceability between the lakehouse silver layer and the operational MES for shop floor execution and WIP (Work in Progress) tracking.
Scheduled date for the next calibration or measurement system verification at this work center. Triggers maintenance work orders in SAP PM and quality alerts in the MES when approaching or overdue.
Number of production shifts per day this work center operates (typically 1, 2, or 3). Used in daily capacity calculation and workforce planning.
Standard number of direct labor workers assigned to this work center per shift. Used for workforce planning, labor cost allocation, and ergonomic assessment.
DECIMAL(6,3)
confidential
Manufacturing overhead absorption rate as a percentage applied to this work center's direct costs for product costing and standard cost calculation in SAP CO.
SAP plant code identifying the manufacturing facility where this work center is physically located. Aligns with SAP S/4HANA organizational structure for production planning.

Identifier of the PLC (Programmable Logic Controller) node associated with this work center in the shop floor control network. Used for real-time production control integration and SCADA data correlation.

Manufacturing process category to which this work center belongs, reflecting the major shop segment (e.g., stamping, body shop, paint, final assembly, powertrain). Used for shop floor segmentation, capacity analysis, and APQP (Advanced Product Quality Planning) alignment. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: stamping|body_shop|paint|final_assembly|powertrain|chassis|trim|quality_inspection|logistics — promote to reference product]
Code identifying the production line (e.g., stamping, body shop, paint, final assembly) to which this work center belongs. Supports JIS (Just-in-Sequence) scheduling and MES line-level reporting.
Native work center identifier in SAP S/4HANA PP module. Used for cross-system reconciliation between the lakehouse and SAP for production order routing, capacity planning, and cost center allocation.

Identifier of the SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition) node associated with this work center. Enables real-time monitoring, alarm management, and production data acquisition from the shop floor.
Standard setup/changeover time in minutes required to prepare this work center for a new production run or model variant. Used in SAP PP capacity planning and MES work order scheduling.

Code referencing the shift schedule model assigned to this work center (e.g., 1-shift, 2-shift, 3-shift, weekend shift). Determines available production windows for capacity planning and MES scheduling.

SAP PP standard value key (e.g., SAP1, SAP2) defining which standard values (setup, machine, labor, teardown times) are relevant for this work center in routing operations. Governs how production order times are calculated.

Takt time in seconds representing the rate at which vehicles must be produced to meet customer demand. Calculated as available production time divided by customer demand rate. Used for JIS (Just-in-Sequence) line balancing and MES pacing.
Standard teardown/cleanup time in minutes required after completing a production run at this work center. Included in total station time calculations for capacity planning.

SAP PP work center category classifying the primary resource type: machine (machine-driven capacity), labor (labor-driven capacity), machine_labor (both machine and labor capacity), or external (subcontracted operation). Determines how capacity and costing are calculated in SAP.
machine|labor|machine_labor|external

Externally-known alphanumeric code that uniquely identifies the work center across MES, SAP PP, and SCADA systems. Used as the business key in cross-system integration (e.g., Apriso/Dassault MES work center identifier).
Detailed textual description of the work center's function, scope of operations, and any special capabilities or constraints relevant to production planning and scheduling.
Unique surrogate identifier for the work center (station) record within the manufacturing data platform. Primary key for the work_center master entity.
Human-readable name of the work center station (e.g., 'Body Framing Station 04', 'Final Torque Assembly Line 2'). Used in shop floor displays, MES dashboards, and production reporting.

Current lifecycle status of the work center: active (in production use), inactive (temporarily not in use), under_maintenance (scheduled or unscheduled maintenance), decommissioned (permanently retired), or planned (not yet commissioned). Drives MES scheduling eligibility and capacity planning.
active|inactive|under_maintenance|decommissioned|planned

Classification of the work center by its operational mode: manual (human-operated), automated (machine-driven without robotics), robotic (robot arm/AGV-integrated), semi_automated (human-assisted automation), inspection (quality gate), or rework (defect correction station). Drives capacity planning and labor allocation.
manual|automated|robotic|semi_automated|inspection|rework

Body shop specific process parameters including weld current, weld time, adhesive application, hemming force, and dimensional measurements per station and vehicle.
Cycle time tracking per station recording actual vs planned cycle times for each vehicle passing through each work center, enabling bottleneck analysis and line balancing.
Energy consumption tracking per production line and plant for ESG reporting, recording electricity, gas, water, and compressed air usage with CO2 equivalent calculations.
Packaging specifications for parts and components used in manufacturing logistics (container types, dimensions)
Pre-aggregated Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) metrics per production line, work center, and shift, decomposed into availability, performance, and quality components.
Pre-aggregated Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) metrics per plant/line/work-center/shift for analytics readiness.
Paint shop specific process parameters including booth temperature, humidity, film thickness, color coat application settings, and cure oven profiles tracked per vehicle and station.
Operator assignments per station tracking which operators are assigned to which work centers/stations per shift, including qualification verification and rotation schedules.
MES work instructions per station defining the step-by-step operations, tools required, quality checks, and safety precautions for each assembly or process station.

Supports real-time material flow visibility and AGV fleet utilization reporting.
affected_objects.after: Automated Guided Vehicle movement events tracking material transport on the shop floor

Master reference table for agv_route. Referenced by route_id.
affected_objects.after: AGV route definitions within a plant including waypoints, speed limits, and priority zones

affected_objects.before: supply_management

JIS (Just-in-Sequence) build sequence record defining the ordered sequence of vehicles to be assembled on a production line for a given shift or production run. Captures sequence number, planned build date, shift, line assignment, vehicle configuration reference (model, trim, powertrain, color), sequence status, and freeze timestamp. Critical for JIS supplier call-offs and AGV routing. Sourced from Apriso MES sequencing module.
affected_objects.after: Vehicle build sequence defining the order of vehicles on the production line with configuration and scheduling details

affected_objects.before: production_execution

Reference master defining the standard build stages in the vehicle manufacturing process (e.g., Stamping, Body Shop, E-Coat, Paint, Trim-1, Chassis, Trim-2, Final, PDI). affected_objects.after: Manufacturing build stage definitions (body shop, paint, trim, final assembly) with process parameters

affected_objects.before: production_execution

Master record for plant and line capacity planning, capturing planned production capacity by plant, production line, shift pattern, and planning period (weekly/monthly). Includes rated capacity (JPH × available hours), demonstrated capacity, capacity utilization percentage, bottleneck work center, planned overtime hours, and capacity plan version. Supports S&OP (Sales and Operations Planning) and capital investment decisions.
affected_objects.after: Production capacity planning records for lines and plants with demand vs available capacity

affected_objects.before: Transactional record for production line changeover events when switching between vehicle models, body styles, or powertrain variants on a shared production line. Captures changeover type (model mix change, color change, tooling swap, line retooling), planned and actual changeover start/end times, duration, affected production line, changeover team, and production loss (units not produced). Supports SMED (Single-Minute Exchange of Die) improvement programs.
affected_objects.after: Production line changeover events when switching between vehicle models or variants

affected_objects.before: production_execution

This association product records the compliance certification of a production order against a specific regulatory requirement. It captures the compliance status, supporting evidence document path, and the date the certification was achieved for each order‑requirement pair.. Existence Justification: Each production order must be verified against multiple regulatory requirements, and each regulatory requirement applies to many production orders. The compliance status, supporting evidence, and certification date are recorded for every order‑requirement pair, and quality engineers actively create, update, and delete these records as part of the manufacturing compliance process.
affected_objects.after: Manufacturing compliance certifications (ISO, IATF, environmental) for plants and production lines

affected_objects.before: quality_assurance

Transactional record capturing unplanned and planned production downtime events at the work center or line level. Tracks downtime start and end timestamps, duration (minutes), downtime category (mechanical failure, tooling change, material shortage, quality hold, scheduled maintenance, changeover), affected work center, production order impact, and responsible team. Critical for OEE analysis and SCADA-integrated downtime reporting.
affected_objects.after: Production line and equipment downtime events with root cause, duration, and OEE impact

affected_objects.before: production_execution
Master reference table for factory_calendar. Referenced by factory_calendar_id.
affected_objects.after: Factory calendar defining working days, holidays, shutdown periods, and special production days

affected_objects.before: Line-item record within a manufacturing BOM representing a single component or sub-assembly required to build a vehicle. Captures component part number, description, quantity per vehicle, unit of measure, installation work center, installation sequence, alternative part references, effectivity start/end dates, and scrap factor. Supports JIT/JIS material call-offs and shop floor assembly instructions.
affected_objects.after: Individual component line items within a production BOM with quantities, effectivity, and sourcing details

affected_objects.before: supply_management

Represents the contractual agreement between a manufacturing plant and a supplier. Each record captures the specific terms that apply to that plant‑supplier pair, such as lead time, minimum order quantity, pricing, and quality requirements.. Existence Justification: Each manufacturing plant can source materials from multiple suppliers, and each supplier can serve multiple plants. The business manages these plant‑supplier links through contracts that capture lead times, minimum order quantities, pricing, and other terms. The relationship is actively created, updated, and tracked as a distinct agreement.
affected_objects.after: Supply agreements between manufacturing plants and suppliers for JIT/JIS material delivery

affected_objects.before: supply_management

Transactional record tracking the usage of production tooling (dies, fixtures, jigs, welding guns, torque tools) against specific production orders and work centers. Captures tool ID, tool type, usage start and end timestamps, production order reference, work center, stroke count or cycle count, cumulative usage against tool life limit, and tool condition at usage. Supports predictive tooling maintenance and PPAP tooling traceability.
affected_objects.after: Tooling usage records tracking tool deployment, cycle counts, and wear on the manufacturing floor This product is the single source of truth (SSOT) for its concept in the ECM Lakehouse.

affected_objects.before: production_execution

Transactional record capturing actual material consumption (goods issue) against a production order on the shop floor. Tracks consumed part number, quantity consumed, unit of measure, consumption timestamp, work center, production order reference, storage location, batch number, and variance from planned BOM quantity. Feeds SAP MM goods movement and cost accounting for production variance reporting.
affected_objects.after: Material consumption postings against production orders tracking actual vs planned usage

affected_objects.before: production_execution
Master reference table for operator_team. Referenced by operator_team_id.
affected_objects.after: Operator team definitions for production line staffing and shift assignments

affected_objects.before: Master record for each manufacturing plant or assembly facility operated by Automotive. Captures plant identity, location, type (stamping, body shop, paint, final assembly, CKD/SKD), production capacity, SOP/EOP dates, plant code, and operational status. SSOT for plant-level identity referenced across MES, SAP PP, and logistics domains.
affected_objects.after: Manufacturing plant/facility master data including location, capacity, certifications and operational parameters

affected_objects.before: Transactional record capturing actual process parameter readings collected from PLC/SCADA systems during manufacturing operations. Includes parameter type (weld current, weld time, torque value, paint film thickness, oven temperature, press force, adhesive bead width), measured value, upper and lower control limits (UCL/LCL), pass/fail status, timestamp, work center, production order, and VIN reference. Supports SPC (Statistical Process Control) and IATF 16949 process monitoring requirements.
affected_objects.after: Manufacturing process parameters (torque, temperature, pressure, etc.) captured from PLC/SCADA systems

affected_objects.before: production_execution

Manufacturing Bill of Materials (BOM) record representing the production-level BOM used on the shop floor for a specific vehicle configuration and model year. Distinct from the engineering BOM (eBOM) in the engineering domain — this is the manufacturing BOM (mBOM) as released to production. Captures BOM header (vehicle model, MY, plant, effectivity dates), BOM status, and reference to the engineering change order that authorized it. Managed via SAP PP and Teamcenter PLM BOM transfer.
affected_objects.after: Production bill of materials (MBOM) derived from engineering BOM with plant-specific configurations

affected_objects.before: supply_management

Transactional record confirming the completion of a production order or a partial operation within a production order. Captures confirmation number, production order reference, confirmed quantity (yield and scrap), actual activity times (setup, machine, labor), confirmation timestamp, shift, work center, and operator. Triggers SAP PP order settlement and inventory goods receipt. SSOT for actual production output reporting.
affected_objects.after: Production order confirmations recording completed operations, quantities, and labor/machine hours

affected_objects.before: production_execution

Master record for each production line within a plant, including stamping lines, body shop lines, paint booths, and final assembly lines. Tracks line code, line type, designed throughput (JPH - Jobs Per Hour), current shift configuration, AGV integration flags, PLC/SCADA system references, and operational status. Owned by manufacturing as the SSOT for line-level capacity and configuration.
affected_objects.after: Assembly/production line master data including capacity, automation level, and MES integration

affected_objects.before: Core transactional record representing a manufacturing work order issued to produce a specific vehicle or sub-assembly. Captures order number, order type (vehicle build, sub-assembly, rework), planned and actual start/finish dates, target quantity, produced quantity, order status, priority, shift assignment, and MES order reference. Links to plant, production line, and vehicle configuration. SSOT for shop floor execution tracking in SAP PP and Apriso MES.
affected_objects.after: Production/manufacturing order for vehicle or component production with scheduling, costing, and status tracking

affected_objects.before: production_execution

Represents the allocation of a manufacturing production order to a dealership. Each record links one production order to one dealership and captures allocation-specific details such as allocation number, status, date, priority tier, and type.. Existence Justification: Production orders are work orders that generate vehicles, and the allocation process assigns portions of these orders to multiple dealerships for distribution. A single production order can be split across several dealerships, and each dealership receives many production orders over time. The allocation itself carries attributes such as allocation number, status, date, priority tier, and type, which are managed as a distinct business entity.
affected_objects.after: Allocation of production orders to specific lines, shifts, and time slots for scheduling optimization

affected_objects.before: quality_assurance

Master production schedule (MPS) record defining planned vehicle production volumes by plant, production line, model, MY (Model Year), and time period (daily, weekly, monthly). Captures scheduled quantity, confirmed quantity, schedule version, freeze horizon, schedule status, and MRP run reference. Integrates with SAP PP MRP and supports capacity planning and supplier call-off generation.
affected_objects.after: Production scheduling data including planned volumes, capacity utilization, and freeze horizons

affected_objects.before: Reference master defining the valid production variants (option combinations) that can be built on a specific production line for a given model year. Captures variant code, model, MY, powertrain type (ICE, HEV, PHEV, BEV), body style, trim level, market destination, and line compatibility flags. Supports build sequence feasibility validation and JIS sequencing rules. Distinct from the commercial product catalog — this is the manufacturing-feasible variant definition.
affected_objects.after: Production variant definitions representing buildable vehicle configurations on a production line

affected_objects.before: quality_assurance

Transactional record for rework or repair operations initiated on a vehicle or sub-assembly that failed an in-process quality check. Captures rework order number, originating production order, VIN reference, defect description, rework type (in-line repair, offline rework, teardown), assigned work center, planned and actual rework hours, rework status, and disposition (repaired, scrapped, concession). Integrates with quality domain defect records.
affected_objects.after: Rework orders for defective units requiring correction before proceeding in production

affected_objects.before: quality_assurance
Master reference table for routing. Referenced by routing_id.
affected_objects.after: Manufacturing routing definitions specifying the sequence of operations for producing a product

affected_objects.before: supply_management

Transactional record capturing scrapped materials, components, or vehicle units during the manufacturing process. Tracks scrap item (part number or VIN), scrap quantity, scrap reason code, scrap location (work center, process stage), production order reference, scrap value, disposal method, and authorization reference. Feeds SAP CO production variance accounting and quality PPM (Parts Per Million) defect rate reporting.
affected_objects.after: Scrap records for materials and components scrapped during production with reason codes and costs

affected_objects.before: production_execution

Reference master for production shift definitions at each plant and production line. Captures shift code, shift name (Day, Afternoon, Night, Weekend), planned start and end times, break schedule, planned production hours, and applicable plant and line assignments. Used for production order scheduling, OEE calculation, and workforce planning integration.
affected_objects.after: Shift definition and scheduling including break patterns, capacity targets, and OEE goals

affected_objects.before: Granular transactional record capturing real-time shop floor events generated by MES, PLC, and SCADA systems during production. Includes event type (station entry, station exit, torque confirmation, weld completion, paint cure, AGV arrival, hold trigger, alarm), event timestamp, work center, production order reference, VIN reference, operator ID, and event payload. Enables real-time production monitoring and OEE (Overall Equipment Effectiveness) calculation.
affected_objects.after: Real-time shop floor events from MES/SCADA including quality checks, machine events, and operator actions

affected_objects.before: production_execution

Transactional record capturing the actual build event for a single vehicle unit on the shop floor, from body-in-white through final assembly. Tracks VIN assignment, production order reference, actual start and completion timestamps per build stage (stamping, body shop, paint, trim, chassis, final), build status, shift, operator team, and any hold or rework flags. SSOT for vehicle-level build traceability and genealogy in the manufacturing domain.
affected_objects.after: Individual vehicle build record tracking the manufacturing lifecycle from body shop through final assembly

affected_objects.before: production_execution

Represents the contractual relationship between a vehicle build and a mobility service. Each record captures the period of subscription, billing details, status, and the service tier applicable to that vehicle.. Existence Justification: Each vehicle build can be subscribed to multiple mobility services (e.g., remote diagnostics, OTA updates) and each mobility service can be subscribed by many vehicle builds across the fleet. The subscription is an operational contract that is created, updated, and terminated by business users, and it carries its own attributes such as start/end dates, billing amount, and status.
affected_objects.after: Subscription-based vehicle production orders linking mobility service subscriptions to manufacturing

affected_objects.before: quality_assurance

Snapshot and movement record for Work-in-Progress (WIP) inventory on the shop floor. Tracks WIP item identity, associated VIN or sub-assembly ID, current location (work center, buffer zone, AGV carrier), quantity, WIP status (in-process, on-hold, awaiting inspection, scrapped), entry and exit timestamps per location, and production order reference. Supports real-time WIP visibility and JIT material flow management.
affected_objects.after: Work-in-progress inventory tracking parts and sub-assemblies on the production floor

affected_objects.before: production_execution

Master record for individual work centers (stations) within a production line. Captures work center code, name, type (manual, automated, robotic), cycle time standard, takt time, capacity category, shift availability, and associated PLC/SCADA node identifiers. Supports JIS sequencing and MES shop floor execution at the station level.
affected_objects.after: Work center master data representing individual manufacturing stations with capacity, cost rates, and equipment details

before.description: Identifier of the AGV fleet management controller or traffic management system (e.g., a specific SCADA or AGV supervisor node) that dispatched and managed this movement. Supports multi-controller fleet architectures and fault isolation.

The manufacturing assembly stage to which this AGV movement is associated (e.g., stamping, body shop, paint, trim, chassis, final assembly). Enables stage-level material flow analysis and supports multi-stage production traceability.
The average travel speed of the AGV in metres per second during this movement. Used to identify speed anomalies, assess compliance with shop floor speed limits, and support throughput optimization.

The AGV battery state of charge as a percentage at the time the movement task ended. Combined with battery_level_start_pct to calculate energy consumption per movement and model battery degradation over time.

The AGV battery state of charge as a percentage at the time the movement task began. Used for fleet energy management, charge scheduling optimization, and identifying movements that may have been impacted by low battery conditions.

The shop floor location code of the target delivery point for this AGV movement. Used to verify correct delivery to the intended assembly station or buffer zone and to support JIS (Just-in-Sequence) call-off validation.
Human-readable descriptive name of the destination location (e.g., 'Final Assembly Line 2 Station 14', 'Trim Shop Sequencing Buffer'). Supports operational dashboards and exception reporting.

The total distance in metres travelled by the AGV during this movement event, as reported by the AGV's odometry or navigation system. Used for fleet utilization reporting, energy consumption modelling, and route efficiency analysis.

before.description: The identifier of the shop floor operator or MES user who manually initiated, overrode, or acknowledged this AGV movement task. Null for fully automated movements with no human intervention. Supports operator accountability and manual override tracking.

The fault or exception code reported by the AGV or fleet controller during this movement (e.g., obstacle detected, navigation error, battery low, load sensor failure). Null if no fault occurred. Used for predictive maintenance, FMEA (Failure Mode and Effects Analysis), and fleet reliability reporting.
Human-readable description of the fault or exception that occurred during this movement. Provides operational context for maintenance technicians and MES operators beyond the structured fault_code.

The precise date and time when the fault or exception was detected during this AGV movement. Null if no fault occurred. Used for mean time between failures (MTBF) calculation and maintenance response time analysis.

Indicates whether this AGV movement was manually overridden or initiated by a human operator rather than being fully automated by the MES or AGV fleet controller (True = manual override, False = fully automated). Used for automation rate reporting and exception analysis.

Indicates whether this AGV movement was triggered by a JIS (Just-in-Sequence) call-off signal from the assembly line (True = JIS-triggered, False = standard replenishment or non-sequenced movement). Critical for sequencing compliance reporting and line-feed performance analysis.

The weight in kilograms of the load carried by the AGV during this movement, as measured by the AGV's onboard load sensor. Used for payload compliance monitoring, energy consumption analysis, and overload fault detection.

The unique task or dispatch identifier assigned by the MES (Manufacturing Execution System) — specifically Apriso/Dassault — to this AGV movement instruction. Used for cross-system reconciliation between the AGV fleet controller and the MES shop floor execution layer.

The precise date and time (ISO 8601 with timezone offset) when the AGV completed or terminated the movement task. Null if the movement is still in progress. Used with movement_start_timestamp to derive actual cycle time.

The precise date and time (ISO 8601 with timezone offset) when the AGV began executing the movement task. Used for cycle time calculation, throughput analysis, and JIS (Just-in-Sequence) compliance verification.

before.description: The identifier of the shop floor operator or MES user who manually initiated, overrode, or acknowledged this AGV movement task. Null for fully automated movements with no human intervention. Supports operator accountability and manual override tracking.

The shop floor location code (e.g., storage lane, buffer zone, work station address) from which the AGV departed for this movement. Encoded per the plant's internal location addressing scheme (e.g., aisle-bay-level). Used for material flow mapping and route optimization.

Human-readable descriptive name of the origin location (e.g., 'Body Shop Buffer Lane 3', 'Paint Shop Entry Conveyor', 'Stamping Parts Supermarket'). Supports operational reporting and shop floor visualization dashboards.

Human-readable description of the part or component being transported (e.g., 'Front Door Inner Panel LH', 'Battery Module Assembly EV'). Supports operational reporting without requiring a join to the parts master.

The OEM (Original Equipment Manufacturer) part number of the primary component or assembly being transported by the AGV. Supports Bill of Materials (BOM) traceability and JIS (Just-in-Sequence) delivery verification at the assembly line.
The MES-scheduled completion time for this AGV movement task. Compared against movement_end_timestamp to measure on-time delivery performance and identify bottlenecks in material flow.
The MES-scheduled start time for this AGV movement task. Compared against movement_start_timestamp to measure schedule adherence and identify JIS (Just-in-Sequence) delivery deviations.

The dispatch priority assigned to this AGV movement by the MES or AGV fleet controller. Critical and high priority movements are typically associated with JIS (Just-in-Sequence) call-offs or line-stop prevention. Used for queue management and SLA reporting.

The number of parts, units, or assemblies carried by the AGV in this movement. Used for material flow volume reporting, inventory reconciliation, and JIT (Just-in-Time) delivery quantity verification.

Indicates whether the AGV deviated from its assigned route during this movement (True = deviation occurred, False = route followed as planned). Deviations may indicate obstacles, dynamic re-routing, or system faults requiring investigation.

Maximum number of vehicle units that can be held in the buffer/queue between this build stage and the next stage. Defines the WIP (Work in Progress) inventory limit for line balancing and is used in production simulation and bottleneck analysis.

Standard CO2-equivalent emissions in kilograms per vehicle unit processed at this build stage. Supports EPA and CARB (California Air Resources Board) environmental compliance reporting, sustainability KPIs, and manufacturing carbon footprint tracking.

Reference code of the APQP (Advanced Product Quality Planning) control plan document governing quality control activities at this build stage. Specifies product/process characteristics, control methods, and reaction plans for out-of-control conditions per IATF 16949.

The EOP (End of Production) date on which this build stage is scheduled to be or was decommissioned. Null if the stage is currently active with no planned end date. Used for production planning horizon management and asset retirement scheduling.

Reference identifier linking this build stage to its corresponding FMEA (Failure Mode and Effects Analysis) document. Ensures traceability between the process stage definition and its risk assessment per IATF 16949 and APQP (Advanced Product Quality Planning) requirements.

Classification of hazardous materials present or used at this build stage per DOT and EPA regulations (e.g., paint solvents, E-Coat chemicals, welding fumes). Drives EHS (Environmental Health and Safety) compliance, PPE requirements, and ISO 14001 environmental management reporting.

IATF 16949 process category designation for this build stage: special-characteristic (processes producing special product/process characteristics requiring enhanced control), standard-process, critical-process (safety-critical per FMVSS), or monitoring-only (observation without active control). Drives audit scope and PPAP (Production Part Approval Process) requirements.

Maximum allowable ambient or process temperature in degrees Celsius for this build stage. Exceeding this threshold triggers a quality hold and SCADA alarm. Particularly relevant for paint curing ovens, E-Coat baths, and weld quality control.

Minimum allowable ambient or process temperature in degrees Celsius for this build stage to operate within specification. Critical for paint shop, E-Coat, and adhesive curing stages where temperature directly affects product quality. Used in SPC (Statistical Process Control) monitoring.

Comma-separated list of MY (Model Year) designations for which this build stage definition is applicable (e.g., MY2024,MY2025) or ALL if applicable across all model years. Supports model-year-specific production routing and engineering change management.

Alphanumeric code identifying the specific plant area or shop within the manufacturing facility where this build stage is physically located (e.g., SH01 for Stamping Hall 1, BS02 for Body Shop 2). Aligns with SAP S/4HANA work center and plant layout master data.

Identifier of the PLC (Programmable Logic Controller) program controlling the automated equipment at this build stage. Used for change management, version control of control programs, and traceability of equipment configuration changes per IATF 16949 requirements.

Target defect rate for this build stage expressed in PPM (Parts Per Million). Defines the quality performance benchmark used in IATF 16949 supplier and process quality reporting, SPC control limit setting, and continuous improvement initiatives.

Stage code of the immediately preceding build stage in the standard production sequence. Defines the upstream dependency for production flow control, WIP (Work in Progress) tracking, and JIS (Just-in-Sequence) scheduling. Null for the first stage in the sequence.

Reference code of the SAP QM (Quality Management) inspection plan associated with this build stage. Defines the inspection characteristics, sampling procedures, and acceptance criteria applied during quality gate checks. Linked to FMEA (Failure Mode and Effects Analysis) and APQP documentation.

Safety risk classification of this build stage per DOT and OSHA standards: standard (routine operations), elevated-risk (requires additional PPE or safety protocols), critical-safety (safety-critical operations with mandatory sign-off), or restricted-access (limited to certified personnel only).

The SAP S/4HANA PP routing operation code corresponding to this build stage. Enables direct linkage between the build stage reference master and SAP production order routing operations for cost allocation, scheduling, and confirmation.

Standard shift pattern under which this build stage operates: single (one shift per day), double (two shifts), triple (three shifts), or continuous (24/7 operation). Used for capacity planning, labor scheduling in SuccessFactors, and production throughput calculations.

The SOP (Start of Production) date on which this build stage was first commissioned and became operational for regular production. Used for asset lifecycle tracking, warranty baseline calculations, and production history reporting.

Stage code of the immediately succeeding build stage in the standard production sequence. Defines the downstream handoff point for production flow control and vehicle build traceability. Null for the final stage (PDI) in the sequence.

Date and time when the capacity plan was formally approved by the designated authority. Marks the transition from 'submitted' to 'approved' status in the S&OP governance process.
Name or employee identifier of the S&OP or manufacturing leadership authority who approved this capacity plan. Required for audit trail and governance compliance under IATF 16949.

Total scheduled production hours available in the planning period after accounting for planned downtime, shift breaks, and scheduled maintenance. Used in conjunction with rated_capacity_jph to compute rated capacity in units.

Narrative description of the primary capacity constraint at the bottleneck work center (e.g., 'Paint oven cycle time limits throughput to 58 JPH', 'Robotic welding cell maintenance window reduces available hours'). Supports root cause analysis and CapEx justification.
