before.description: Reference to the work center identified as the capacity bottleneck constraining overall line throughput during this planning period. Used to prioritize capacity improvement investments and focus S&OP constraint management.

Difference between planned_production_units and demonstrated_capacity_units, representing the capacity shortfall or surplus for the planning period. Positive value indicates a capacity gap requiring corrective action (overtime, additional shifts, CapEx); negative value indicates surplus capacity.

Classification of the capacity planning methodology used. 'rough_cut' (RCCP — Rough Cut Capacity Planning) for high-level S&OP; 'detailed' for work-center-level CRP (Capacity Requirements Planning); 'constraint_based' for Theory of Constraints analysis; 'what_if' for scenario planning and CapEx evaluation.

Planned capacity utilization rate expressed as a percentage, calculated as (planned_production_units / rated_capacity_units) × 100. Drives S&OP decisions on overtime, additional shifts, and capital investment. Target thresholds are typically 85–95% for automotive assembly.

Estimated capital expenditure amount required to address the capacity gap identified in this plan. Expressed in the plant's operating currency. Used for CapEx budget submissions and investment approval processes.

Indicates whether this capacity plan identifies a requirement for capital investment (CapEx) to close a capacity gap (e.g., new tooling, additional robots, facility expansion). Triggers CapEx approval workflow in SAP FI/CO.

Hours allocated for model changeovers, tooling changes, and line reconfigurations during the planning period. Relevant for mixed-model assembly lines producing multiple vehicle variants (e.g., ICE and BEV on the same line).

ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for all monetary values in this capacity plan record (e.g., USD, EUR, MXN, CNY). Ensures consistent financial reporting across multi-plant, multi-currency manufacturing operations.

Planned number of vehicles to be produced per working day during the planning period, derived from planned_production_units / working_days. Used for daily MES scheduling and shift-level production targets.

Actual production output achieved in a comparable prior period, used as the realistic baseline for capacity planning. Reflects real-world constraints such as quality losses, minor stoppages, and changeovers. Key input to APQP (Advanced Product Quality Planning) capacity studies.

affected_objects.before: workforce.employee.employee_id

before.description: Reference to the manufacturing or industrial engineering employee responsible for maintaining and updating this capacity plan. Supports accountability tracking in S&OP governance.

Planned End of Production (EOP) date for the vehicle model or program covered by this capacity plan. Marks the milestone when production of the model is scheduled to cease. Used for capacity wind-down planning and asset redeployment decisions.
Fiscal year (FY) to which this capacity plan belongs, used for CapEx (Capital Expenditure) alignment, budget planning, and financial reporting. Format: FY followed by 4-digit year (e.g., FY2025).

Total direct labor headcount required to execute the planned production volume during the planning period. Used for workforce planning, hiring decisions, and labor cost budgeting in SuccessFactors and SAP CO.

Indicates whether the capacity plan is constrained by a bottleneck work center that limits overall line throughput below the planned production target. When True, the bottleneck_work_center_id and bottleneck_constraint_description fields are populated.
Automotive model year (MY) for which this capacity plan is prepared. Capacity plans are typically aligned to MY production programs, SOP (Start of Production), and EOP (End of Production) milestones.
Number of production shifts planned per working day for this capacity plan (e.g., 1, 2, or 3 shifts). Directly determines available production hours and total capacity for the planning period.
Last calendar date of the planning period covered by this capacity plan record. Together with plan_start_date, defines the planning window for capacity supply and demand balancing.

Externally-known, human-readable business identifier for the capacity plan record, used in S&OP (Sales and Operations Planning) communications, SAP PP capacity planning transactions (CM01/CM21), and cross-functional reporting. Format: CP-{PLANT}-{YEAR}-{MONTH}-{SEQ}.

affected_objects.before: workforce.employee.employee_id

before.description: Reference to the manufacturing or industrial engineering employee responsible for maintaining and updating this capacity plan. Supports accountability tracking in S&OP governance.
First calendar date of the planning period covered by this capacity plan record. Used to align capacity supply with demand signals from S&OP and MRP (Material Requirements Planning) runs.

Version identifier of the capacity plan, enabling management of multiple planning iterations (e.g., v1.0, v2.0) within the same planning period. Supports S&OP cycle versioning and plan-over-plan variance analysis.

Total planned downtime hours for the production line during the planning period, including scheduled maintenance, tooling changeovers, model changeovers, and planned shutdowns. Reduces available production hours from the theoretical maximum.

Subset of planned downtime hours specifically allocated to preventive and predictive maintenance activities on production equipment. Tracked separately from changeover downtime for maintenance KPI reporting and SAP PM integration.

Total overtime hours planned for the production line during the planning period to meet production targets beyond standard shift capacity. Feeds into workforce cost planning and labor budget in SAP CO.

Number of vehicles planned for production in the planning period as agreed in the S&OP process. Represents the demand signal that capacity must satisfy. Compared against rated and demonstrated capacity to identify gaps.

Granularity of the capacity planning horizon for this record. 'weekly' supports short-term MES scheduling; 'monthly' supports S&OP cycles; 'quarterly' and 'annual' support CapEx and strategic workforce planning.

Demand scenario underpinning this capacity plan. 'base' reflects the consensus S&OP forecast; 'optimistic' reflects upside demand; 'pessimistic' reflects downside risk; 'stretch' reflects maximum achievable output. Enables scenario comparison for executive decision-making.

Powertrain technology type planned for production in this capacity plan. ICE = Internal Combustion Engine; HEV = Hybrid Electric Vehicle; PHEV = Plug-in Hybrid Electric Vehicle; BEV = Battery Electric Vehicle; FCEV = Fuel Cell Electric Vehicle. Impacts tooling, line configuration, and capacity requirements.

Theoretical maximum production rate expressed in Jobs Per Hour (JPH) for the production line under ideal conditions. Derived from takt time and line design specifications. Used as the baseline for capacity utilization calculations in S&OP.

Theoretical maximum number of vehicles that can be produced in the planning period, calculated as rated_capacity_jph × available_hours. Represents the upper bound of production capacity for S&OP and CapEx planning.

Source system identifier for this capacity plan record in SAP S/4HANA PP (Production Planning) module, used for data lineage traceability and reconciliation between the lakehouse Silver layer and the operational ERP system.

before.description: Reference to the shift pattern (e.g., 1-shift, 2-shift, 3-shift) applied in this capacity plan. Shift pattern determines available production hours and directly impacts rated capacity calculation.

Indicates whether the control plan reaction plan was triggered as a result of this parameter reading (True = reaction plan activated due to out-of-spec or out-of-control condition). Supports IATF 16949 audit evidence.

Exact date and time when the process parameter value was measured by the PLC/SCADA system. This is the principal business event timestamp for this record, representing the real-world moment of measurement.
Timestamp when this process parameter record was first ingested into the data platform (silver layer). Distinct from reading_timestamp which represents the actual measurement event time.
Timestamp of the most recent update to this process parameter record in the data platform. Used for incremental load tracking and audit trail purposes.
Sequential sample number within the SPC subgroup or sampling plan for this parameter at this work center. Used to construct X-bar/R charts and other SPC control charts.
Identifier of the SCADA system instance that collected and transmitted this process parameter reading to the MES/data platform.
Code identifying the production shift during which this parameter reading was captured (e.g., 'SHIFT_A', 'SHIFT_B', 'SHIFT_C'). Supports shift-level SPC analysis and quality reporting.

Identifies the specific SPC detection rule that was violated when is_out_of_control is True (e.g., 'RULE_1_BEYOND_3SIGMA', 'RULE_2_NINE_CONSECUTIVE', 'RULE_3_SIX_TRENDING'). Null when no rule is violated.
Identifier of the SPC rational subgroup to which this reading belongs. Subgroups are used to calculate control limits and assess process variation in X-bar/R or X-bar/S charts.

before.description: Identifier of the specific tool or fixture used during the operation (e.g., torque bit ID, weld electrode ID, press die ID). Distinct from equipment_id; a single machine may use multiple interchangeable tools.
Statistical Upper Control Limit (UCL) for this process parameter as defined by SPC methodology. Readings above this value indicate the process is out of statistical control.

affected_objects.before: manufacturing.vehicle_build.vehicle_build_id

before.description: Reference to the vehicle build record associated with this process parameter reading, enabling full build traceability per VIN.
Internal vehicle model or platform code for the vehicle being built (e.g., 'F150', 'RAV4', 'MODEL_3'). Supports model-level process capability analysis and SPC stratification.

The date on which this manufacturing BOM received formal approval from the designated authority. Precedes the release_date in the BOM lifecycle workflow. Required for IATF 16949 documented information control.

User ID or employee identifier of the approving authority (e.g., Chief Engineer, Manufacturing Manager) who approved this BOM for production release. Distinct from released_by — approval may be a separate workflow step in Teamcenter PLM or SAP workflow.

Current APQP phase associated with this BOM's program lifecycle. Phase 1=Plan and Define, Phase 2=Product Design and Development, Phase 3=Process Design and Development, Phase 4=Product and Process Validation, Phase 5=Launch/Feedback. Tracks BOM maturity relative to the program development gate.

Indicates whether the vehicle is assembled as a Completely Built Unit (CBU), Completely Knocked Down (CKD) kit for overseas assembly, or Semi Knocked Down (SKD) kit. Determines the BOM structure, component packaging, and applicable customs/import regulations for the target market.

SAP BOM alternative identifier (e.g., '01', '02') distinguishing multiple valid BOM configurations for the same material and plant. Supports variant BOMs for different production lines or regional configurations (e.g., LHD vs RHD, CKD vs SKD).

The maximum depth/level of the BOM hierarchy for this manufacturing BOM (e.g., 1 = single-level, 5 = five levels deep). Used to understand BOM complexity and to control multi-level BOM explosion in MRP and production scheduling.

SAP BOM usage indicator defining the organizational context in which the BOM is applied. 'production' (SAP usage 1) is the standard for shop floor manufacturing. 'engineering' (SAP usage 2) is for design/development. 'universal' (SAP usage 3) applies across all usages. Determines which BOM is selected during MRP and production order processing.

Free-text description of the business reason for creating or modifying this BOM version (e.g., 'Cost reduction – substitute supplier for part X', 'Regulatory compliance – CARB Tier 3 emission update', 'Quality improvement – NVH fix per TSB-2024-001'). Required for IATF 16949 change control documentation.

affected_objects.before: engineering.bom.bom_id

before.description: Reference identifier linking this manufacturing BOM (mBOM) to the originating engineering BOM (eBOM) in Siemens Teamcenter PLM or PTC Windchill. Enables traceability from shop floor execution back to the engineering design intent. The eBOM-to-mBOM transformation is managed via the PLM-SAP integration.

The planned or actual End of Production (EOP) date for the vehicle program associated with this BOM. Marks the milestone when serial production of this vehicle configuration ceases. Used for last-time-buy planning, spare parts provisioning, and regulatory compliance archiving.

Status of the regulatory homologation (type approval) for the vehicle configuration defined by this BOM in the target regulatory market. 'approved' is required before vehicles built to this BOM can be legally sold in the target market. Managed through the Regulatory Compliance and Homologation process.

Indicates whether the header material of this BOM is a phantom assembly — a logical grouping of components that is not physically stocked or produced as a discrete unit. Phantom assemblies are 'exploded through' during MRP and production order processing. Common for sub-assemblies in JIS manufacturing.

Classification of the vehicle powertrain technology for which this BOM is defined. ICE = Internal Combustion Engine, HEV = Hybrid Electric Vehicle, PHEV = Plug-in Hybrid Electric Vehicle, BEV = Battery Electric Vehicle, FCEV = Fuel Cell Electric Vehicle. Determines applicable emissions regulations (EPA, CARB, WLTP) and BOM component sets.

Status of the Production Part Approval Process (PPAP) for the components in this BOM. PPAP is the AIAG/IATF 16949 process that verifies supplier components meet design and specification requirements before production launch. 'approved' is required before the BOM can be released to production.

BOM number of the previous manufacturing BOM version that this BOM supersedes. Enables backward navigation in the BOM version chain for change impact analysis and quality investigations. Null for the initial BOM version.

Code identifying the specific production line or assembly line within the plant for which this BOM is configured (e.g., 'LINE-A', 'TRIM-CHASSIS-1'). Used in Apriso/Dassault MES for shop floor routing and JIS (Just-in-Sequence) scheduling.

Code identifying the target regulatory market for which this BOM is homologated (e.g., 'US-FEDERAL', 'US-CARB', 'EU-EURO6', 'JP-JC08', 'CN-CHINA6'). Determines applicable emissions standards (EPA, CARB, Euro 6, WLTP), safety regulations (NHTSA FMVSS, UNECE), and CAFE compliance requirements.

The date on which this manufacturing BOM was formally released to production (status changed to 'released'). Marks the point at which the BOM is authorized for use in production orders and MRP planning. Corresponds to the SAP BOM release date.

User ID or employee identifier of the manufacturing engineer or release authority who formally released this BOM to production in SAP PP or Teamcenter PLM. Required for audit trail and change control compliance under IATF 16949.

Alphanumeric revision level of the BOM (e.g., 'A', 'B', 'C' or '01', '02'). Used in conjunction with bom_version to track incremental changes within a version. Aligns with SAP BOM revision level and Teamcenter PLM revision management.

SAP routing number linking this manufacturing BOM to the associated production routing (sequence of operations, work centers, and standard times). The BOM and routing together define the complete manufacturing recipe for the vehicle. Corresponds to SAP PP routing header (CA01).

The planned or actual Start of Production (SOP) date for the vehicle program associated with this BOM. Marks the milestone when serial production begins using this BOM configuration. Critical for program management, supplier readiness, and PPAP completion tracking.

Identifies the operational system of record from which this manufacturing BOM record was sourced (e.g., 'SAP_PP' for SAP Production Planning, 'TEAMCENTER' for Siemens Teamcenter PLM). Required for data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver Layer and for resolving conflicts during BOM synchronization between PLM and ERP.

BOM number of the newer manufacturing BOM that has replaced this one (populated when bom_status = 'superseded'). Enables forward navigation in the BOM version chain for traceability and historical analysis. Null when this is the current active BOM.

Code identifying the specific vehicle configuration (variant) for which this BOM is defined, including body style, drivetrain, trim level, and market variant (e.g., 'SUV-AWD-PREMIUM-NA'). Used in SAP Variant Configuration (VC) to select the correct BOM components for a specific vehicle order.
Internal OEM code identifying the vehicle model (nameplate) for which this mBOM is defined (e.g., 'F150', 'RAV4', 'MODEL3'). Used to associate the BOM with the correct vehicle program in PLM and SAP.

SAP CO activity type (LSTAR) used to record the confirmed actual activities (setup, machine, labor) against the production order. Drives cost settlement rates and actual cost calculation in SAP CO-PC (Product Costing). Required for standard vs. actual cost variance analysis.

The manufacturing assembly stage at which this confirmation was recorded. Reflects the major production process area within the vehicle manufacturing flow. Used for stage-level throughput analysis, WIP (Work in Progress) tracking, and process bottleneck identification. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: stamping|body_shop|paint|final_assembly|powertrain|chassis|trim — promote to reference product]

The unit of measure in which yield, scrap, and rework quantities are expressed. Typically 'EA' (Each) for vehicles and assemblies, 'PC' (Piece) for components, 'KG' for weight-based materials. Maps to SAP MM/PP base unit of measure (MEINS). Required for correct inventory posting and quantity reconciliation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: EA|PC|KG|L|M|SET|VH — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

SAP batch number (CHARG) assigned to the confirmed production output. Used for batch-managed materials to enable full forward and backward traceability of components and finished vehicles. Critical for recall management, warranty analysis, and regulatory compliance with NHTSA traceability requirements.

Method by which this production confirmation was entered into SAP PP. 'manual' = entered by operator via CO11N; 'automatic' = system-generated via PP-PI or SCADA integration; 'mes_interface' = posted via Apriso/Dassault MES interface; 'backflush' = automatic backflush confirmation triggered by goods issue. Used for data quality auditing and process automation tracking.

Current lifecycle status of the production confirmation record. 'created' = confirmation entered but not yet posted; 'posted' = successfully posted to SAP PP and inventory updated; 'reversed' = confirmation reversed via CO13; 'cancelled' = voided before posting; 'partial' = partial quantity confirmed, order still open; 'final' = final confirmation closing the production order.

SAP CO cost center (KOSTL) associated with the work center where this confirmation was posted. Used for actual cost allocation, activity-based costing, and manufacturing cost variance reporting. Enables EBITDA (Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortization) analysis at the plant and cost center level.

Total unplanned downtime duration recorded during this production confirmation period, in minutes. Captured from SCADA/PLC systems or MES downtime tracking. Used for OEE (Overall Equipment Effectiveness) availability calculation, maintenance planning, and production loss analysis.

Coded reason for any downtime recorded during this confirmation period. Maps to the plant's downtime reason catalog (e.g., 'MECH' = Mechanical Failure, 'MATL' = Material Shortage, 'QUAL' = Quality Hold, 'CHNG' = Changeover). Used for root cause analysis, maintenance prioritization, and production loss reporting.

Indicates whether this confirmation is the final confirmation for the production order (SAP PP IEDD — Final Confirmation Indicator). When True, SAP PP automatically closes the production order, triggers goods receipt for the finished product, and initiates order settlement to CO (Controlling). Critical for order lifecycle management and inventory accuracy.

Indicates whether the automatic goods receipt (GR) to inventory has been successfully posted as a result of this production confirmation. True = inventory has been updated with the confirmed yield quantity. Used for inventory reconciliation and to identify confirmations where GR posting failed or is pending.

Actual direct labor time consumed for this production operation, recorded in minutes. Maps to SAP PP activity type for labor (ISRLA — Actual Labor Time). Used for labor cost settlement to the production order, workforce productivity analysis, and standard vs. actual cost variance reporting.
Planned direct labor time for this operation as defined in the SAP PP routing, recorded in minutes. Baseline for labor efficiency variance analysis and standard cost calculation.

The timestamp when this production confirmation record was last modified in the source system. Tracks reversals, corrections, and status updates. Used for incremental data loading in the Databricks Silver Layer pipeline and change data capture (CDC) processing.

Actual machine runtime consumed for this production operation, recorded in minutes. Maps to SAP PP activity type for machine time (ISRÜT — Actual Machine Time). Core input for OEE calculation, takt time variance analysis, and capacity utilization reporting. Compared against planned machine time from the routing to identify bottlenecks.
Planned machine time for this operation as defined in the SAP PP routing, recorded in minutes. Baseline for actual vs. planned machine time variance analysis and takt time adherence reporting.

SAP material number (MATNR) of the finished or semi-finished product being confirmed. Identifies the vehicle model, sub-assembly, or component produced in this confirmation. Essential for inventory goods receipt posting and BOM (Bill of Materials) reconciliation.

The confirmation or transaction reference number from the Apriso/Dassault MES system that corresponds to this SAP PP production confirmation. Enables cross-system traceability between the MES shop floor execution record and the SAP ERP confirmation posting. Critical for audit trails and discrepancy resolution.

The vehicle model year (MY) of the product being confirmed. Used for production output reporting by model year, regulatory compliance tracking (CAFE, EPA emissions), and alignment with SOP (Start of Production) and EOP (End of Production) milestones. Retained as a denormalized attribute for direct reporting without joining to vehicle configuration.

Status of the SAP CO production order settlement triggered by this final confirmation. 'pending' = settlement not yet executed; 'settled' = actual costs fully settled to cost objects; 'partially_settled' = partial settlement completed; 'not_required' = non-final confirmation, settlement not applicable. Used for period-end closing and financial reporting.

affected_objects.before: manufacturing.plant.plant_id

before.description: Reference to the manufacturing plant where this production confirmation was posted. Enables plant-level production output reporting, capacity utilization analysis, and multi-plant benchmarking.

The powertrain technology type of the vehicle or assembly being confirmed. ICE = Internal Combustion Engine, HEV = Hybrid Electric Vehicle, PHEV = Plug-in Hybrid Electric Vehicle, BEV = Battery Electric Vehicle, FCEV = Fuel Cell Electric Vehicle. Used for regulatory reporting (CAFE, EPA, CARB), EV production mix analysis, and R&D investment tracking.

SAP PP production order number (AUFNR) to which this confirmation is posted. Links the confirmation to the originating manufacturing order for order settlement, cost collection, and goods receipt triggering. Retained as a business attribute for direct shop floor reporting without requiring a join.

SAP QM inspection lot number (PRUEFLOS) created automatically upon goods receipt posting from this confirmation. Links the production output to the quality inspection record for in-process and final inspection results. Used for quality traceability and IATF 16949 inspection record management.

Flag indicating whether this confirmation record is a reversal entry (CO13 reversal in SAP PP). True = this record reverses a previously posted confirmation. Used to identify correction entries in production output reporting and to exclude reversed confirmations from yield and time aggregations.

before.description: Reference to the original production confirmation record that this entry reverses. Populated only when reversal_indicator is True. Enables audit trail reconstruction and net quantity calculation when reversals are present. Self-referencing within the production_confirmation product.

Coded reason for scrap recorded against this confirmation. Maps to SAP QM defect codes or MES scrap reason catalog (e.g., 'DIM' = Dimensional Non-conformance, 'WLD' = Weld Defect, 'PNT' = Paint Defect, 'ASY' = Assembly Error). Required for PPM (Parts Per Million) defect analysis, FMEA updates, and quality improvement initiatives per IATF 16949.

Actual machine/workstation setup time consumed for this operation, recorded in minutes. Maps to SAP PP activity type for setup (ISRST — Actual Setup Time). Used for capacity planning, OEE (Overall Equipment Effectiveness) calculation, and comparison against planned setup time from the routing.

Planned setup time for this operation as defined in the SAP PP routing, recorded in minutes. Provides the baseline for actual vs. planned setup time variance analysis. Sourced from the routing master data at the time of production order creation.

before.description: Reference to the production shift during which this confirmation was recorded. Enables shift-level production output analysis, yield comparison across shifts, and workforce productivity reporting.

SAP storage location (LGORT) to which the confirmed yield quantity is posted as a goods receipt. Identifies the physical inventory location within the plant (e.g., finished goods area, WIP buffer, sequencing area). Required for inventory management and JIS (Just-in-Sequence) delivery coordination.

Actual takt time achieved for this production confirmation, expressed in seconds per unit. Calculated as total operation time divided by yield quantity. Used for production line balancing, bottleneck identification, and comparison against the planned takt time to assess line efficiency. Key metric in JIS (Just-in-Sequence) production management.

Actual teardown/cleanup time consumed after the production operation, recorded in minutes. Maps to SAP PP activity type for teardown. Included in total operation time for accurate takt time and capacity utilization calculations. Relevant for paint booth cleaning, tooling changeover, and AGV (Automated Guided Vehicle) repositioning cycles.

17-character Vehicle Identification Number assigned to the vehicle unit confirmed in this production record. Populated for final assembly confirmations where a specific vehicle unit is produced. Null for sub-assembly or component-level confirmations. Enables full build traceability from production confirmation to vehicle delivery.

Indicates the assembly kit type this line is configured to process: CKD (Completely Knocked Down — full kit assembly from parts), SKD (Semi Knocked Down — partial pre-assembly), CBU (Completely Built Up — no kit assembly, line-off only), or multi (capable of multiple kit types). Relevant for export assembly plants and regulatory homologation.

Current IATF 16949 (International Automotive Task Force) quality management system audit status for this production line: compliant (no non-conformances), minor_nc (minor non-conformance identified), major_nc (major non-conformance — corrective action required), suspended (production suspended pending corrective action), or not_audited (not yet subject to IATF audit).

Date of the most recent IATF 16949 quality management system audit conducted on this production line. Used for audit cycle management, corrective action tracking, and regulatory compliance reporting to OEM customers and certification bodies.

Type of paint application system used on this line (applicable to paint shop lines): waterborne (water-based paint — lower VOC emissions), solventborne (solvent-based paint), powder_coat (electrostatic powder coating), or none (non-paint line). Drives EPA/CARB VOC (Volatile Organic Compound) emissions compliance reporting and environmental permit management.

Identifier or name of the PLC (Programmable Logic Controller) system or network controlling this production line's automated equipment (e.g., 'Siemens S7-1500 Network A', 'Allen-Bradley ControlLogix Zone 3'). Used for maintenance management in SAP PM, SCADA integration, and cybersecurity asset inventory.

Identifier or name of the SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition) system monitoring and controlling this production line (e.g., 'Ignition SCADA Plant2-Zone1', 'Wonderware InTouch Line FA-01'). Used for real-time production monitoring, alarm management, and integration with MES and ERP systems.

Current shift schedule configuration for the production line, indicating the number of operating shifts per day: 1_shift (single day shift), 2_shift (day and afternoon), 3_shift (continuous 24-hour), or 4_shift_rotating (rotating continental schedule). Drives capacity planning, workforce scheduling in SuccessFactors, and MRP calculations in SAP PP.

Identifies the operational system of record from which this production line master record was sourced: SAP_PP (SAP S/4HANA Production Planning), Apriso_MES (Apriso/Dassault Manufacturing Execution System), Teamcenter (Siemens Teamcenter PLM), Manual (manually entered), or SCADA (derived from SCADA system configuration). Used for data lineage and reconciliation.

The Just-in-Sequence (JIS) sequence number assigned to this production order, defining its position in the assembly line build sequence. Critical for JIS supply chain synchronization — ensures parts arrive at the line in the exact order vehicles are built. Managed by MES and communicated to tier-1 suppliers.

Priority tier assigned to the allocation for fulfillment sequencing
Name or employee identifier of the production planning manager who formally approved this schedule version for release to the shop floor. Required for IATF 16949 document control and audit trail.
Timestamp when the production schedule was formally approved for release. Marks the transition from 'draft' to 'released' status and triggers supplier call-off generation.

Manufacturing process stage covered by this schedule record. Reflects the major shop areas in automotive assembly: stamping (metal forming), body shop (welding/joining), paint (surface treatment), final assembly (powertrain/trim installation), or trim-chassis-final (TCF integrated line).
Total available production capacity in hours for this schedule period on the assigned production line, accounting for planned downtime, maintenance windows, and shift patterns.
Body style classification of the vehicles scheduled for production. Used for production line configuration, tooling setup, and capacity planning by body type.

Ending sequence number for the JIS (Just-in-Sequence) build order within this schedule period. Together with build_sequence_start defines the range of vehicle sequence numbers assigned to this schedule.

Starting sequence number for the JIS (Just-in-Sequence) build order within this schedule period. Used by MES and AGV systems to sequence vehicle bodies through the production line in the correct order.

Classification of the production build type. 'standard' = full series production; 'ckd' = Completely Knocked Down (CKD) kit assembly; 'skd' = Semi Knocked Down (SKD) assembly; 'pilot' = pre-production pilot build; 'pre_series' = pre-series validation build.
Timestamp when supplier delivery call-offs were transmitted to the supply base for this production schedule. Used for OTD (On-Time Delivery) tracking and supplier performance measurement.
Official End of Production (EOP) date for the vehicle model/model year. Schedules beyond this date are invalid. Used for phase-out planning, last-time-buy procurement, and regulatory deregistration.

Fiscal period (month number 1-12 or 1-16 for special periods) within the fiscal year. Enables alignment of production volumes with financial reporting periods for management accounting and EBITDA analysis.
Fiscal year (FY) to which this production schedule belongs. Used for financial planning, CapEx allocation, and EBITDA reporting alignment between production volumes and financial periods.

ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code for the primary regulatory market for which these vehicles are being produced. Determines applicable homologation standards (NHTSA/FMVSS for USA, UNECE for Europe, etc.), emissions certification (EPA, CARB, Euro 6), and CAFE compliance tracking. Business reason code or description for the most recent schedule revision. Examples: material shortage, capacity constraint, demand change, quality hold, tooling failure, model mix adjustment. Required for change control audit trail per IATF 16949.

Free-text field for production planners to record contextual notes, exceptions, or special instructions associated with this schedule record. Examples: tooling changeover notes, quality hold references, special customer order constraints.
Precise timestamp when production is scheduled to complete for this schedule record. Used for shift planning, takt time validation, and downstream logistics coordination.
Precise timestamp when production is scheduled to begin on the line for this schedule record. Used for JIS (Just-in-Sequence) sequencing, AGV routing, and supplier call-off timing.

Official Start of Production (SOP) date for the vehicle model/model year being scheduled. Marks the formal launch of series production. Used to validate that schedule dates fall within the active production window.

Boolean flag indicating whether supplier delivery call-offs (JIT/JIS delivery schedules) have been generated and transmitted to suppliers based on this production schedule. True = call-offs sent; False = pending call-off generation.

before.description: Reference to the vehicle model (e.g., sedan, SUV, truck, EV) being scheduled for production. Links to the vehicle master product record.

SAE J3016 automation level of the ADAS (Advanced Driver Assistance Systems) suite fitted to this production variant: L0 (no automation), L1 (driver assistance), L2 (partial automation), L2_PLUS (enhanced partial automation), L3 (conditional automation). Drives ECU (Electronic Control Unit) software configuration, OTA (Over-the-Air Update) eligibility, and UNECE UN R157 regulatory compliance.

Numeric score (1–10) representing the relative assembly complexity of this production variant compared to the base variant on the same production line. Higher scores indicate more assembly operations, longer cycle times, or specialized tooling requirements. Used for JIS (Just-in-Sequence) sequencing optimization to balance line loading and avoid consecutive high-complexity builds.

Usable battery pack capacity in kilowatt-hours (kWh) for BEV, PHEV, and HEV variants. Null for pure ICE variants. Drives assembly sequencing for battery marriage station, WLTP (Worldwide Harmonised Light Vehicles Test Procedure) range certification, and EPA electric range labelling.

Standardized code identifying the vehicle body configuration for this production variant (e.g., SEDAN, SUV, TRUCK, COUPE, HATCHBACK, MINIVAN). Determines stamping die sets, body shop tooling, and paint booth configuration requirements. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: SEDAN|SUV|TRUCK|COUPE|HATCHBACK|MINIVAN|CONVERTIBLE|WAGON|VAN|CROSSOVER — promote to reference product]

Certified CO2 tailpipe emission in grams per kilometre (g/km) under WLTP or NEDC test cycle for this production variant. Used for EU CO2 fleet average compliance (Regulation (EU) 2019/631), CAFE (Corporate Average Fuel Economy) calculations, and vehicle taxation band classification in destination markets.

Three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code identifying the primary market for which this production variant is homologated and destined (e.g., 'USA', 'DEU', 'JPN'). Governs regulatory compliance requirements (NHTSA FMVSS, Euro NCAP, UNECE), emission standards, and right-hand vs left-hand drive configuration.

Drivetrain configuration specifying which axles receive motive power: FWD (Front-Wheel Drive), RWD (Rear-Wheel Drive), AWD (All-Wheel Drive), or 4WD (Four-Wheel Drive). Determines chassis assembly routing, driveshaft fitment, and NVH (Noise Vibration Harshness) validation requirements.

Total engine displacement in cubic centimetres (cc) for ICE (Internal Combustion Engine) and HEV/PHEV variants. Null for BEV and FCEV variants. Used for regulatory classification under EPA, CARB, and UNECE emissions standards, and for CAFE (Corporate Average Fuel Economy) fleet averaging calculations.

Current engineering change revision level for this production variant as managed in Siemens Teamcenter PLM or PTC Windchill (e.g., 'A', 'B', 'C1', 'REV3'). Tracks design maturity and ensures the correct BOM (Bill of Materials) version is applied during production. Incremented upon each approved engineering change notice (ECN).

The vehicle model year (MY) of the unit undergoing rework. Used for regulatory compliance reporting, warranty analysis, and production quality trending by model year.
Code identifying the specific production line (e.g., stamping, body shop, paint, final assembly) where the defect was originally detected and the rework order was raised.

Document number or reference to the approved rework instruction, repair standard, or Technical Service Bulletin (TSB) that governs the rework procedure. Ensures traceability to authorized repair methods.

Total internal labor cost incurred for the rework operation, calculated from actual rework hours and the applicable labor rate. Expressed in the plant's operating currency. Used for quality cost (Cost of Poor Quality - COPQ) reporting.

Cost of replacement parts and materials consumed during the rework operation. Sourced from SAP MM goods issue postings against the rework order. Contributes to total Cost of Poor Quality (COPQ) calculation.
Current lifecycle status of the rework order within the shop floor execution workflow. Tracks progression from creation through completion or cancellation as managed in MES or SAP QM.

Standardized code classifying the root cause of the defect as determined through root cause analysis (e.g., 5-Why, Ishikawa). Populated upon rework completion. Supports FMEA (Failure Mode and Effects Analysis) and SPC (Statistical Process Control) improvement actions.
Number of components or sub-assemblies scrapped as a result of this rework order where repair was not feasible. Used for PPM (Parts Per Million) defect rate calculation and scrap cost reporting.

Code identifying the operational system of record from which this rework order record was sourced (e.g., SAP QM, Apriso/Dassault MES, or manual entry). Supports data lineage and Silver Layer ingestion traceability.
Internal product/model code identifying the vehicle nameplate or platform (e.g., truck, SUV, EV, HEV) associated with the rework order. Aligns with PLM product structure in Siemens Teamcenter.

17-character Vehicle Identification Number (VIN) of the vehicle or vehicle body on which rework is being performed. Nullable for sub-assembly rework not yet associated with a VIN. Conforms to ISO 3779 standard.

The SAP material number or BOM (Bill of Materials) component part number of the scrapped item. Null if the scrapped item is a complete vehicle unit (VIN-level scrap). Used for BOM-level scrap analysis and MRP (Material Requirements Planning) adjustments.

Externally visible, human-readable document number assigned to this scrap transaction, typically generated by SAP MM/PP goods movement (movement type 551/552). Used for audit trail and cross-system reconciliation.

The quantity of material or components scrapped in this transaction, expressed in the base unit of measure of the material (e.g., EA for each, KG for weight-based materials, M for length-based). Must be greater than zero.
Free-text narrative description of the scrap reason, providing additional context beyond the reason code. Entered by the operator or quality technician at the time of scrap recording in MES.

Current lifecycle status of the scrap record. 'pending' = awaiting supervisor confirmation; 'confirmed' = approved and posted to SAP CO; 'disposed' = material physically removed; 'reversed' = scrap posting reversed; 'under_review' = flagged for quality investigation.

The gross standard cost value of the scrapped material or component, calculated as scrap quantity multiplied by the SAP standard cost rate. Posted to SAP CO production variance account. Used for financial reporting of manufacturing losses.

Code identifying the production shift during which the scrap event occurred. D = Day, A = Afternoon, N = Night, E = Extended. Enables shift-level scrap pattern analysis for workforce and process improvement.

Physical weight of the scrapped material in kilograms. Used for environmental reporting (ISO 14001 waste generation metrics), recycling tracking, and logistics planning for scrap removal.

Pay rate multiplier applied to base wages for this shift (e.g., 1.5000 for time-and-a-half overtime, 1.2500 for night shift differential). Used in payroll cost calculations and labour cost reporting. Classified confidential as it contains compensation data.

Shift operating model classification indicating the overall production schedule structure at the plant (e.g., single_shift, two_shift, three_shift, four_shift_continental). Drives capacity planning and workforce rostering strategy.

Shift identifier as defined in SAP S/4HANA PP module (Schicht). Used for production order scheduling, capacity planning, and cross-system reconciliation with the ERP source of record.

Code identifying the SCADA monitoring zone associated with this shift definition. Used to correlate shift-level production data with real-time SCADA telemetry for process control and quality monitoring.
Ordinal position of the shift within a 24-hour production cycle at the plant/line (e.g., 1 = first shift, 2 = second shift, 3 = third shift). Used for JIS sequencing and handover management.

Free-text description providing additional context about the shift definition, including special operating conditions, seasonal variations, or programme-specific notes (e.g., 'Reduced capacity shift during model year changeover').

Outcome of the most recent quality inspection gate for this WIP item: 'pass' = conforms to specification; 'fail' = non-conforming; 'conditional_pass' = accepted with deviation; 'pending' = inspection not yet completed.
Date and time when the WIP item entered the current work center, buffer zone, or AGV carrier position. Used to calculate dwell time and identify bottlenecks in the production flow.

Four-digit model year (MY) of the vehicle being manufactured. Used to segregate WIP by model year for production planning, regulatory compliance (CAFE, EPA), and inventory valuation.
Date and time when the manufacturing operation on this WIP item was completed or closed. Used to calculate actual operation duration and compare against standard cycle time.
SAP PP routing operation number (Vorgangs-Nr.) identifying the specific manufacturing step being performed on this WIP item. Aligns with the production order routing sequence.
Date and time when the manufacturing operation on this WIP item was started by the operator or automated system. Represents the principal business event time for this WIP transaction.

Production priority assigned to this WIP item. 'EXPEDITE' indicates a rush order requiring immediate processing to meet customer or dealer commitment. Used by shop floor supervisors to manage queue sequencing.

Planned date by which this WIP item is expected to complete the current operation or exit the current stage, as defined in the production order schedule. Used for OTD (On-Time Delivery) tracking.

Planned standard cycle time in seconds for the current operation on this WIP item, as defined in the SAP PP routing. Used to calculate actual vs. standard cycle time variance and identify takt time deviations.

Unique identifier for a sub-assembly unit (e.g., powertrain module, instrument panel, axle assembly) when the WIP item is not yet associated with a full VIN. Assigned by the MES during component-level traceability.
Reference number for an approved supplier deviation or concession allowing a non-standard component to be used in this WIP item. Issued via PPAP (Production Part Approval Process) deviation process.
Internal code identifying the vehicle model or nameplate being assembled (e.g., F-150, Silverado, Model 3 equivalent). Supports model-mix analysis and JIS sequencing.

before.description: Identifier of the production supervisor or team leader responsible for this work center. Used for accountability tracking, escalation routing, and workforce management integration with SuccessFactors.

affected_objects.before: Unique surrogate identifier for each AGV movement event record on the shop floor. Primary key for the agv_movement data product.
The unique physical identifier assigned to the AGV unit performing the movement. Used for fleet management, maintenance scheduling, and utilization tracking per individual vehicle.
The date and time when this AGV movement record was first created in the MES or data platform. Used for audit trail, data lineage, and Silver layer ingestion tracking.

Current lifecycle state of the AGV movement event. Tracks whether the movement is actively executing, successfully completed, aborted due to an obstacle, faulted due to a system error, or cancelled by the MES scheduler.
in_progress|completed|aborted|faulted|cancelled

Categorical classification of the AGV movement event: load (picking up a carrier/part), transport (moving between locations), unload (depositing a carrier/part), charge (returning to charging station), idle (stationary with no task), fault (movement interrupted by exception).
load|transport|unload|charge|idle|fault
Reference to the manufacturing plant where this AGV movement occurred. Links to the plant master for facility-level reporting and fleet utilization analysis.
Primary key for agv_route
Timestamp when the route record was first created in the system.
Indicates whether the route can be traversed in both directions.
Numeric priority (1 = highest) used by the scheduler to rank routes.
Unique alphanumeric code assigned to the route for lookup and integration with MES.
Human‑readable name of the AGV route used for display and reporting.
Classification of the route purpose within the plant.
Timestamp of the most recent update to the route record.
Actual date and time at which assembly of the vehicle at this sequence position was completed on the production line, as recorded by the MES. Null until assembly is complete.
Actual date and time at which assembly of the vehicle at this sequence position commenced on the production line, as recorded by the MES. Null until assembly begins.
Code identifying the body style of the vehicle (e.g., sedan, SUV, truck, coupe, van). Influences stamping and body shop routing within the production sequence.

Unique surrogate identifier for the Just-in-Sequence (JIS) build sequence record in the Databricks Silver Layer. Primary key generated by the Apriso/Dassault MES sequencing module upon sequence creation.

Classification of the vehicle build purpose: 'retail' = customer-ordered retail unit; 'fleet' = fleet customer order; 'stock' = dealer stock build; 'pilot' = pre-production pilot build; 'homologation' = regulatory homologation unit; 'press' = media/press fleet unit.
retail|fleet|stock|pilot|homologation|press
Reference to the vehicle configuration record defining the model, trim, powertrain, and option codes for the vehicle to be assembled at this sequence position.
Date and time at which this build sequence record was first created in the MES sequencing module and ingested into the Databricks Silver Layer. Supports audit trail and data lineage.
Sales order number from SAP SD or Salesforce Automotive Cloud associated with this build sequence position, if the vehicle is built to a specific customer or dealer order. Null for stock builds.

Unique identifier of the dealer for whom this vehicle is being built, if applicable. Sourced from the dealer master in CDK Global DMS or Salesforce Automotive Cloud. Null for unallocated stock builds.

Three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code indicating the intended destination market for the vehicle. Determines homologation variant, regulatory compliance requirements (NHTSA, UNECE, CARB), and market-specific option content.
Paint color code for the vehicle exterior as specified in the build sequence. Drives paint shop scheduling, batch sequencing for color changeover optimization, and JIS paint material call-off.

Date and time at which the build sequence was frozen and locked for JIS supplier call-off. After this timestamp, sequence changes are restricted and require formal change control. Critical for JIS supplier synchronization.
Interior trim and upholstery color code for the vehicle. Used for JIS seat and interior component call-off to tier-1 suppliers.

Indicates whether the build sequence record has been frozen for JIS supplier call-off. When True, sequence changes are restricted and require formal change control approval. Directly linked to freeze_timestamp.

Indicates whether this vehicle has been flagged as a priority build (e.g., executive order, critical dealer allocation, regulatory compliance unit). Priority builds may override standard JIS sequencing rules.

Date and time at which the JIS supplier call-off message was transmitted for this sequence position. Triggers sequenced part delivery from tier-1 JIS suppliers. Critical for supply chain synchronization and OTD measurement.
Native sequence record identifier from the Apriso/Dassault MES sequencing module. Serves as the source system key for lineage and reconciliation between the Silver Layer and the operational MES.
Four-digit model year (MY) of the vehicle to be assembled at this sequence position. Determines applicable BOM revision, regulatory homologation requirements, and CAFE/EPA compliance targets.
Code representing the bundled option package (e.g., technology package, towing package, safety package) selected for the vehicle. Determines additional BOM components and JIS call-off requirements.
Calendar date on which the vehicle at this sequence position is planned to be assembled. Used for JIS supplier call-off scheduling and production planning in SAP PP.
Precise date and time at which assembly of the vehicle at this sequence position is planned to complete. Used for takt time validation and shift throughput planning.
Precise date and time at which assembly of the vehicle at this sequence position is planned to begin on the production line. Drives JIS call-off timing and AGV dispatch scheduling.
Reference to the manufacturing plant where this build sequence is executed. Links to the plant master record in the enterprise data model.

Classification of the vehicle powertrain to be assembled: ICE (Internal Combustion Engine), HEV (Hybrid Electric Vehicle), PHEV (Plug-in Hybrid Electric Vehicle), BEV (Battery Electric Vehicle), or FCEV (Fuel Cell Electric Vehicle). Drives line routing, tooling selection, and regulatory compliance checks.
ICE|HEV|PHEV|BEV|FCEV
Reference to the specific assembly or production line to which this build sequence is assigned. Drives AGV routing and JIS supplier call-off logic.

Foreign key linking to manufacturing.production_order. Business justification: Rename work_order_id to production_order_id to follow FK naming convention and link each build sequence to its parent production order.

Indicates whether this build sequence position has been placed on a quality hold, preventing progression to the next assembly stage. Triggered by MES quality gate failures or FMEA-driven stop conditions.

Ordered position number of this vehicle within the production run for the assigned line and shift. Drives JIS supplier call-off sequencing and AGV routing. Must be unique within a plant, line, shift, and planned build date combination.
Incremental revision counter tracking how many times this build sequence record has been modified since initial creation. Supports audit trail and change control compliance under IATF 16949.

Externally-known identifier for the production sequence set or run to which this record belongs, as generated by the MES sequencing module. Used for JIS call-off batch identification and supplier communication.

Current lifecycle state of the build sequence record within the MES workflow. 'planned' = sequence created but not yet released to shop floor; 'released' = released for production; 'in_progress' = vehicle currently being assembled; 'completed' = assembly finished; 'cancelled' = sequence removed from run; 'on_hold' = temporarily suspended pending resolution.
planned|released|in_progress|completed|cancelled|on_hold

Classification of the build sequence record indicating whether it is the original planned sequence, a revised sequence after change control, an emergency insertion, or a resequenced position due to line disruption.
initial|revised|emergency|resequenced
Reference to the production shift during which this build sequence is scheduled to execute. Determines labor allocation and JIS call-off windows.
Planned takt time in seconds allocated for assembly of the vehicle at this sequence position. Derived from the line rate and used for production pacing, WIP tracking, and OTD performance measurement.
Type of transmission to be installed in the vehicle at this sequence position. Drives drivetrain component JIS call-off and assembly station routing.
automatic|manual|CVT|DCT|single_speed
Code identifying the trim or grade level of the vehicle (e.g., base, mid, premium, sport). Determines option content, BOM variant, and JIS part call-off requirements.
Date and time of the most recent modification to this build sequence record, as recorded in the MES or Silver Layer. Used for incremental data loading, change detection, and audit compliance.
Alphanumeric code identifying the vehicle model (e.g., platform or nameplate code) to be assembled at this sequence position. Sourced from Teamcenter PLM product structure.

17-character Vehicle Identification Number (VIN) assigned to the vehicle at this sequence position, conforming to ISO 3779 and NHTSA standards. May be pre-assigned at sequence creation or stamped during body shop operations. Critical for build traceability and regulatory compliance.

Indicates whether AGV (Automated Guided Vehicle) systems are deployed at this build stage for material transport, vehicle body movement, or component sequencing. Drives AGV routing configuration and integration with SCADA and MES systems.

Classification of the degree of automation at this build stage: manual (operator-driven), semi-automated (operator-assisted machinery), fully-automated (machine-driven with minimal operator oversight), or robotic (AGV/robot-cell driven). Informs CapEx planning, maintenance scheduling, and OEE benchmarking.
manual|semi-automated|fully-automated|robotic

Unique surrogate identifier for each build stage record in the vehicle manufacturing process. Primary key for the build_stage reference master. [REFERENCE_LOOKUP role — canonical_skip_reason: This entity is a reference master defining standard build stages; per-role minimums for REFERENCE_LOOKUP are exempt, but all meaningful business attributes are still included for completeness.]
Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Stage‑level cost capture for capacity planning and cost of quality uses a finance cost center; the FK replaces the string code.

Timestamp when this build stage record was first created in the system. Provides audit trail for master data governance and change history tracking per IATF 16949 documented information control requirements.

The date from which this build stage definition record is valid and applicable for production use. Supports temporal versioning of the build stage master, enabling historical traceability of process changes and engineering change management.

The date until which this build stage definition record is valid. Null indicates the record is currently active with no planned expiry. Used for managing engineering changes, process revisions, and model-year transitions in the build stage master.

Standard energy consumption in kilowatt-hours (kWh) per vehicle unit processed through this build stage. Used for manufacturing sustainability reporting, carbon footprint calculation, and ISO 14001 environmental management compliance. Particularly significant for paint ovens and E-Coat tanks.

Indicates whether this build stage is designated as a quality gate checkpoint where vehicles must pass defined quality criteria before advancing to the next stage. Quality gates are mandatory hold points per IATF 16949 and APQP (Advanced Product Quality Planning) requirements.

Indicates whether vehicles failing quality checks at this build stage are eligible for rework and re-entry into the production flow, as opposed to being routed to scrap or offline repair. Drives rework routing logic in MES and quality management workflows.

The standard number of direct labor operators assigned to this build stage per shift under normal production conditions. Used for workforce planning, capacity balancing, and labor cost standard costing in SAP S/4HANA CO.

The native stage identifier as defined in the Apriso/Dassault MES system. Used for cross-system reconciliation between the lakehouse silver layer and the operational MES, ensuring traceability of production events back to the source system of record.

The physical or functional manufacturing area where this build stage is executed (e.g., Stamping Plant, Body Shop, Paint Shop, General Assembly, Chassis Line, PDI Bay). Maps to plant layout zones and is used for capacity planning and SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition) integration. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: Stamping|Body Shop|Paint Shop|E-Coat|General Assembly|Chassis Line|Trim Line|PDI Bay|Quality Gate|Logistics — promote to reference product]
Foreign key linking to manufacturing.production_line. Business justification: Build stages are defined per production line; adding production_line_id FK groups stages under their line.

Integer defining the sequential position of this build stage within the overall vehicle assembly process flow. Used to enforce JIS (Just-in-Sequence) ordering, production line scheduling, and WIP (Work in Progress) traceability. Lower values indicate earlier stages.

Indicates whether SPC (Statistical Process Control) monitoring is active for this build stage. When true, process parameters are continuously monitored against control limits and deviations trigger automated alerts in the MES and SAP QM systems per IATF 16949 requirements.

Short alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the build stage within the manufacturing process (e.g., STAMP, BODY, ECOAT, PAINT, TRIM1, CHAS, TRIM2, FINAL, PDI). Used as the business key in MES (Manufacturing Execution System) integrations and production reporting.

Detailed narrative description of the manufacturing activities, operations, and objectives performed at this build stage. Provides context for production engineers, quality auditors, and training documentation. Sourced from PLM and MES configuration documentation.

Full descriptive name of the build stage as used in production planning and reporting (e.g., Stamping, Body Shop, E-Coat, Paint, Trim-1, Chassis, Trim-2, Final Assembly, PDI — Pre-Delivery Inspection). Displayed in MES dashboards and production schedules.

Current lifecycle status of the build stage definition: active (in production use), inactive (temporarily not in use), pilot (under validation/trial), suspended (halted due to quality or safety issue), or decommissioned (permanently retired from the process). Controls whether the stage is available for new production orders.
active|inactive|pilot|suspended|decommissioned

Categorical classification of the build stage by its primary manufacturing function: assembly (joining components), fabrication (forming/stamping metal), coating (E-Coat/paint application), inspection (quality gate checks), testing (functional/NVH testing), or logistics (material staging/sequencing).
assembly|fabrication|coating|inspection|testing|logistics

The engineered standard cycle time for this build stage measured in seconds. Represents the designed takt-aligned duration for one vehicle unit to complete the stage under normal operating conditions. Used for production scheduling, OEE (Overall Equipment Effectiveness) calculation, and bottleneck analysis.

The customer-demand-driven takt time for this build stage in seconds, calculated as available production time divided by required production volume. Defines the rhythm of production and is used to balance line capacity and identify over/under-capacity stages.

Timestamp of the most recent update to this build stage record. Used for change detection in ETL pipelines, audit trail maintenance, and engineering change management workflows per IATF 16949 documented information control.
Unique surrogate identifier for each capacity plan record in the manufacturing domain. Primary key for the capacity_plan data product.
Date and time when this capacity plan record was first created in the system. Provides the audit trail creation anchor for data lineage and compliance purposes.

Current lifecycle state of the capacity plan record. 'draft' indicates work-in-progress; 'submitted' indicates pending approval; 'approved' indicates sign-off by S&OP leadership; 'active' indicates the operative plan driving production scheduling; 'superseded' indicates replaced by a newer version; 'archived' indicates historical record.
draft|submitted|approved|active|superseded|archived
Reference to the manufacturing plant for which this capacity plan is defined. Links to the manufacturing.plant master record.

Reference to the specific production line (e.g., final assembly line, body shop line, paint line) within the plant for which capacity is being planned. Links to the manufacturing.work_center or production line master.
Date and time when this capacity plan record was last modified. Tracks plan revisions through the S&OP cycle and supports change management auditing.
INT
Actual elapsed time in minutes from changeover start to completion. Core metric for SMED (Single-Minute Exchange of Die) analysis and OEE (Overall Equipment Effectiveness) calculations.
Unique surrogate identifier for each production line changeover event record in the manufacturing execution system.
Current lifecycle state of the changeover event as tracked in the MES (Manufacturing Execution System). Drives shop floor workflow and reporting.
scheduled|in_progress|completed|cancelled|aborted

Classification of the changeover event indicating the nature of the switch on the production line. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: model_mix_change|color_change|tooling_swap|line_retooling|powertrain_variant|body_style_change — promote to reference product]
model_mix_change|color_change|tooling_swap|line_retooling|powertrain_variant|body_style_change
Timestamp when the changeover record was first created in the MES (Manufacturing Execution System) or data platform. Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements.
INT
Planned duration of the changeover in minutes as defined in the production schedule. Baseline for SMED (Single-Minute Exchange of Die) improvement tracking.
Reference to the manufacturing plant where the changeover event occurred.
Reference to the specific production or assembly line on which the changeover was performed.

Number of vehicle units not produced due to the changeover downtime. Calculated as the difference between potential production capacity and actual output during the changeover window. Key metric for OEE (Overall Equipment Effectiveness) and capacity planning.
Primary key for the ComplianceCertification association

The timestamp when the downtime event record was first created in the source system (MES, SAP PM, or SCADA). Represents the audit creation time, distinct from start_timestamp which is the actual business event time. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the maintenance_cost_local field (e.g., USD, EUR, MXN, CNY). Required for multi-plant, multi-currency cost consolidation in global automotive manufacturing operations.

Primary classification of the downtime event type. 'mechanical_failure' covers equipment breakdowns; 'tooling_change' covers die/tool swap activities; 'material_shortage' covers JIT/JIS supply disruptions; 'quality_hold' covers production stops due to quality issues; 'scheduled_maintenance' covers planned PM activities; 'changeover' covers model or variant changeover activities. Drives OEE availability loss categorization.
mechanical_failure|tooling_change|material_shortage|quality_hold|scheduled_maintenance|changeover
Unique surrogate identifier for each downtime event record in the manufacturing execution system. Primary key for the downtime_event data product.

Indicates whether the downtime event was planned (scheduled maintenance, changeover, tooling change per production schedule) or unplanned (unexpected breakdown, quality hold, material shortage). Critical for separating planned vs. unplanned OEE availability losses.
planned|unplanned

Total elapsed duration of the downtime event in minutes, calculated as the difference between end_timestamp and start_timestamp. Stored as a business field for direct use in OEE (Overall Equipment Effectiveness) availability calculations and SCADA-integrated downtime reporting. Null if the event has not yet ended.
The exact date and time when the downtime event ended and production resumed, as recorded by the MES or SCADA system. Null if the event is still active. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
Reference to the specific machine, robot, AGV (Automated Guided Vehicle), or equipment asset that experienced the downtime. Maps to SAP PM Equipment master record.

Externally-known, human-readable business identifier for the downtime event, typically generated by the MES (Manufacturing Execution System) or SAP PM (Plant Maintenance) module. Format: DT-{YYYY}-{NNNNNN}. Used for cross-system referencing and shop floor communication.

Current lifecycle status of the downtime event record. 'open' indicates the event is active and unresolved; 'in_progress' indicates a repair or corrective action is underway; 'resolved' indicates the root cause has been addressed; 'closed' indicates the event is fully documented and closed; 'cancelled' indicates the event was logged in error.
open|in_progress|resolved|closed|cancelled

Standardized code identifying the specific failure mode that caused the downtime event, aligned with the FMEA (Failure Mode and Effects Analysis) failure mode library. Examples: electrical fault, hydraulic leak, sensor failure, conveyor jam. Enables FMEA-driven root cause trending and PPAP (Production Part Approval Process) corrective action tracking.

Indicates whether this downtime event is a recurrence of a previously recorded failure on the same equipment or work center within a defined lookback period (typically 30 days). True = repeat failure; False = first occurrence. Used to identify chronic equipment issues requiring escalated corrective action under IATF 16949 Section 10.2.

Indicates whether the downtime event involved a safety incident, near-miss, or safety-critical equipment failure (e.g., AGV collision, robot safety stop, lockout/tagout activation). True = safety-related; False = non-safety. Triggers mandatory safety reporting and OSHA/DOT compliance escalation workflows.

The timestamp when the downtime event record was most recently modified in the source system, such as when resolution notes were added, status was updated, or cost data was posted. Used for incremental data pipeline processing and audit trail in the Silver layer. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
confidential

Total direct maintenance cost incurred to resolve the downtime event, including labor, spare parts, and external service costs, expressed in the plant's local currency. Sourced from SAP PM actual cost settlement. Used for cost-of-downtime analysis and CapEx vs. OpEx maintenance budget reporting.

The percentage of scheduled production time lost due to this downtime event, calculated as (duration_minutes / scheduled_production_time_minutes) × 100. Represents the availability loss component of the OEE (Overall Equipment Effectiveness) metric for the affected work center during the event period. Stored as a business field for direct use in OEE dashboards.
Reference to the manufacturing plant where the downtime event occurred. Corresponds to the SAP Plant (Werk) organizational unit.
Reference to the production line (e.g., stamping line, body shop line, paint line, final assembly line) affected by the downtime event. Enables line-level OEE and throughput impact analysis.

Number of vehicle units or production units lost due to the downtime event, based on the planned production rate for the affected work center. Used to quantify the production order impact and schedule recovery requirements.
Reference to the SAP PP Production Order (Fertigungsauftrag) that was active or impacted at the time of the downtime event. Used to quantify production order impact and schedule deviation.

Free-text field capturing the maintenance technician's description of the actions taken to resolve the downtime event and restore production. Complements corrective_action_code with detailed narrative. Stored in the Silver layer for use in AI/ML-based predictive maintenance model training.

Standardized code identifying the confirmed root cause of the downtime event after investigation, aligned with the SAP PM cause code catalog. Distinct from failure_mode_code which captures the symptom; root_cause_code captures the underlying reason (e.g., inadequate lubrication, worn tooling, incorrect setup, supplier part defect).

The exact date and time when the downtime event began, as recorded by the MES or SCADA system. This is the principal real-world event time used for duration calculation and shift-level reporting. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

Reference to the specific work center or production cell where the downtime event was recorded. Maps to SAP PP Work Center (Arbeitsplatz) or MES work station definition. Critical for OEE (Overall Equipment Effectiveness) analysis at the work center level.
Business‑defined unique code used to reference the calendar in planning systems.
Human‑readable name of the calendar (e.g., "2025 Production Schedule").
Date‑time when the calendar record was first created in the system.
Primary key for factory_calendar
Identifier of the manufacturing plant to which the calendar applies.
Date‑time of the most recent update to the calendar record.

Indicates whether this component is backflushed (automatically goods-issued upon production order confirmation) rather than requiring a discrete goods movement transaction. True = backflush; False = manual goods issue required. Common for bulk and low-value components.

Hierarchical depth of this component within the multi-level BOM structure. Level 0 is the finished vehicle; level 1 is a major assembly; deeper levels represent sub-assemblies and individual parts. Used for BOM explosion and cost rollup.

Current lifecycle status of this BOM component line. 'superseded' indicates the part has been replaced by an alternate; 'pending_approval' indicates the component is awaiting PPAP (Production Part Approval Process) sign-off before use in production.
active|superseded|obsolete|pending_approval|on_hold

Classification of the BOM item indicating how it is sourced and consumed in the manufacturing process. 'phantom' denotes a logical grouping with no physical stock; 'bulk_material' denotes items issued without discrete picking. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: raw_material|purchased_part|sub_assembly|phantom|co_product|bulk_material — promote to reference product]
raw_material|purchased_part|sub_assembly|phantom|co_product|bulk_material
Timestamp when this BOM component record was first created in the source system (SAP or Teamcenter PLM). Provides audit trail for BOM change history and regulatory traceability.
Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the standard cost value (e.g., 'USD', 'EUR', 'JPY'). Enables multi-currency BOM cost analysis across global manufacturing plants.

Date after which this BOM component line is no longer valid and should be excluded from production builds. Null indicates an open-ended validity. Supports EOP (End of Production) transitions and engineering change cutover.

Date from which this BOM component line is valid and should be included in production builds. Supports engineering change management and model year (MY) transitions. Components before this date are not called off.

Reference to the Engineering Change Notice (ECN) or Engineering Change Order (ECO) that introduced or last modified this BOM component line. Provides full traceability of design changes from PLM through to the manufacturing BOM.

Numeric sequence defining the order in which this component is installed relative to other components at the same work center. Critical for JIS (Just-in-Sequence) material call-offs and shop floor assembly instruction generation.
Timestamp of the most recent modification to this BOM component record in the source system. Used for incremental data loading, change detection, and BOM audit trail compliance.

Code identifying the specific manufacturing process step (e.g., STAMP-001, BODY-WELD-045, PAINT-CURE-010, ASSY-TORQUE-120) within the routing. Aligns with SAP PP routing operations.
Reference to the SAP PP production order under which this shop floor event was generated. Links the event to the scheduled manufacturing work order.

Outcome of the quality check associated with this event. Determines whether the vehicle unit proceeds to the next station, requires rework, or is scrapped. Feeds into IATF 16949 quality records and PPM reporting.
