Reference to the production shift during which this event was recorded. Enables shift-level OEE and throughput analysis.
Unique surrogate identifier for each shop floor event record generated by MES, PLC, or SCADA systems during production operations.
Unique code of the specific work station or assembly point within the production line where the event was triggered. Enables station-level cycle time and downtime analysis.

Timestamp of the most recent update to this shop floor event record in the Silver layer (e.g., when quality result or hold status was updated post-event). Supports change data capture and audit compliance.
Upper statistical process control limit for the measured value at this station. Used in SPC (Statistical Process Control) to detect process drift and trigger quality holds.
Reference to the vehicle unit being processed at the time of this event. Enables full build traceability from stamping through final assembly per NHTSA VIN requirements.
Reference to the SAP PP/MES work center (station, cell, or line segment) where this event occurred. Identifies the physical production resource.

The unique serial number of the high-voltage traction battery pack installed in this vehicle (applicable to HEV, PHEV, BEV). Null for ICE vehicles. Critical for EV battery genealogy, warranty, and end-of-life regulatory compliance.
Actual timestamp when the body shop stage was completed and the body-in-white was released to the paint shop. Null if stage not yet completed.
Actual timestamp when the vehicle body-in-white (BIW) entered the body shop for welding and assembly. Key milestone for build genealogy and stage cycle time tracking.
The body style classification of the vehicle being built. Used for production line routing, tooling selection, and regulatory homologation grouping.
sedan|suv|truck|van|coupe|convertible

The specific BOM (Bill of Materials) version or engineering change level used to build this vehicle. Captured at build time for genealogy and recall traceability. Links to Siemens Teamcenter PLM BOM management.

Actual date and time when the vehicle build was completed at the final assembly stage and signed off for PDI (Pre-Delivery Inspection). Null if the build is still in progress. Used for cycle time, throughput, and SOP/EOP milestone tracking.

The Just-in-Sequence (JIS) production sequence number assigned to this vehicle on the assembly line. Determines the order in which vehicles are built and parts are delivered to the line. Critical for JIS/JIT supply chain synchronization.
Foreign key linking to manufacturing.build_stage. Business justification: Vehicle build references its current build stage; replace string column with FK to build_stage for normalization.

Actual date and time when the vehicle build process commenced at the first production stage (typically body-in-white or stamping entry). Principal business event timestamp for the build lifecycle. Used for cycle time calculation and OTD (On-Time Delivery) analysis.

Current lifecycle status of the vehicle build record. Drives shop floor workflow, MES gating, and production reporting. 'on_hold' indicates a quality or material hold; 'rework' indicates a defect requiring corrective action before completion.
in_progress|completed|on_hold|rework|scrapped|cancelled

Classification of the vehicle build type: standard (full local assembly), CKD (Completely Knocked Down – assembled from imported kits), SKD (Semi Knocked Down), pilot (pre-SOP trial build), or prototype (engineering validation). Affects BOM, duty classification, and regulatory reporting.
standard|ckd|skd|pilot|prototype

Timestamp when this vehicle build record was first created in the MES/data platform. Represents the audit trail creation event, distinct from the build_start_timestamp which is the actual shop floor event time.

Result of the automated end-of-line (EOL) functional test performed on the completed vehicle, covering powertrain, brakes, ADAS, and electrical systems. Distinct from quality_gate_status which covers visual/dimensional inspection.
pass|fail|retest_required
The unique serial number of the engine unit installed in this vehicle during chassis assembly. Critical for powertrain genealogy, warranty traceability, and recall management.
Actual timestamp when the final assembly stage was completed and the vehicle was released for PDI (Pre-Delivery Inspection). Null if stage not yet completed.
Actual timestamp when the vehicle entered the final assembly stage for fluids, wheels, glass, and end-of-line checks.

Indicates whether this vehicle build is currently under a production hold (True = on hold). A hold may be triggered by a quality non-conformance, missing parts, engineering change, or safety concern. Drives MES gating to prevent further assembly until resolved.

Coded reason for the production hold applied to this vehicle build (e.g., QUALITY_DEFECT, MISSING_PART, ECN_CHANGE, SAFETY_CONCERN). Null if hold_flag is False. The automotive model year (MY) designation for the vehicle being built (e.g., 2025). Determines applicable regulatory standards, BOM revision, and homologation requirements. Distinct from the calendar year of production.
Reference to the operator team or crew responsible for executing this vehicle build. Used for workforce productivity and quality traceability.

The manufacturer's paint color code applied to this vehicle during the paint stage (e.g., G1W – Super White, 040 – Classic White). Used for paint shop scheduling, color sequencing optimization, and customer order matching.
Actual timestamp when the paint stage was completed and the vehicle body was released to the trim/general assembly line. Null if stage not yet completed.
Actual timestamp when the vehicle body entered the paint shop for priming, painting, and clear-coat application.
Reference to the manufacturing plant where this vehicle was assembled. Enables plant-level production reporting and capacity analysis.

Classification of the vehicle powertrain technology being assembled: ICE (Internal Combustion Engine), HEV (Hybrid Electric Vehicle), PHEV (Plug-in Hybrid Electric Vehicle), BEV (Battery Electric Vehicle), or FCEV (Fuel Cell Electric Vehicle). Drives assembly line routing, tooling, and EPA/CARB emissions compliance tracking.
ICE|HEV|PHEV|BEV|FCEV
Reference to the SAP PP production order that authorized and scheduled this vehicle build. Links the build event to the manufacturing planning hierarchy.

Result of the end-of-line quality gate inspection for this vehicle build. 'conditional_pass' indicates the vehicle passed with minor deviations requiring dealer rectification. Drives release-to-shipping authorization.
pass|fail|conditional_pass|pending

Number of rework operations performed on this vehicle build. A count greater than zero indicates quality issues encountered during assembly. Used for PPM (Parts Per Million) defect rate calculation and FMEA analysis.

Indicates whether this vehicle build has been flagged for rework due to a detected defect or non-conformance (True = rework required). Distinct from hold_flag; a vehicle can be in rework while not on hold.
The planned calendar date on which this vehicle was scheduled to be built per the production plan (MRP/MES schedule). Used to measure schedule adherence and production plan vs. actual variance.
Reference to the production shift during which this vehicle build was executed. Supports shift-level throughput and quality analysis.
The unique serial number of the transmission unit installed in this vehicle. Used for drivetrain genealogy, warranty claims, and component-level recall traceability.
Timestamp of the most recent update to this vehicle build record. Used for incremental data pipeline processing, audit trails, and detecting stale records in the Silver layer.

Internal product/model code identifying the vehicle nameplate and variant being built (e.g., F150-XLT-4WD). Maps to the PLM product structure in Siemens Teamcenter. Used for BOM resolution and build sequence planning.

The globally unique 17-character Vehicle Identification Number (VIN) assigned to this vehicle unit at body-in-white or VIN stamping stage. Conforms to ISO 3779 / NHTSA VIN standard. SSOT for vehicle-level traceability across manufacturing, sales, and after-sales domains.
Foreign key linking to vehicle.vin_registry. Business justification: VIN Registration Integration needed for warranty, recall, and regulatory reporting linking build record to VIN registry.

Indicates whether this WIP item has been routed to a rework station for corrective operations (True) or is following the standard production flow (False). Used to track rework rates and associated costs.

Date and time when this WIP inventory record was last modified in the source MES system. Used for change detection and incremental Silver Layer ingestion.

internal

Unique surrogate identifier for each WIP inventory snapshot or movement record on the shop floor. Primary key for this entity.

Human-readable, externally visible business identifier for this WIP inventory record, generated by the MES (Manufacturing Execution System). Used on shop floor traveler documents and in MES dashboards.

Current lifecycle status of the WIP item on the shop floor. 'in_process' = actively being worked on; 'on_hold' = paused pending resolution; 'awaiting_inspection' = queued for quality gate; 'scrapped' = condemned and removed from flow; 'completed' = operation finished; 'rework' = returned for corrective operations.
in_process|on_hold|awaiting_inspection|scrapped|completed|rework
confidential

Reference to the specific work center (Arbeitsplatz) on the shop floor where the WIP item is currently being processed or staged. Supports JIS sequencing and real-time WIP location tracking.
Indicates whether this work center is integrated with AGV (Automated Guided Vehicle) systems for automated material delivery and WIP transport. Drives AGV routing configuration in the MES.

Degree of automation at this work center: fully_automated (no human intervention), highly_automated (minimal human oversight), semi_automated (human-assisted), manual (entirely human-operated), or collaborative (human-robot collaboration). Informs CapEx planning and Industry 4.0 transformation roadmap.
fully_automated|highly_automated|semi_automated|manual|collaborative
Total available production hours per day for this work center, accounting for planned shift schedules and scheduled breaks. Used in SAP PP capacity requirements planning (CRP) and MES scheduling.

Capacity classification of the work center: bottleneck (constraining throughput of the line), standard (normal capacity), buffer (excess capacity used to absorb variation), or flexible (can be redeployed across lines). Critical for Theory of Constraints analysis and production scheduling.
bottleneck|standard|buffer|flexible
Date on which this work center was officially commissioned and made available for production use. Used for asset age tracking, depreciation calculation, and maintenance lifecycle management.

Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Work‑center cost tracking for OEE and labor cost reporting uses a finance cost center; replacing cost_center_code with cost_center_id is standard practice.
Timestamp when this work center master record was first created in the data platform. Used for data lineage, audit trail, and record lifecycle management.
ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the cost rates (machine_rate_per_hour, labor_rate_per_hour) associated with this work center (e.g., USD, EUR, JPY).

Standard cycle time in seconds for this work center to complete one unit of work. Used in production scheduling, capacity calculation, and bottleneck analysis. Represents the designed throughput rate per station.

Date on which this work center was or is planned to be permanently decommissioned and removed from production service. Nullable for active stations. Used for asset lifecycle planning and capacity forecasting.

Identifier of the production supervisor or team leader responsible for this work center. Used for accountability tracking, escalation routing, and workforce management integration with SuccessFactors.

Rated energy consumption of this work center in kilowatts (kW) under standard operating conditions. Used for energy management, sustainability reporting, and ISO 14001 environmental compliance tracking.
Physical floor area occupied by this work center in square meters. Used for facility layout planning, ergonomic assessments, and plant capacity management.

Foreign key linking to asset.functional_location. Business justification: Required for Work Center Maintenance Planning reports linking each work center to its functional location in the plant hierarchy.

Indicates whether this work center has been identified as a production bottleneck constraining overall line throughput. Bottleneck stations receive priority in capacity planning, maintenance scheduling, and continuous improvement initiatives.

Indicates whether this work center participates in JIS (Just-in-Sequence) production sequencing. When true, the MES enforces strict vehicle sequence delivery to this station to support mixed-model assembly.

Indicates whether this work center serves as a quality gate (inspection checkpoint) in the production flow. Quality gate stations require SPC (Statistical Process Control) data capture and may hold WIP pending quality approval.
DECIMAL(10,2)
confidential
Standard direct labor cost rate per hour (in local currency) for this work center. Used in production order costing, standard cost roll-up, and labor efficiency variance reporting.
Date of the most recent calibration or measurement system verification performed on this work center's tooling and gauges. Required for IATF 16949 Clause 7.1.5 measurement system compliance.
Timestamp of the most recent update to this work center master record. Used for change tracking, data freshness monitoring, and incremental ETL processing in the Databricks lakehouse.
Textual description of the physical location of the work center within the plant (e.g., 'Building A, Bay 3, Row 5'). Supports maintenance routing, safety inspections, and shop floor navigation.
DECIMAL(10,2)
confidential
Standard machine cost rate per hour (in local currency) for this work center, used in production order costing, standard cost calculation, and variance analysis in SAP CO.

Maintenance strategy applied to this work center: preventive (scheduled interval-based), predictive (condition-monitoring-based), corrective (repair after failure), or condition_based (triggered by sensor thresholds). Drives SAP PM maintenance planning.
preventive|predictive|corrective|condition_based

Standard mean time between failures (MTBF) in hours for this work center, representing the expected average operational time between unplanned breakdowns. Used in reliability analysis, maintenance planning, and OEE (Overall Equipment Effectiveness) benchmarking.

Standard mean time to repair (MTTR) in hours for this work center, representing the average time required to restore the station to operational status after a failure. Used in maintenance planning and availability calculations.

Native work center identifier in the Apriso/Dassault MES system. Used for cross-system traceability between the lakehouse silver layer and the operational MES for shop floor execution and WIP (Work in Progress) tracking.
Scheduled date for the next calibration or measurement system verification at this work center. Triggers maintenance work orders in SAP PM and quality alerts in the MES when approaching or overdue.
Number of production shifts per day this work center operates (typically 1, 2, or 3). Used in daily capacity calculation and workforce planning.
Standard number of direct labor workers assigned to this work center per shift. Used for workforce planning, labor cost allocation, and ergonomic assessment.
DECIMAL(6,3)
confidential
Manufacturing overhead absorption rate as a percentage applied to this work center's direct costs for product costing and standard cost calculation in SAP CO.
SAP plant code identifying the manufacturing facility where this work center is physically located. Aligns with SAP S/4HANA organizational structure for production planning.

Identifier of the PLC (Programmable Logic Controller) node associated with this work center in the shop floor control network. Used for real-time production control integration and SCADA data correlation.

Manufacturing process category to which this work center belongs, reflecting the major shop segment (e.g., stamping, body shop, paint, final assembly, powertrain). Code identifying the production line (e.g., stamping, body shop, paint, final assembly) to which this work center belongs. Supports JIS (Just-in-Sequence) scheduling and MES line-level reporting.
Native work center identifier in SAP S/4HANA PP module. Used for cross-system reconciliation between the lakehouse and SAP for production order routing, capacity planning, and cost center allocation.

Identifier of the SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition) node associated with this work center. Enables real-time monitoring, alarm management, and production data acquisition from the shop floor.
Standard setup/changeover time in minutes required to prepare this work center for a new production run or model variant. Used in SAP PP capacity planning and MES work order scheduling.

Code referencing the shift schedule model assigned to this work center (e.g., 1-shift, 2-shift, 3-shift, weekend shift). Determines available production windows for capacity planning and MES scheduling.

SAP PP standard value key (e.g., SAP1, SAP2) defining which standard values (setup, machine, labor, teardown times) are relevant for this work center in routing operations. Governs how production order times are calculated.

Takt time in seconds representing the rate at which vehicles must be produced to meet customer demand. Calculated as available production time divided by customer demand rate. Used for JIS (Just-in-Sequence) line balancing and MES pacing.
Standard teardown/cleanup time in minutes required after completing a production run at this work center. Included in total station time calculations for capacity planning.

SAP PP work center category classifying the primary resource type: machine (machine-driven capacity), labor (labor-driven capacity), machine_labor (both machine and labor capacity), or external (subcontracted operation). Determines how capacity and costing are calculated in SAP.
machine|labor|machine_labor|external

Externally-known alphanumeric code that uniquely identifies the work center across MES, SAP PP, and SCADA systems. Used as the business key in cross-system integration (e.g., Apriso/Dassault MES work center identifier).
Detailed textual description of the work center's function, scope of operations, and any special capabilities or constraints relevant to production planning and scheduling.
Unique surrogate identifier for the work center (station) record within the manufacturing data platform. Primary key for the work_center master entity.
Human-readable name of the work center station (e.g., 'Body Framing Station 04', 'Final Torque Assembly Line 2'). Used in shop floor displays, MES dashboards, and production reporting.

Current lifecycle status of the work center: active (in production use), inactive (temporarily not in use), under_maintenance (scheduled or unscheduled maintenance), decommissioned (permanently retired), or planned (not yet commissioned). Drives MES scheduling eligibility and capacity planning.
active|inactive|under_maintenance|decommissioned|planned

Classification of the work center by its operational mode: manual (human-operated), automated (machine-driven without robotics), robotic (robot arm/AGV-integrated), semi_automated (human-assisted automation), inspection (quality gate), or rework (defect correction station). manual|automated|robotic|semi_automated|inspection|rework

Standard contracted annual mileage allowance included in the base product terms for lease and PCP products. Excess mileage is charged at the excess_mileage_rate.

The Annual Percentage Rate (APR) for this finance product, expressed as a decimal. Mandatory regulatory disclosure metric representing the true cost of credit including fees. Required under Consumer Credit Directive.
Fixed fee charged to the customer at the inception of the finance agreement. Included in APR calculations and disclosed in pre-contractual information.

The guaranteed future value (GFV) or balloon payment expressed as a percentage of the vehicle's on-the-road price. Applicable to PCP (Personal Contract Purchase) and balloon finance products. Null for standard loans.
Reference rate index to which a variable rate product is linked (e.g., SOFR, EURIBOR, Bank of England Base Rate). Null for fixed-rate products.
Timestamp when this finance product record was first created in the data lakehouse. Used for audit trail and data governance purposes.
Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code in which the finance product is denominated (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Determines the currency of all monetary terms associated with this product.
The commission rate payable to the dealer for introducing this finance product, expressed as a decimal. Subject to FCA discretionary commission arrangement (DCA) rules. Confidential commercial term.
The date on which this finance product was formally discontinued and removed from the active product catalog. Null for active products.
Fee charged to the customer for settling the finance agreement before the contracted end date. Subject to statutory rebate rules under the Consumer Credit Act.
The date from which this finance product is available for new originations. Used in product eligibility date-range checks during quote generation.
The date after which this finance product is no longer available for new originations. Null indicates the product is open-ended with no planned end date.
Maximum age of the vehicle in years at the time of finance origination. Used to restrict certain products to new or nearly-new vehicles and to manage residual value risk.
Charge per unit of distance (mile or kilometre) for mileage exceeding the contracted annual mileage allowance. Applicable to lease and PCP products. Null for loan products.
The identifier for this finance product in the originating source system (e.g., SAP SD material number, Salesforce product ID). Used for cross-system reconciliation and data lineage.

FCA-defined product category classification for regulated credit products (e.g., 'Hire Purchase', 'Conditional Sale', 'Personal Contract Purchase', 'Finance Lease'). Required for FCA regulatory reporting.
The distribution channel through which this finance product is offered. Determines eligibility rules, commission structures, and regulatory disclosure requirements.
Primary key for finance_product
Indicates whether this finance product is eligible for government or manufacturer EV purchase incentives (e.g., Plug-in Car Grant, IRA EV tax credit). Used in incentive program eligibility logic.

Indicates whether this finance product is a regulated credit agreement subject to consumer credit legislation and conduct of business rules. Drives mandatory disclosure and affordability assessment requirements.
Fee charged per late payment event under this finance product. Must be disclosed in the pre-contractual information and is subject to FCA fairness rules.
The date on which this finance product was first made commercially available to dealers and customers. Used in product performance analytics and vintage analysis.
ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the market in which this finance product is offered. Finance products are market-specific due to regulatory and tax differences.
Maximum number of basis points by which a dealer is permitted to mark up the standard rate when quoting to a customer. Regulated under FCA DCA rules. Confidential commercial term.
Maximum deposit percentage allowed under this finance product. Prevents over-capitalisation and ensures the product remains within its intended credit structure.
Maximum principal amount that can be financed under this product. Caps the exposure per agreement and is used in credit risk and underwriting rules.
Maximum contract duration in months for this finance product. Defines the upper bound for repayment schedules and residual value calculations.
Unit of distance measurement used for mileage allowance and excess mileage charges. Varies by market (miles in UK/US, km in continental Europe).
Minimum required deposit (down payment) as a percentage of the vehicle's on-the-road price, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.10 for 10%). Used in affordability and eligibility checks.
Minimum principal amount that can be financed under this product. Used in eligibility checks during quote generation and order capture in SAP SD and Salesforce.
Minimum contract duration in months for this finance product. Used in eligibility validation and product suitability assessments.
Indicates whether this finance product is available for new vehicles, used/pre-owned vehicles, or both. Drives product filtering in dealer quoting systems.
The stated annual nominal interest rate (flat rate) for this finance product, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.0699 for 6.99%). Used in payment schedule calculations.
Frequency at which regular repayments are due under this finance product. Monthly is standard for retail automotive finance; quarterly or annual may apply to fleet or commercial products.
Number of rental payments collected in advance at the start of the agreement (e.g., 3 months in advance for a lease). Common in fleet and business lease products.
Business segment category for the finance product, distinguishing retail consumer finance from fleet, commercial, dealer stock, or wholesale financing arrangements.
Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the finance product within the automotive finance product catalog. Used in SAP SD and Salesforce Automotive Cloud for product referencing.
Detailed narrative description of the finance product, including its key features, target customer segment, and commercial positioning. Used in dealer training materials and product documentation.
Human-readable commercial name of the finance product (e.g., 'Standard Auto Loan', 'Balloon Finance Plan', 'Lease with Maintenance'). Used in dealer-facing and customer-facing materials.
Name or identifier of the business owner responsible for this finance product's commercial performance, pricing, and compliance. Used in governance and escalation workflows.
Current lifecycle status of the finance product. Controls whether the product is available for new originations, under review, or retired from the product catalog.

Classification of the finance product by its fundamental structure. Determines the financial mechanics, regulatory treatment, and accounting classification. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: loan|lease|balloon|hire_purchase|fleet_finance|subscription|pcp|pcm — promote to reference product]
The margin in basis points added to the benchmark rate index for variable-rate products. For example, a margin of 150 bps over EURIBOR. Null for fixed-rate products.
Indicates whether the interest rate for this finance product is fixed for the full term, variable (linked to a benchmark rate), capped, or stepped over the contract period.

The primary regulatory framework governing this finance product (e.g., 'Consumer Credit Act 1974', 'Consumer Credit Directive 2008/48/EC', 'Regulation Z / TILA'). Determines disclosure and conduct obligations.
Estimated residual value of the vehicle at the end of the finance term, expressed as a percentage of the original vehicle price. Used in lease and PCP product pricing and risk modelling.
Code identifying the operational system of record from which this finance product definition originates (e.g., 'SAP_SD', 'SALESFORCE_AC', 'DEALER_FMS'). Used for data lineage and reconciliation.
Indicates whether the finance product is subsidised by the manufacturer (subvented rate), the dealer, or is unsubsidised. Subvented products are funded by the OEM to support vehicle sales incentives.
The rate subsidy provided by the manufacturer or dealer to reduce the customer-facing APR below the standard market rate. Expressed as a decimal. Confidential commercial term.

Classification of the lender by institutional type. Captive lenders are OEM-owned finance arms (e.g., GMAC, BMW Financial Services); banks and credit unions are third-party. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: captive|bank|credit_union|independent_finance|leasing_company|government — promote to reference product]
Maximum vehicle financing loan amount (in lender's primary currency) that the lender will approve per transaction. Caps deal size for risk management purposes.

Maximum loan-to-value ratio (expressed as a percentage) the lender will finance relative to the vehicle's MSRP or appraised value. A value of 110.00 means the lender will finance up to 110% of vehicle value (including negative equity).
Maximum financing term in months that the lender offers for vehicle purchase loans (e.g., 84 months). Longer terms reduce monthly payments but increase total interest cost.
Maximum age of the vehicle (in years from model year) that the lender will finance. Older vehicles typically carry higher default risk and are excluded by prime lenders.
Maximum odometer reading (in miles or kilometers per lender's market standard) of a used vehicle that the lender will finance. High-mileage vehicles are excluded from many prime lending programs.
Minimum vehicle financing loan amount (in lender's primary currency) that the lender will approve. Used to filter lender eligibility during deal structuring in the F&I (Finance and Insurance) office.
Minimum financing term in months that the lender offers for vehicle purchase loans (e.g., 12 months). Used to filter lender eligibility for short-term financing requests.
Date on which the next scheduled compliance and performance review of the lender is due. Drives compliance calendar and audit scheduling workflows.
Date on which the lender was formally onboarded and activated in the OEM's financing ecosystem, including DMS integration, portal access provisioning, and compliance verification completion.
Self-referencing identifier for the parent lender entity, enabling hierarchical lender group structures (e.g., a regional subsidiary referencing its national parent captive finance company).

Numeric ranking (1 = highest preference) indicating the OEM's or dealer group's preferred routing order for financing applications. Lower rank lenders receive first-look submission priority in the dealer's F&I workflow.

Official government-issued legal entity registration or charter number for the lending institution (e.g., NMLS ID in the USA, BaFin registration in Germany). Required for regulatory compliance verification.

SSOT for vehicle nameplate definitions — the commercial brand identity of a vehicle line (e.g., F-150, Silverado, Camry, Mustang). Owns nameplate code, brand affiliation, vehicle segment classification (car/truck/SUV/commercial), powertrain family (ICE/HEV/PHEV/EV), market positioning tier, global vs. regional availability flag, nameplate lifecycle status (active/discontinued), SOP (Start of Production) year, EOP (End of Production) year, and nameplate heritage lineage. This is the root anchor for all program and model year planning.

before.description: Defines the annual program plan for each nameplate by MY (Model Year). Captures MY designation, program code, program phase (concept/development/launch/production/runout), SOP date, EOP date, target plant assignments, planned production volume, regulatory homologation targets (CAFE, WLTP, EPA), program budget envelope (CapEx), and program manager reference. Acts as the planning backbone linking nameplate definitions to annual production and sales programs.

Defines commercially available option packages and standalone options that can be ordered on a vehicle (e.g., Technology Package, Tow Package, Panoramic Roof, Premium Audio). Captures package code, package name, package type (group/standalone/accessory), MSRP uplift price, content description, constraint rules (requires/excludes other packages), availability by trim level, market availability regions, and lifecycle status. Distinct from engineering feature definitions — this is the commercial catalog layer.

Defines the commercial trim hierarchy for a model year program (e.g., Base, XL, XLT, Lariat, Platinum, Limited). Captures trim code, trim name, trim rank/order within the nameplate hierarchy, standard feature set description, MSRP base price, market segment positioning, availability regions, and active/inactive lifecycle status. Trim levels are the primary commercial differentiation layer between the nameplate and individual option packages.

Reference catalog of commercial body style definitions available across nameplates (e.g., 2-door coupe, 4-door sedan, crew cab pickup, extended cab, SUV 3-row, cargo van). Captures body style code, body style name, door count, seating capacity, cargo volume, roof type, body structure classification (unibody/body-on-frame), and applicable vehicle segment. Used in SKU construction, order management, and regulatory homologation classification.

Commercial color catalog defining all available exterior paint colors and interior color/material combinations offered across model year programs. Captures color code, color name, color type (exterior/interior), color family, paint technology (solid/metallic/pearl/matte), interior material type (cloth/leather/synthetic/premium), availability by trim level, MSRP uplift (for premium colors), regional availability, and active/discontinued status. Used in SKU configuration, order management, and production scheduling.

Defines market-specific homologation variants of a base SKU required to meet local regulatory standards (UNECE, FMVSS, ADR, etc.). Captures homologation variant code, base SKU reference, target market/country, regulatory standard (UNECE/FMVSS/ADR/CARB), required modification description, homologation approval number, approval authority, approval date, expiry date, and variant status. Bridges the commercial product catalog to the compliance domain's regulatory approval records.
Master reference table for market. Referenced by market_id.

Defines the feature-to-market availability matrix — which SKUs, trim levels, and option packages are available in which geographic markets and sales channels. Captures market code, sales channel (retail/fleet/government/export), availability status (available/restricted/not-offered), launch date, withdrawal date, homologation approval status, import duty classification, and CKD/SKD (Completely Knocked Down / Semi Knocked Down) assembly flag. Critical for order management, dealer ordering systems, and regulatory compliance.

SSOT for MSRP (Manufacturer Suggested Retail Price) price books by model year, market, and currency. Captures price book code, effective date range, market/region code, currency code, price book status (draft/approved/published/superseded), approval authority, and publication date. The price book is the container for all MSRP pricing entries and governs which prices are active for dealer ordering and consumer-facing communications.

Individual MSRP (Manufacturer Suggested Retail Price) pricing entries within a price book. Captures the SKU or option package being priced, base MSRP amount, destination charge, gas guzzler tax (if applicable), effective start and end dates, price type (base vehicle/option/package/accessory), and prior price for change tracking. Enables dealer invoice generation, consumer window sticker production, and competitive pricing analysis.

SSOT for vehicle nameplate definitions — the commercial brand identity of a vehicle line (e.g., F-150, Silverado, Camry, Mustang). Owns nameplate code, brand affiliation, vehicle segment classification (car/truck/SUV/commercial), powertrain family (ICE/HEV/PHEV/EV), market positioning tier, global vs. regional availability flag, nameplate lifecycle status (active/discontinued), SOP (Start of Production) year, EOP (End of Production) year, and nameplate heritage lineage. This is the root anchor for all program and model year planning.

The formal dealer order guide defining which SKUs, trim levels, option packages, and colors are orderable by dealers for a given MY, market, and sales channel. Captures order guide version, effective date range, market/region, sales channel, orderable SKU list, option availability matrix, minimum/maximum order constraints, and order guide approval status. Published to dealer DMS systems and governs what dealers can order from the factory.

Commercial powertrain configuration catalog defining the orderable powertrain combinations available for each nameplate and MY. Captures powertrain code, engine displacement, cylinder count, fuel type (gasoline/diesel/hybrid/PHEV/BEV/FCEV), electric motor configuration (for EV/HEV/PHEV), combined horsepower, combined torque, transmission type, EPA fuel economy rating (city/highway/combined), WLTP range (for EVs), battery capacity (kWh for EVs), and emissions classification. Distinct from engineering powertrain design data — this is the commercial specification layer.

SSOT for the orderable SKU (Stock Keeping Unit) — the fully specified, buildable vehicle configuration combining nameplate, MY, trim level, powertrain, body style, and option packages into a unique orderable unit. Captures SKU code, SKU description, body style, drivetrain type (FWD/RWD/AWD/4WD), engine/powertrain code, transmission type, exterior color code, interior color/material code, market destination code, and SKU lifecycle status. The SKU is the atomic unit used in order management, production scheduling, and dealer inventory.

after.description: Master reference table for market. Referenced by market_id.

SSOT for vehicle nameplate definitions — the commercial brand identity of a vehicle line (e.g., F-150, Silverado, Camry, Mustang). Owns nameplate code, brand affiliation, vehicle segment classification (car/truck/SUV/commercial), powertrain family (ICE/HEV/PHEV/EV), market positioning tier, global vs. regional availability flag, nameplate lifecycle status (active/discontinued), SOP (Start of Production) year, EOP (End of Production) year, and nameplate heritage lineage. This is the root anchor for all program and model year planning.
Master reference table for extended_warranty_provider. Referenced by extended_warranty_provider_id.
Individual activities performed during a field visit (inspections, repairs, training)
Field failure analysis and quality investigations conducted by OEM field engineers
Dispatch assignments for OEM field technicians to service locations
Tracks scheduled and ad-hoc field visits by OEM field representatives to dealers or customer sites
Roadside assistance and breakdown/towing events triggered by customer or connected vehicle
Master reference table for third_party_warranty_contract. Referenced by third_party_warranty_contract_id.

before.description: Defines the annual program plan for each nameplate by MY (Model Year). Captures MY designation, program code, program phase (concept/development/launch/production/runout), SOP date, EOP date, target plant assignments, planned production volume, regulatory homologation targets (CAFE, WLTP, EPA), program budget envelope (CapEx), and program manager reference. Acts as the planning backbone linking nameplate definitions to annual production and sales programs.

Defines commercially available option packages and standalone options that can be ordered on a vehicle (e.g., Technology Package, Tow Package, Panoramic Roof, Premium Audio). Captures package code, package name, package type (group/standalone/accessory), MSRP uplift price, content description, constraint rules (requires/excludes other packages), availability by trim level, market availability regions, and lifecycle status. Distinct from engineering feature definitions — this is the commercial catalog layer.

Defines the commercial trim hierarchy for a model year program (e.g., Base, XL, XLT, Lariat, Platinum, Limited). Captures trim code, trim name, trim rank/order within the nameplate hierarchy, standard feature set description, MSRP base price, market segment positioning, availability regions, and active/inactive lifecycle status. Trim levels are the primary commercial differentiation layer between the nameplate and individual option packages.

Reference catalog of commercial body style definitions available across nameplates (e.g., 2-door coupe, 4-door sedan, crew cab pickup, extended cab, SUV 3-row, cargo van). Captures body style code, body style name, door count, seating capacity, cargo volume, roof type, body structure classification (unibody/body-on-frame), and applicable vehicle segment. Used in SKU construction, order management, and regulatory homologation classification.

Commercial color catalog defining all available exterior paint colors and interior color/material combinations offered across model year programs. Captures color code, color name, color type (exterior/interior), color family, paint technology (solid/metallic/pearl/matte), interior material type (cloth/leather/synthetic/premium), availability by trim level, MSRP uplift (for premium colors), regional availability, and active/discontinued status. Used in SKU configuration, order management, and production scheduling.

Defines market-specific homologation variants of a base SKU required to meet local regulatory standards (UNECE, FMVSS, ADR, etc.). Captures homologation variant code, base SKU reference, target market/country, regulatory standard (UNECE/FMVSS/ADR/CARB), required modification description, homologation approval number, approval authority, approval date, expiry date, and variant status. Bridges the commercial product catalog to the compliance domain's regulatory approval records.
Master reference table for market. Referenced by market_id.

Defines the feature-to-market availability matrix — which SKUs, trim levels, and option packages are available in which geographic markets and sales channels. Captures market code, sales channel (retail/fleet/government/export), availability status (available/restricted/not-offered), launch date, withdrawal date, homologation approval status, import duty classification, and CKD/SKD (Completely Knocked Down / Semi Knocked Down) assembly flag. Critical for order management, dealer ordering systems, and regulatory compliance.

SSOT for MSRP (Manufacturer Suggested Retail Price) price books by model year, market, and currency. Captures price book code, effective date range, market/region code, currency code, price book status (draft/approved/published/superseded), approval authority, and publication date. The price book is the container for all MSRP pricing entries and governs which prices are active for dealer ordering and consumer-facing communications.

Individual MSRP (Manufacturer Suggested Retail Price) pricing entries within a price book. Captures the SKU or option package being priced, base MSRP amount, destination charge, gas guzzler tax (if applicable), effective start and end dates, price type (base vehicle/option/package/accessory), and prior price for change tracking. Enables dealer invoice generation, consumer window sticker production, and competitive pricing analysis.

SSOT for vehicle nameplate definitions — the commercial brand identity of a vehicle line (e.g., F-150, Silverado, Camry, Mustang). Owns nameplate code, brand affiliation, vehicle segment classification (car/truck/SUV/commercial), powertrain family (ICE/HEV/PHEV/EV), market positioning tier, global vs. regional availability flag, nameplate lifecycle status (active/discontinued), SOP (Start of Production) year, EOP (End of Production) year, and nameplate heritage lineage. This is the root anchor for all program and model year planning.

The formal dealer order guide defining which SKUs, trim levels, option packages, and colors are orderable by dealers for a given MY, market, and sales channel. Captures order guide version, effective date range, market/region, sales channel, orderable SKU list, option availability matrix, minimum/maximum order constraints, and order guide approval status. Published to dealer DMS systems and governs what dealers can order from the factory.

Commercial powertrain configuration catalog defining the orderable powertrain combinations available for each nameplate and MY. Captures powertrain code, engine displacement, cylinder count, fuel type (gasoline/diesel/hybrid/PHEV/BEV/FCEV), electric motor configuration (for EV/HEV/PHEV), combined horsepower, combined torque, transmission type, EPA fuel economy rating (city/highway/combined), WLTP range (for EVs), battery capacity (kWh for EVs), and emissions classification. Distinct from engineering powertrain design data — this is the commercial specification layer.

SSOT for the orderable SKU (Stock Keeping Unit) — the fully specified, buildable vehicle configuration combining nameplate, MY, trim level, powertrain, body style, and option packages into a unique orderable unit. Captures SKU code, SKU description, body style, drivetrain type (FWD/RWD/AWD/4WD), engine/powertrain code, transmission type, exterior color code, interior color/material code, market destination code, and SKU lifecycle status. The SKU is the atomic unit used in order management, production scheduling, and dealer inventory.

Captures line number, item type (vehicle/part/labor/accessory/fee), item code, item description, VIN reference for vehicle lines, part number for parts lines, quantity, unit price, MSRP, negotiated price, discount amount, tax code, tax amount, line total, and revenue category. lineage.vibe: R&D coverage gap: add dedicated data products for advanced R&D simulation data management (CFD, FEA, NVH result datasets), test bench data, and autonomous driving development data (sensor datasets, scenario libraries), plus a requirements traceability data product (DOORS/Polarion/Jira integration) currently only implied through 'linked requirements'. The Engineering domain is otherwise well covered.
lineage.interpretation: Strengthen R&D with simulation result, test bench, AD sensor/scenario, and requirements traceability products

lineage.vibe: Purchasing/Procurement: the ECM Procurement domain is well covered, but consider modeling e-procurement portals / supplier collaboration platforms (e.g., Ariba, Covisint/SupplyOn) and commodity management and hedging (important for raw material purchasing in automotive), which are currently absent.
lineage.interpretation: Add e-procurement/supplier collaboration and commodity management/hedging coverage

lineage.vibe: Manufacturing: add a more structured MES integration layer (work instructions, operator assignments per station, cycle time tracking), an explicit OEE metric view or pre-aggregated OEE data product, more explicit paint shop / body shop / assembly process parameters (currently generalized under process_parameter), and energy consumption tracking per production line/plant for ESG reporting.
lineage.interpretation: Strengthen manufacturing with MES detail, OEE, process-area params, and energy tracking

lineage.vibe: Logistics: improve coverage of yard management (vehicle compound storage optimization, slot assignments), last-mile delivery (dealer delivery scheduling, customer home delivery for direct-to-consumer), returnable packaging / container management (Ladungstraeger-Management), and dangerous goods handling, all currently underrepresented or absent.
lineage.interpretation: Strengthen logistics with yard mgmt, last-mile, returnable packaging, and dangerous goods

lineage.vibe: Sales: address gaps in online/digital sales channels (configurator sessions, online orders, e-commerce), a complete Certified Pre-Owned (CPO) used vehicle workflow beyond used_vehicle_appraisal, Finance & Insurance (F&I) financing and leasing (a notable gap and major revenue stream), and connecting subscription-based vehicle (vehicle-as-a-service) models from the Mobility domain into the Sales flow.
lineage.interpretation: Strengthen sales with digital channels, CPO, F&I, and subscription linkage

lineage.vibe: Aftersales: connect connected-vehicle diagnostics (OBD-II live data) and OTA software updates to aftersales service operations, model customer self-service portals (appointment booking, service history access), and expand extended warranty / third-party warranty provider data which is currently limited.
lineage.interpretation: Strengthen aftersales with connected-vehicle/OTA linkage, self-service, and extended warranty

lineage.vibe: Field Services is the weakest area of value chain coverage and should be consolidated into a dedicated Field Services domain (or subdomain) covering field technician dispatching, mobile service orders, roadside assistance, towing/breakdown management, field quality investigations / field failure analysis, and field engineering reports, plus modeling the cross-domain workflow that integrates connected vehicle telemetry with service scheduling (proactive maintenance triggers).
lineage.interpretation: Add a dedicated Field Services domain consolidating scattered field concepts

lineage.vibe: Industry 4.0 / Digitalization: be more explicit about IoT sensor data, edge computing data flows, and AI/ML model metadata (e.g., predictive quality models, computer vision inspection results), which are currently only partially represented via AGV, digital twins, and OTA.
lineage.interpretation: Add IoT/edge/AI-ML metadata coverage

lineage.vibe: ESG / Sustainability data is underrepresented: add data products for CO2 emissions tracking, energy consumption, water usage, social compliance audits, and ESG reporting structures (CSRD, EU Taxonomy), which are increasingly mandatory and currently not modeled.
lineage.interpretation: Add ESG/sustainability data products

lineage.vibe: Data Governance: explicitly model data catalog metadata, data quality rules, data lineage, and data ownership, which are important for a Lakehouse architecture and currently not modeled despite the presence of compliance and audit domains.
lineage.interpretation: Add data governance metadata/quality/lineage/ownership modeling
